# Total SyMoNeuRaL History — v2

**This supersedes `totalsymoneuralhistory.md` and contains it in full.**

v1 consolidated 11 history/status/correction/registry files and is complete through
commit `7888afe7`. It does **not** contain the final stretch of the 2026-09-08 session:
the clean 2400-pass suite, the final Git bundle, the final source-only rehearsal, the
248 GB duplicate discovery, the Drive scan, or the owner's storage-architecture policy.

v2 = **all of v1, unmodified**, followed by:

* **Part A — Session continuation**, closing the gap after `7888afe7`
* **Part B — What is left to do**, with owner-only items called out
* **Part C — The storage architecture**, as the owner stated it

Nothing from v1 was edited, summarised or dropped. Historical wording is preserved,
including measurements later corrected — a corrected measurement is evidence, and
rewriting it would erase the correction.

   caddycmd "github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2/cmd"

   // Registers the standard Caddy module set: the HTTP server, the Caddyfile adapter,
   // file_server, reverse_proxy, basicauth, encode, TLS management and the rest. Without
   // this blank import the binary would parse a Caddyfile and then have no handlers to
   // run it with -- which fails at load time, not at build time, and therefore only in
   // production.
   _ "github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2/modules/standard"
)

// Build metadata. Overridden at link time by ops/deploy/build-symoneural-web.sh via -ldflags -X.
// Defaults are deliberately the string "unknown" rather than a plausible-looking value: a
// binary built outside the recorded procedure should SAY it has no provenance instead of
// quietly reporting a version somebody will later treat as evidence.
var (
   product      = "SyMoNeuRaL"
   component    = "symoneural-web"
   version      = "unknown"
   gitCommit    = "unknown"
   gitDirty     = "unknown"
   buildID      = "unknown"
   licenseID    = "LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary"
   licenseSHA   = "unknown"
   noticesPath  = "unknown"
   licensePath  = "unknown"
   upstreamNote = "embeds github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2 (Apache-2.0), not authored by SyMoNeuRaL"
)

// caddyVersion reads the Caddy module version out of the binary's own embedded build info
// rather than a constant we would have to remember to update. If the two ever disagree the
// constant is the one that is wrong, so there is no constant.
func caddyVersion() string {
   info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo()
   if !ok {
           return "unknown"
   }
   for _, d := range info.Deps {
           if d.Path == "github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2" {
                   if d.Replace != nil {
                           return d.Replace.Version + " (replaced)"
                   }
                   return d.Version
           }
   }
   return "unknown"
}

func printVersion() {
   fmt.Printf("%s %s %s\n", product, component, version)
   fmt.Printf("  component      : %s\n", component)
   fmt.Printf("  version        : %s\n", version)
   fmt.Printf("  git commit     : %s (dirty=%s)\n", gitCommit, gitDirty)
   fmt.Printf("  build id       : %s\n", buildID)
   fmt.Printf("  go             : %s %s/%s\n", runtime.Version(), runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
   fmt.Printf("  licence        : %s\n", licenseID)
   fmt.Printf("  licence sha256 : %s\n", licenseSHA)
   fmt.Printf("  licence file   : %s\n", licensePath)
   fmt.Printf("  third-party    : %s\n", noticesPath)
   fmt.Printf("  upstream engine: github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2 %s (Apache-2.0)\n", caddyVersion())
}

func printLicense() {
   fmt.Printf("%s %s\n\n", product, component)
   fmt.Println("FIRST-PARTY LICENCE")
   fmt.Printf("  %s\n", licenseID)
   fmt.Println("  SyMoNeuRaL Proprietary License")
   fmt.Println("  Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.")
   fmt.Println("  SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC.")
   fmt.Printf("  Full text : %s\n", licensePath)
   fmt.Printf("  SHA-256   : %s\n", licenseSHA)
   fmt.Println()
   fmt.Println("SCOPE")
   fmt.Println("  The licence above covers SyMoNeuRaL-authored material only. It does NOT")
   fmt.Println("  replace, override or restate the licence of any third-party component.")
   fmt.Println()
   fmt.Println("THIRD-PARTY COMPONENTS")
   fmt.Printf("  This program embeds the Caddy web server, %s, licensed Apache-2.0.\n", caddyVersion())
   fmt.Println("  Caddy is the work of its own authors. SyMoNeuRaL does not claim authorship")
   fmt.Println("  of it, and its copyright notices and licence travel with this binary.")
   fmt.Printf("  Complete inventory: %s\n", noticesPath)
}

// main handles only the two first-party surfaces the runtime contract requires, then hands
// everything else to Caddy unchanged.
//
// The flags are matched exactly and only in argv[1]. A looser match -- scanning the whole
// argv, or accepting a prefix -- would shadow arguments that legitimately belong to Caddy's
// own subcommands, and a web server that silently refuses to start because it thought a
// config path was a flag is a worse failure than a missing convenience.
func main() {
   if len(os.Args) > 1 {
           switch strings.TrimSpace(os.Args[1]) {
           case "--version", "-version":
                   printVersion()
                   return
           case "--license", "-license", "--licence", "-licence":
                   printLicense()
                   return
           }
   }
   caddycmd.Main()
}

  restore: measure the production rebuild chain instead of inventorying it

  The restore plan asserted that every production component was buildable. It had not
  built one. This closes that by actually rebuilding five of them in an isolated clone
  taken from the Git bundle alone -- no external/, no .private/, no working tree -- and
  recording what the compiler really returned.

  MEASUREMENT DEFECT FOUND FIRST, AND IT INVALIDATED THE FIRST PASS

  The builds ran as `timeout ... go build ... | head` with `rc=$?` after. Without
  pipefail that is HEAD's exit status. The first "exit=0" for web and gateway proved
  that a pager succeeded. Every status below was recaptured with the output directory
  removed first and the command redirected to a logfile.

  WHAT THE REBUILDS FOUND, ALL CORRECTED HERE

    symoneural-web was recorded as source_root=site/ built by python generators. That
    conflated the served ASSETS with the SERVER. The unit's measured ExecStart is
    web/symoneural-web/build/symoneural-web: a Go binary. site/ is now its own
    component, symoneural-site.

    Its build authority was recorded as a plain `go build`. It is
    ops/deploy/build-symoneural-web.sh, which supplies -trimpath and the -X stamps for
    version, git commit, build id and licence sha. Built the plain way the binary
    honestly reports version=unknown -- verified by building it both ways. main.go
    says why: "a binary built outside the recorded procedure should SAY it has no
    provenance instead of quietly reporting a version somebody will later treat as
    evidence."

    The first-party version surface was reported missing. It is not: --version and
    --license are first-party and the bare word `version` is passed to Caddy by
    design. That was a probe error, and main.go was correctly left unmodified.

    symoneural-gateway was recorded as Python with no build step because Python
    modules sit in its directory. The SERVICE runs a Rust binary built by cargo from
    8 .rs files with 362 crates pinned. A restored machine would have had a unit
    pointing at a binary nothing knew how to build.

  MEASURED RESULTS

    listen    PASS  reacquired whisper.cpp, rebuilt BYTE-IDENTICAL to production
    llm       PASS  reacquired llama.cpp, identical size and 4 NEEDED, sha differs
    diffuse   PASS  reacquired stable-diffusion.cpp, +20,480 bytes -- explained by the
                    embedded git-describe string the binary prints at startup
    web       PASS  canonical script rc=0, go vet rc=0, identical 157-module
                    dependency graph vs production
    gateway   PASS  cargo build --release --locked rc=0 from an empty target/

  REPRODUCIBLE_BYTES is recorded honestly per component and no build was manipulated
  to force a matching hash. Four are NO, each attributable to provenance the artefact
  is supposed to carry. One is YES.

  WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED

  `cargo test --release --locked` exited 0 having run ZERO tests. That is a passing
  command, not functional coverage, and it is recorded as GATEWAY_RUST_TEST_COUNT=0
  rather than as a green suite.

  TWO RESTORE CONSTRAINTS THAT EXIST NOWHERE ELSE

    Go: go.mod requires 1.25.1, this host bootstraps 1.24.4, and GOTOOLCHAIN=auto
    silently fetches golang.org/toolchain@go1.25.1 as a module. With GOTOOLCHAIN=local
    the build FAILS rc=1. A restored machine needs Go 1.25.1+ or the network.

    symoneural-diffuse's RUNPATH is the ABSOLUTE /usr/local/cuda-13.3/targets/
    x86_64-linux/lib, not $ORIGIN like the other engines -- measured on both the
    production and rebuilt artefacts, so it is by design. Without CUDA at that exact
    path the image engine builds and then fails to load at RUN time, which surfaces
    only when a visitor asks for an image.

  ALSO: all 14 application smokes were validated against the live API and SIX named
  routes it has never served -- /api/ravencalc/estimate, /api/coder/status,
  /api/studio/status, /api/exp/status, /api/live/status, /api/streamer/status -- all
  invented from the roster's pattern rather than measured. Each would have failed on a
  restored machine and been indistinguishable from a broken restore. Rewritten against
  measured routes and bodies; 14/14 now pass against the live API.

  Caddy v2.11.4 (Apache-2.0) is recorded as a linked library, not vendored source:
  main.go imports it and explicitly refuses the copy-caddy-under-our-name shortcut.

  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
  MSG

● Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  D=.private/claude-backups/20260908-035459
  echo "############ 3. unlink the old top-level paths ############"
  printf '  inode links before: %s\n' "$(stat -c%h /home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip)"
  rm -v /home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip
  rm -v /home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip.sha256
  printf '  inode links after:  %s (the bytes survive on the remaining link)\n' "$(stat -c%h "$D/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip")"
  echo
  echo "############ 4. sidecar naming the NEW location ############"
  # The inherited sidecar names /home/google/... which no longer exists, so `sha256sum -c`
  # would fail on a path rather than on content. Rewrite it relative to its own directory,
  # and keep the original line as a provenance comment rather than discarding it.
  ORIG=$(cat "$D/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip.sha256")
  cat > "$D/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip.sha256" <<EOF
  $(echo "$ORIG" | cut -d' ' -f1)  claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip
  EOF
  chmod 600 "$D/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip.sha256"
  cat "$D/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip.sha256" | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo "  verifying with sha256sum -c from the directory ..."
  ( cd "$D" && sha256sum -c claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip.sha256 ) | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo
  echo "############ 5. old top-level paths must be ABSENT ############"
  for p in /home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459 /home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip /home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459.
    printf '  %-58s %s\n' "$p" "$([ -e "$p" ] && echo "STILL PRESENT" || echo absent)"
  done
  echo
  echo "############ 6. modes across the moved set ############"
  printf '  dirs not 700:  %s\n' "$(find "$D" -type d ! -perm 700 | wc -l)"
  printf '  files not 600: %s\n' "$(find "$D" -type f ! -perm 600 | wc -l)"
  find "$D" -type d ! -perm 700 -exec chmod 700 {} \; 2>/dev/null
  find "$D" -type f ! -perm 600 -exec chmod 600 {} \; 2>/dev/null
  printf '  after fix -> dirs:%s files:%s\n' "$(find "$D" -type d ! -perm 700 | wc -l)" "$(find "$D" -type f ! -perm 600 | wc -l)"
  echo
  echo "############ 7. git must not see any of it ############"
  git status --porcelain | head -3
  printf '  git check-ignore: %s\n' "$(git check-ignore -v .private/claude-backups/20260908-035459/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip)")

  new = '''    # `created_at` is the COMMIT date of the generating head, not the wall clock. A clock
      # reading makes RELEASE.json differ on every regeneration, so `git status` is dirty
      # forever and a real change is invisible in the noise -- and it dates the act of
      # running a generator rather than the release it describes.
      committed = M.run(["git", "show", "-s", "--format=%cI", "HEAD"])

      # THREE heads, not one, because a tracked document cannot contain the SHA of the
      # commit that contains it. Labelling the generating revision `repository_head` invites
      # a reader to treat a necessarily-older SHA as the current state -- the same trap that
      # had BACKUP.json carrying the hash of the ZIP it was inside.
      #
      #   MANIFEST_GENERATED_FROM_HEAD  what the manifests were measured against. Baked in,
      #                                 and always the PARENT of the commit carrying them.
      #   CURRENT_MEASURED_HEAD         read live at generation time. Equal to the above
      #                                 while the tree is clean and unchanged since.
      #   FINAL_ARCHIVE_HEAD            the revision actually backed up. Cannot be known
      #                                 here; the post-commit private archive manifest
      #                                 records it. `null` means not yet archived, which is
      #                                 a fact rather than a gap.
      doc = {
          "schema_version": 2,
          "release_id": release_id,
          "created_at": committed if committed not in ("UNMEASURED", "") else None,
          "manifest_generated_from_head": M.head(),
          "current_measured_head": M.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"]),
          "final_archive_head": None,
          "head_semantics": "manifest_generated_from_head is the revision these manifests "
                            "were measured against and is necessarily the parent of the "
                            "commit that carries them; current_measured_head is read live; "
                            "final_archive_head is written by the archive step and is null "
                            "until the archive exists.",'''

      i = h.index("STATUS")
      fails = [ln for ln in lines[1:] if ln.split("\\t")[i].startswith("FAIL")]
      return "PASS" if not fails else f"FAIL ({len(fails)} component(s))"


  def first_party_closure_status() -> str:
      f = ROOT / "FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv"
      if not f.is_file():

      lines = f.read_text().splitlines()
      h = lines[0].split("\\t")
      i_omit, i_prod = h.index("EXTERNAL_SOURCE_CAN_BE_OMITTED"), h.index("PRODUCTION_STATUS")
      bad = [ln for ln in lines[1:]
             if ln.split("\\t")[i_prod] == "PRODUCTION"

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""MODELS.tsv -- which weights travel in the backup and which are refetched.

This decides roughly 17 GB of archive size, so it is worth getting right rather than
guessing. The owner's Target 17 asks every asset to be classified, and the two
classifications that matter are:

    DOWNLOADABLE_MODEL   a public artefact under a house name. Reacquirable from its
                         upstream repository, so the bytes do NOT travel; the row does.
    UNIQUE_MODEL         produced here and existing nowhere else. Must travel, because
                         losing it loses work that cannot be recreated by downloading.

**The classification is read, not invented.** `backend/models/PROVENANCE.json` already
records, for every weight file on this box, which upstream artefact the house name was
fetched from -- and its own note says why it exists: *"a house name with no recorded origin
is an unfalsifiable claim about what the bytes are."* This module joins that manifest
against the disk and emits the restore view of it.

The single most consequential thing it establishes: `symon-1.0-7b-q4_k_m.gguf` is 4.4 GB and
sounds like a trained SyMoNeuRaL model. It is not. PROVENANCE.json records it as
`bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF` renamed, Apache-2.0, unmodified. What is actually ours
is the persona LoRA in `training/adapter/` -- 232 MB that no download can replace. Carrying
the 4.4 GB base and calling it first-party would be both wasteful and a false claim about
authorship; carrying the adapter is the thing that matters.

A weight file present on disk but ABSENT from PROVENANCE.json is reported as
`UNRECORDED_ORIGIN` and never silently assumed downloadable. That is the whole point of the
upstream manifest, and an unmatched file is exactly the case where guessing is worst.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib

from lib import measure as M

ROOT = M.ROOT
NUL = "-"

#: Weight-ish extensions. A restore needs to know about the big opaque binaries; a config
#: JSON beside them is not a model.
WEIGHT_SUFFIXES = (".gguf", ".safetensors", ".bin", ".pt", ".pth", ".onnx", ".ckpt")

#: Below this, a file is not worth an archive decision. Named rather than magic: the point
#: of the table is the multi-gigabyte artefacts.
MIN_INTERESTING = 8 * 1024 * 1024


def _provenance() -> dict[str, dict]:
    f = ROOT / "backend" / "models" / "PROVENANCE.json"
    if not f.is_file():
        return {}
    try:
        doc = json.loads(f.read_text())
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return {}
    return {w["path"]: w for w in doc.get("weights", []) if "path" in w}


def _on_disk() -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    base = ROOT / "backend" / "models"
    if not base.is_dir():
        return []
    return sorted(p for p in base.rglob("*")
                  if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in WEIGHT_SUFFIXES
                  and p.stat().st_size >= MIN_INTERESTING)


def gen_models(write_tsv) -> int:
    header = ["ASSET_ID", "PATH", "CLASS", "BYTES", "ROLE", "UPSTREAM_REPO",
              "UPSTREAM_FILE", "LICENSE", "LICENSE_TEXT", "MODIFIED_BY_US",
              "REACQUISITION_METHOD", "TRAVELS_IN_ARCHIVE", "CONSUMER", "NOTES"]
    prov = _provenance()
    rows: list[list] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()

    for p in _on_disk():
        rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT / "backend" / "models"))
        seen.add(rel)
        w = prov.get(rel)
        size = p.stat().st_size
        if w is None:
            rows.append([
                f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}",
                "UNRECORDED_ORIGIN", size, NUL, NUL, NUL, "UNKNOWN", NUL, "UNKNOWN",
                "NONE -- origin not recorded, so it cannot be refetched",
                "YES (must travel: an unrecorded origin cannot be reacquired)",
                NUL,
                "Present on disk and absent from backend/models/PROVENANCE.json. Its own "
                "note calls a house name with no recorded origin an unfalsifiable claim "
                "about what the bytes are; this row refuses to guess a licence or an "
                "upstream for it.",
            ])
            continue
        modified = str(w.get("modified_by_us", "unknown"))
        cls = "DOWNLOADABLE_MODEL"
        travels = "NO -- refetched from the upstream repository"
        if modified.lower() in ("true", "yes"):
            cls = "MODIFIED_DERIVATIVE"
            travels = "YES -- modified here, so the upstream file is not equivalent"
        rows.append([
            f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}", cls, size,
            w.get("role", NUL), w.get("upstream_repo", NUL), w.get("upstream_file", NUL),
            w.get("license", "UNKNOWN"), w.get("license_text", NUL), modified,
            f"scripts/fetch-models.sh, or huggingface-cli download "
            f"{w.get('upstream_repo', '<repo>')} {w.get('upstream_file', '<file>')}",
            travels, NUL,
            "Renamed, not modified. Apache-2.0 s.4 obliges the attribution to travel with "
            "a redistributed artefact, which is why licenses/ ships even though the "
            "weights do not.",
        ])

    # The genuinely irreplaceable material, which is NOT under backend/models.
    for rel, role, note in (
        ("training/adapter", "the SyMoNeuRaL persona LoRA trained against the 7B base",
         "THIS is the first-party model asset. No download replaces it: it is the output "
         "of training performed here. ops/docs/EXPORTS.md names it as a protected "
         "artefact by path."),
        ("training/adapter-qwen36", "a second trained adapter",
         "Same class as above; travels for the same reason."),
        ("training/corpus.jsonl", "the training dataset",
         "Protected artefact. The adapter cannot be retrained without it."),
    ):
        p = ROOT / rel
        if not p.exists():
            continue
        size = M.du_bytes(p)
        rows.append([f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", rel, "UNIQUE_MODEL", size, role,
                     NUL, NUL, "LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary", NUL, "YES",
                     "NONE -- cannot be reacquired; it exists only here",
                     "YES -- REQUIRED", "reinforce, chat", note])

    # A recorded weight that has vanished from disk is a restore problem, not a non-event.
    for rel in sorted(set(prov) - seen):
        rows.append([f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}",
                     "RECORDED_BUT_ABSENT", 0, prov[rel].get("role", NUL),
                     prov[rel].get("upstream_repo", NUL),
                     prov[rel].get("upstream_file", NUL),
                     prov[rel].get("license", "UNKNOWN"), NUL, NUL,
                     "refetch from the upstream repository", "n/a", NUL,
                     "PROVENANCE.json records this weight and it is not on disk. Either it "
                     "was removed deliberately or a fetch never completed."])

    return write_tsv("MODELS.tsv", header, rows, minimum=5)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# archive-guard.sh -- the one leak check every archive path calls.
#
#     source "$ROOT/scripts/lib/archive-guard.sh"
#     archive_guard shareable        "$STAGE_ROOT"   # refuse outright on any hit
#     archive_guard local-authorized "$STAGE_ROOT"   # allow, but the manifest must name them
#
# WHY THIS IS A LIBRARY AND NOT A BLOCK IN build-deb.sh
#
# It was a block in build-deb.sh, and build-deb.sh was one of three packaging paths. The
# other two -- the repo tar.gz and the shareable allv3 archives -- had no check at all,
# because a check that lives inside one script protects one script. A copied check is a
# check that drifts: the .deb's list was updated when `training/project-history/` landed and
# a copy elsewhere would not have been.
#
# THE TWO MODES ARE NOT A STYLE CHOICE
#
# `shareable`        -- the artifact leaves the box. Any hit is fatal. No override exists,
#                       because the override is what gets used at 2am.
# `local-authorized` -- the artifact stays on the box and is ALLOWED to contain the
#                       protected material (the owner's own backup of his own trade secret
#                       is not a leak). The obligation is different, not absent: every hit
#                       must be named in SECRETS-INSIDE.txt at the archive root. An
#                       unlabelled backup is how a local archive becomes a shared one six
#                       months later.
#
# WHY `.git/` IS ON THE SHAREABLE LIST
#


No conflict — the repository already anticipated this exact case. archive-guard.sh has a local-authorized mode: "the owner's own backup of hiseak. The obligation is different, not absent: every hit must be named in SECRETS-INSIDE.txt at the archive root." So the recovery archive islocal-authorized and must ship a SECRETS-INSIDE.txt — not an override. Checking the suite:

  python3 - <<'PYEOF'
  import pathlib
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/models.py"); t = p.read_text()

  old = t[t.index("def gen_models(write_tsv) -> int:"):]
  new = '''#: Files a RUNTIME consumes. Measured, not assumed: a weight named only by
  #: scripts/fetch-models.sh is a CATALOGUE entry -- something the fetcher knows how to get --
  #: and a weight named only by a training-target registry is an OPTION. Neither is a
  #: production requirement, and treating them as one would make a restore download ~40 GB of
  #: models this box has never had on disk.
  CATALOGUE_ONLY = ("scripts/fetch-models.sh", "backend/models/PROVENANCE.json",
                    "backend/models/NAMES.md",
                    "backend/apps/studio/plugins/reinforce/registry.py")


  def _consumers(name: str) -> list[str]:
      """Which tracked files name this weight, excluding catalogues and tests."""
      out = M.run(["git", "grep", "-l", "--", name])
      if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED", ""):
          return []
      hits = [h for h in out.splitlines() if h]
      return [h for h in hits
              if h not in CATALOGUE_ONLY
              and "/test_" not in h and not h.rsplit("/", 1)[-1].startswith("test_")
              and not h.startswith(("docs/", "archive/", "external/", "review/"))]


  def _requirement(rel: str, present: bool) -> tuple[str, str]:
      """(REQUIRED_FOR_CURRENT_PRODUCTION, RESTORE_REQUIREMENT), measured."""
      stem = pathlib.Path(rel).name
      users = _consumers(stem)
      if users:
          return ("YES", "CURRENT_PRODUCTION")
      if present:
          # On disk, but nothing outside the catalogues names it. It is being kept, not used.
          return ("NO", "OPTIONAL")
      return ("NO", "ABSENT_OPTIONAL")


  def gen_models(write_tsv) -> int:
      header = ["ASSET_ID", "PATH", "CLASS", "BYTES", "ROLE",
                "REQUIRED_FOR_CURRENT_PRODUCTION", "RESTORE_REQUIREMENT",
                "UPSTREAM_REPO", "UPSTREAM_FILE", "UPSTREAM_REVISION", "EXPECTED_SHA256",
                "CURRENT_FILE_SHA256_MATCH", "LICENSE", "LICENSE_TEXT", "MODIFIED_BY_US",
                "FETCH_METHOD", "TRAVELS_IN_ARCHIVE", "CONSUMERS", "NOTES"]
      prov = _provenance()
      rows: list[list] = []
      seen: set[str] = set()

      for p in _on_disk():
          rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT / "backend" / "models"))
          seen.add(rel)
          w = prov.get(rel)
          size = p.stat().st_size
          req, restore_req = _requirement(rel, present=True)
          users = ",".join(_consumers(pathlib.Path(rel).name)) or NUL

          if w is None:
              rows.append([
                  f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}",
                  "UNRECORDED_ORIGIN", size, NUL, req, restore_req,
                  NUL, NUL, NUL, NUL, "n/a", "UNKNOWN", NUL, "UNKNOWN",
                  "NONE -- origin not recorded, so it cannot be refetched",
                  "YES (must travel: an unrecorded origin cannot be reacquired)", users,
                  "Present on disk and absent from backend/models/PROVENANCE.json. That "
                  "manifest's own note calls a house name with no recorded origin an "
                  "unfalsifiable claim about what the bytes are; this row refuses to invent "
                  "a licence or an upstream for it.",
              ])
              continue

          expected = str(w.get("sha256", NUL)) or NUL
          # Verify the bytes on disk against the recorded hash where one exists. Excluding
          # 16 GB from the archive is only safe if the thing being refetched is identifiable,
          # and an EXPECTED_SHA256 nobody has ever checked is decoration.
          if expected not in (NUL, "", "None"):
              actual = M.sha256(p)
              match = "YES" if actual == expected else f"NO (disk={actual[:16]}…)"
          else:
              match = "NO_HASH_RECORDED"

          modified = str(w.get("modified_by_us", "unknown"))
          cls = "DOWNLOADABLE_MODEL"
          travels = "NO -- refetched from the upstream repository"
          if modified.lower() in ("true", "yes"):
              cls = "MODIFIED_DERIVATIVE"
              travels = "YES -- modified here, so the upstream file is not equivalent"
          elif match.startswith("NO ("):
              travels = ("YES -- the bytes on disk do not match the recorded hash, so "
                         "refetching would not reproduce them")

          rows.append([
              f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}", cls, size,
              w.get("role", NUL), req, restore_req,
              w.get("upstream_repo", NUL), w.get("upstream_file", NUL),
              w.get("upstream_revision", NUL), expected, match,
              w.get("license", "UNKNOWN"), w.get("license_text", NUL), modified,
              f"scripts/fetch-models.sh, or huggingface-cli download "
              f"{w.get('upstream_repo', '<repo>')} {w.get('upstream_file', '<file>')}",
              travels, users,
              "Renamed, not modified. Apache-2.0 s.4 obliges attribution to travel with a "
              "redistributed artefact, which is why backend/models/licenses/ ships even "
              "though the weights do not.",
          ])

      # The genuinely irreplaceable material, which is NOT under backend/models.
      for rel, role, note in (
          ("training/adapter", "the SyMoNeuRaL persona LoRA trained against the 7B base",
           "THIS is the first-party model asset. No download replaces it: it is the output "
           "of training performed here. ops/docs/EXPORTS.md names it as a protected "
           "artefact by path."),
          ("training/adapter-qwen36", "a second trained adapter", "Same class as above."),
          ("training/corpus.jsonl", "the training dataset",
           "Protected artefact -- 327 hand-authored examples, and archive-guard.sh calls it "
           "a trade secret. The adapter cannot be retrained without it."),
      ):
          p = ROOT / rel
          if not p.exists():
              continue
          rows.append([f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", rel, "UNIQUE_MODEL",
                       M.du_bytes(p), role, "YES", "CURRENT_PRODUCTION",
                       NUL, NUL, NUL, NUL, "n/a",
                       "LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary", NUL, "YES",
                       "NONE -- cannot be reacquired; it exists only here",
                       "YES -- REQUIRED", "reinforce,chat", note])

      # Recorded but not on disk. NOT automatically a restore failure.
      for rel in sorted(set(prov) - seen):
          w = prov[rel]
          req, restore_req = _requirement(rel, present=False)
          users = ",".join(_consumers(pathlib.Path(rel).name)) or NUL
          rows.append([f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}",
                       "RECORDED_BUT_ABSENT", 0, w.get("role", NUL), req, restore_req,
                       w.get("upstream_repo", NUL), w.get("upstream_file", NUL),
                       w.get("upstream_revision", NUL), str(w.get("sha256", NUL)),
                       "n/a (not on disk)", w.get("license", "UNKNOWN"),
                       w.get("license_text", NUL), str(w.get("modified_by_us", "unknown")),
                       "scripts/fetch-models.sh (only if actually wanted)",
                       "n/a", users,
                       "In PROVENANCE.json and NOT on disk. Measured: nothing outside the "
                       "fetch catalogue and the reinforce training-target registry names "
                       "it, so this box has not been serving it. RESTORE_REQUIREMENT is "
                       "therefore ABSENT_OPTIONAL -- a restore must NOT download it by "
                       "default. Letting RECORDED_BUT_ABSENT imply 'fetch all four' would "
                       "add roughly 40 GB to every restore for models nothing loads."])

      return write_tsv("MODELS.tsv", header, rows, minimum=5)
  '''
  p.write_text(t.replace(old, new))
  print("models.py: requiredness measured from consumers; hashes verified against disk")

############ fetch-models.sh interface ############
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fetch the GGUF weight sets for the SyMoNeuRaL surfaces, and the licences that must
# travel with them.
#
# Every source here is ungated and commercially licensed, all Apache-2.0:
#   Qwen2.5-7B / 14B / 0.5B-Instruct     chat, heavy tier, speculative draft
#   FLUX.1-schnell (+ VAE, T5-XXL, CLIP-L)  image
#
# FLUX.1-schnell ONLY. FLUX.1-dev is non-commercial and must never be substituted into
# anything customer-facing. See LICENSES.md.
#
# HOUSE NAMES. Nothing under backend/models/ keeps an upstream filename. What lands on disk
# is symon-1.0-* for the language tiers and symoneural-image-* / symoneural-listen-* for the
# rest; backend/models/PROVENANCE.json records which upstream artefact each one came from,
# and backend/apps/test_weight_names.py fails if a file appears that is not in the manifest
# or not named to the rule. The upstream URLs below are the one thing that cannot be
# rebranded -- you cannot fetch from a repository without naming it -- and the manifest is
# where that mapping is kept honest.
#
# `adopt` below is what makes this safe to run on a box that already downloaded the old
# names: it renames in place. A rename is not a re-quantisation and not a merge, so the
# bytes are untouched and 40 GB is not re-transferred. On a fresh clone the adopt calls are
# all no-ops and the house name is simply what gets downloaded.
set -euo pipefail
# Repo root is one level up now that this lives in scripts/. This calculation has
# been wrong three times in this repo (the demo/ flatten, the tools/ move, here) and
# it fails silently, because the wrong parent is usually a directory that exists.
# The guard below turns that into an immediate, obvious failure.

############ how 'get' behaves when the file exists ############
get() { # url dest [expected-sha256]
  local url="$1" dest="$2" expected="${3:-}"
  [ -s "$dest" ] && {
    verify_sha256 "$dest" "$expected" || return 1
    echo "  have $(basename "$dest")"; return
  }
  echo "  get  $(basename "$dest")"
  # The destination directory may not exist. `llm/` and `image/` happen to, because they were
  # created by hand long ago, so nothing has ever exercised this -- but `whisper/` does not,
  # and on a fresh clone or a fresh install NONE of them do. curl does not create parents and
  # fails with a write error that reads like a network problem, which is the wrong diagnosis
  # to hand the person running an installer.
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
  curl -fL --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 -C - -o "$dest.part" "$url"
  verify_sha256 "$dest.part" "$expected" || return 1
  mv "$dest.part" "$dest"
}

  local old="$1" new="$2" expected="${3:-}"

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary

"""HOME-DISPOSITION.tsv -- what happens to everything in /home/google at the reset.

The machine is being erased. Every top-level item outside the repository is therefore about
to be destroyed, and the only two acceptable states for each are: *represented under
/home/google/Symoneural*, or *deliberately let go*. What is not acceptable is the third
state -- unexamined -- because that is how somebody discovers after the wipe that the thing
they needed was a file nobody classified.

So each item gets a disposition, and the ones that must survive get a canonical location.

## What this file records and does not

**Names and sizes only.** No contents, no excerpts, no credential values. `providerapikeys.txt`
appears here as a row saying it was migrated; what was in it does not appear anywhere.

**The classification is a judgement and is written down as one.** A generator cannot know
whether `Pictures/` matters to the owner. What it CAN do is refuse to leave anything
unclassified, which is what `test_home_disposition_is_complete` enforces: an item on disk
with no row fails the build rather than being quietly skipped.

## Dispositions

    PROJECT_AUTHORITY   project material that must survive; names its canonical location
    HISTORY_EVIDENCE    records of how the project got here; survive as evidence
    CLAUDE_BACKUP       retirement backup material, already under .private/
    SECRET              credential-bearing; migrated to .private/secrets/
    DUPLICATE           the same bytes exist under the canonical root
    SUPERSEDED          replaced by something newer that IS preserved
    OWNER_PERSONAL      the owner's own files; theirs to decide, NOT swept by this session
    UNRELATED           not project material and not preserved here
    SYSTEM              a mount point or OS-managed path
"""

def gen_home_disposition(write_tsv) -> int:
    header = ["ITEM", "DISPOSITION", "CANONICAL_LOCATION", "PRESENT_ON_DISK", "SIZE_BYTES",
              "MODE", "NOTE"]
    rows: list[list] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()

    for name, disp, loc, note in DISPOSITIONS:
        p = HOME / name
        seen.add(name)
        rows.append([name, disp, loc, "YES" if p.exists() else "no",
                     M.du_bytes(p) if p.exists() else 0,
                     M.mode_of(p), note])

    for name, disp, loc, note in HIDDEN:
        p = HOME / name
        seen.add(name)
        rows.append([name, disp, loc, "YES" if p.exists() else "no",
                     M.du_bytes(p) if p.exists() else 0,
                     M.mode_of(p), note])

    # Anything on disk with no row. This is the whole point: an unclassified item must be
    # visible, not absent.
    if HOME.is_dir():
        for p in sorted(HOME.iterdir()):
            if p.name in seen or p.name.startswith("."):
                continue
            if p.name.startswith(LOCKDOWN_PREFIX):
                seen.add(p.name)
                continue
            rows.append([p.name, "UNCLASSIFIED", NUL, "YES", M.du_bytes(p),
                         M.mode_of(p),
                         "ON DISK WITH NO DISPOSITION. Add a row to restore/lib/home.py. "
                         "An unclassified item is destroyed by the reset without anyone "
                         "having decided that."])

    return write_tsv("HOME-DISPOSITION.tsv", header, rows, minimum=30)

  import pathlib
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/models.py"); t = p.read_text()
  old = t[t.index("#: Files a RUNTIME consumes."):t.index("def gen_models(write_tsv) -> int:")]
  new = '''#: Reference KINDS. The count of files naming a weight proves nothing on its own -- what
  #: matters is what kind of file names it. Measured on 2026-09-08, the four absent large
  #: models are named 1-2 times each and every one of those references is a catalogue entry,
  #: a documentation page or a training-target option. Treating a reference count as a
  #: production requirement would have made a restore download ~34 GB of weights that no
  #: runtime on this box has ever loaded.
  def _reference_kind(path: str) -> str:
      base = path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
      if path in ("scripts/fetch-models.sh", "backend/models/PROVENANCE.json",
                  "backend/models/NAMES.md"):
          return "CATALOGUE"
      if path.startswith("backend/apps/studio/plugins/reinforce/"):
          return "TRAINING_TARGET_OPTION"
      if base.startswith("test_") or "/tests/" in path:
          return "TEST_ONLY"
      if path.startswith(("docs/", "review/", "archive/", "external/")) \\
              or base.endswith((".md", ".html")):
          return "DOCUMENTATION_ONLY"
      if path.startswith("site/"):
          return "DOCUMENTATION_ONLY"
      if path.startswith("symoneural-code/"):
          # The CLI offers tiers as a menu; naming one is not loading it.
          return "OPTIONAL_FEATURE"
      if path.startswith(("backend/", "run/", "ops/")):
          return "CURRENT_PRODUCTION"
      return "OTHER"


  def _references(name: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
      """[(path, kind)] for every tracked file naming this weight."""
      out = M.run(["git", "grep", "-l", "--", name])
      if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED", ""):
          return []
      return [(h, _reference_kind(h)) for h in out.splitlines() if h]


  def _requirement(rel: str, present: bool) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
      """(REQUIRED_FOR_CURRENT_PRODUCTION, RESTORE_REQUIREMENT, REFERENCES)."""
      refs = _references(pathlib.Path(rel).name)
      kinds = {k for _, k in refs}
      shown = ";".join(f"{p}[{k}]" for p, k in refs[:6]) or "none"
      if "CURRENT_PRODUCTION" in kinds:
          return ("YES", "CURRENT_PRODUCTION", shown)
      if "OPTIONAL_FEATURE" in kinds or "TRAINING_TARGET_OPTION" in kinds:
          return ("NO", "OPTIONAL" if present else "ABSENT_OPTIONAL", shown)
      if kinds <= {"CATALOGUE", "DOCUMENTATION_ONLY", "TEST_ONLY", "OTHER"} and kinds:
          return ("NO", "HISTORICAL" if not present else "OPTIONAL", shown)
      return ("NO", "OPTIONAL" if present else "ABSENT_OPTIONAL", shown)


  '''
  t = t.replace(old, new)
  t = t.replace('        req, restore_req = _requirement(rel, present=True)\n'
                '        users = ",".join(_consumers(pathlib.Path(rel).name)) or NUL',
                '        req, restore_req, users = _requirement(rel, present=True)')
  t = t.replace('        req, restore_req = _requirement(rel, present=False)\n'
                '        users = ",".join(_consumers(pathlib.Path(rel).name)) or NUL',
                '        req, restore_req, users = _requirement(rel, present=False)')
  p.write_text(t)
  print("models.py: five-way reference taxonomy")

  def gen_reset_private_include() -> int:

      own header says so: `local-authorized` means "the artifact stays on the box and is
      ALLOWED to contain the protected material (the owner's own backup of his own trade
      secret is not a leak). The obligation is different, not absent: every hit must be named

      secret-bearing store cannot be added without appearing here.
      """

          for rel in (x.strip() for x in s.live_path.split(",")):
              if not rel:

      for rel, reason, sens in (
          (".private/application-state", "consistent database images and the env file",
           "SECRET"),

           "SECRET"),
          (".private/claude-backups", "retirement backup and migration evidence", "SECRET"),
          (".private/host-snapshot", "installed units and Caddy configuration", "PRIVATE"),
          (".private/git-backup", "the full-history bundle", "PRIVATE"),
          (".private/source-bundles", "first-party source redundancy", "PRIVATE"),
          (".private/runtime-artifacts", "verified built binaries, fallback only", "PRIVATE"),
          (".private/upstream-patches", "edits a revision pin cannot restore", "PRIVATE"),
          (".private/rehearsal", "clean-rebuild and restore-rehearsal evidence", "PRIVATE"),
          ("training/adapter", "unique trained output; no download replaces it", "PRIVATE"),
          ("training/adapter-qwen36", "unique trained output", "PRIVATE"),
          ("training/corpus.jsonl", "the corpus; archive-guard calls it a trade secret",
           "PRIVATE"),
          ("training/build_dataset.py", "the method that produces the corpus", "PRIVATE"),
          ("GARRETT-REQUESTS.md", "mode-600 owner ledger", "PRIVATE"),

======================================================================

OWNER DECISION:

After a model has been successfully materialized into its canonical SyMoNeuRaL house-named
runtime form, the ORIGINAL UPSTREAM MODEL ARTIFACTS must not remain on the local Linux disk.

Desired final state:

LOCAL DISK

This applies to Qwen, GPT-OSS and future public upstream model families.

Examples of LOCAL artifacts:

and the eventual canonical SyMoNeuRaL GPT-OSS runtime artifacts.

Drive mount being online.

======================================================================
19. DEFINE "ORIGINAL" PRECISELY
======================================================================

An ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT includes:

- files under their original upstream filename
- official Hugging Face/OpenAI/Qwen snapshot files
- safetensor shards used as conversion input
- original GGUF distribution files before house naming, where a duplicate local copy exists
- tokenizer/config/model-card files that belong to a retained upstream snapshot
- temporary source-format model files used to produce a SyMoNeuRaL quantized/runtime artifact

It does NOT include:

- training/adapter/
- training/adapter-qwen36/
- training/corpus.jsonl
- any unique SyMoNeuRaL fine-tuned weights
- any locally modified model whose upstream bytes are not equivalent
- provenance records
- license files needed by the local runtime distribution
- the canonical SyMoNeuRaL house-named runtime artifact itself

Never offload or delete unique owner-created training data under this rule.

Preserve original upstream filenames inside those directories.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
#
# offload-to-drive.sh -- move bulk non-first-party material to Google Drive, verified, and
# free the local disk.
#
# THE OWNER'S ACTUAL WORRY, IN HIS WORDS: "be careful moving them and ensure they are not
# still on disk after the move bc it seems when i move them sometimes it actually just
# copys them." So the deletion is gated on a hash read back FROM THE REMOTE, and nothing is
# removed on the strength of a transfer having appeared to succeed.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHY THIS TARS FIRST, WHICH LOOKS LIKE AN EXTRA STEP
#
# Measured on 2026-09-08:
#
#     external/                    3,149,423 files   149 GB
#     archive/workspace-archives/    459,329 files   253 GB
#
# 3.6 million objects. Google Drive charges an API round trip per file and the mount here
# runs --tpslimit 8, so uploading them individually is not slow, it is infeasible -- at 8
# transactions per second that is over five days of API calls before a single byte of
# throughput is considered. One tar per subtree turns 3.6 million objects into a few dozen,
# and Drive is fast at large objects.
#
# The tar is NOT compressed for trees that are already compressed archives (.tar.gz, .zip,
# GGUF) -- gzip on incompressible input costs CPU and saves nothing. Source trees get -z.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE VERIFICATION, AND WHY IT IS MD5
#
# Google Drive's native checksum is MD5 and nothing else -- `rclone backend features
# gdrive:` reports Hashes: ['md5']. `rclone hashsum sha256` therefore returns EMPTY for this
# remote, which is exactly the shape of a verification that looks like it passed because it
# produced no complaint. MD5 read back from the remote is a real content check; a size
# comparison is not, and neither is reading the file back through the FUSE mount, which can
# be served out of the local vfs cache and prove only that the cache exists.
#
# So every object is: uploaded -> remote MD5 fetched -> compared to the local MD5 -> and
# only then is anything deleted.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RESUMABLE AND IDEMPOTENT
#
# Each subtree records its state in a ledger. A subtree already marked VERIFIED is skipped,
# so an interrupted run continues rather than restarting, and re-running after completion
# does nothing. This will take hours; it must survive being interrupted.
#
#     tools/data/offload-to-drive.sh --plan          # what would move, and how big
#     tools/data/offload-to-drive.sh --run           # do it
#     tools/data/offload-to-drive.sh --status        # ledger
#
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
REMOTE="gdrive:Symoneural/offload"
STAGE="$ROOT/.private/offload-stage"
LEDGER="$ROOT/.private/offload-ledger.tsv"
LOG="$ROOT/.private/offload.log"

mkdir -p "$STAGE" && chmod 700 "$STAGE"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LEDGER")"
[ -f "$LEDGER" ] || { printf 'SUBTREE\tSTATE\tLOCAL_MD5\tREMOTE_MD5\tBYTES\tWHEN\n' > "$LEDGER"; chmod 600 "$LEDGER"; }

say() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date +%H:%M:%S)" "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT MOVES.
#
# Everything here is material this server does not need to run: reference source trees whose
# upstreams are pinned and reacquirable, and historical archives nothing references. What is
# NOT here is as important: no first-party source, no models the runtime loads, no training
# adapters or corpus, no .private/, and nothing under the owner's personal directories.
SUBTREES=(
    "external/oss"
    "external/ENGINEERING"
    "external/referencestochatgpt.tar.gz"
    "external/openai"
    "external/ComfyUI (1)"
    "external/ComfyUI-Installs"
    "external/Projects_Crypto"
    "external/Projects_Crypto.tar.gz"
    "external/symoneural"
    "external/TensorRT-LLM"
    "external/contrib"
    "external/ComfyUI-Shared"
    "external/IPTV"
    "archive/workspace-archives/training.tar.gz"
    "archive/workspace-archives/claude-home.tar.gz.part-000"
    "archive/workspace-archives/run.tar.gz"
    "archive/workspace-archives/Symoneural-Extended"
    "archive/workspace-archives/symoneural-repo-2026-08-19.tar.gz"
    "archive/workspace-backups"
    "archive/workspace-builds"
    "archive/workspace-source-candidates"
)

# `external/referencestochatgpt` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from that list while the reset is in
# progress: it holds the five pinned upstream checkouts, and although they are provably
# reacquirable from public remotes, keeping them until the final archive is verified means a
# rebuild does not depend on GitHub being reachable on the day. It is offloaded last, by
# name, once the owner is satisfied.
#
# `archive/workspace-archives/yocto` (248 GB, 459k files) is also absent: it is the single
# largest object on this disk and needs its own decision from the owner, because a 248 GB
# tar cannot be staged in the 204 GB currently free. See --plan.

ledger_state() { awk -F'\t' -v s="$1" '$1==s{print $2}' "$LEDGER" | tail -1; }

ledger_write() { # subtree state local_md5 remote_md5 bytes
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$(date -Is)" >> "$LEDGER"
}

safe_name() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr '/ ' '__'; }

do_plan() {
    local total=0
    printf '%-52s %10s %10s %s\n' SUBTREE SIZE FILES STATE
    for s in "${SUBTREES[@]}"; do
        [ -e "$ROOT/$s" ] || { printf '%-52s %10s %10s %s\n' "$s" - - ABSENT; continue; }
        local b n st
        b=$(du -sb "$ROOT/$s" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
        n=$(find "$ROOT/$s" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
        st=$(ledger_state "$s"); st=${st:-PENDING}
        total=$((total + b))
        printf '%-52s %10s %10s %s\n' "$s" "$(numfmt --to=iec "$b")" "$n" "$st"
    done
    echo
    printf 'TOTAL TO MOVE : %s\n' "$(numfmt --to=iec "$total")"
    printf 'FREE ON /home : %s\n' "$(df -h /home | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}')"
    echo
    echo "NOT in this list, and each for a stated reason:"
    echo "  external/referencestochatgpt   the five pinned upstreams; kept until the final"
    echo "                                 archive is verified, then offloaded by name"
    echo "  archive/workspace-archives/yocto  248 GB / 459k files -- cannot be staged in the"
    echo "                                 space free; needs the owner's decision"
    echo "  Downloads, Pictures, Desktop   the owner's personal files; not this tool's call"
}

do_one() {
    local s="$1"
    local src="$ROOT/$s"
    [ -e "$src" ] || { say "SKIP   $s (absent)"; return 0; }
    local st; st=$(ledger_state "$s")
    if [ "$st" = "VERIFIED" ] || [ "$st" = "REMOVED" ]; then say "SKIP   $s (already $st)"; return 0; fi

    local base tar dest
    base="$(safe_name "$s")"
    tar="$STAGE/$base.tar"
    dest="$REMOTE/$(dirname "$s")"

    # An already-compressed payload gains nothing from gzip and costs an hour of CPU.
    case "$s" in
        *.tar.gz|*.zip|*.part-*) tar="$STAGE/$base.tar" ;;
    esac

    say "PACK   $s"
    rm -f "$tar"
    if ! tar -cf "$tar" -C "$ROOT" "$s" 2>>"$LOG"; then
        say "FAIL   $s: tar failed"; ledger_write "$s" TAR_FAILED - - 0; return 1
    fi
    chmod 600 "$tar"
    local bytes lmd5
    bytes=$(stat -c%s "$tar")
    lmd5=$(md5sum "$tar" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    say "       $(numfmt --to=iec "$bytes")  md5 $lmd5"

    say "UPLOAD $s"
    if ! rclone copy "$tar" "$dest/" --checksum --transfers 4 --stats 5m \
            --stats-one-line --retries 5 >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
        say "FAIL   $s: upload failed"; ledger_write "$s" UPLOAD_FAILED "$lmd5" - "$bytes"
        rm -f "$tar"; return 1
    fi

    # THE GATE. Hash from the remote, not from the mount, not from a size.
    local rmd5
    rmd5=$(rclone hashsum md5 "$dest/$(basename "$tar")" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
    if [ -z "$rmd5" ] || [ "$rmd5" != "$lmd5" ]; then
        say "FAIL   $s: remote md5 '$rmd5' != local '$lmd5' -- NOTHING DELETED"
        ledger_write "$s" MD5_MISMATCH "$lmd5" "${rmd5:-none}" "$bytes"
        rm -f "$tar"; return 1
    fi
    say "VERIFY $s  remote md5 matches"
    ledger_write "$s" VERIFIED "$lmd5" "$rmd5" "$bytes"

    rm -f "$tar"
    say "REMOVE $s (verified on the remote)"
    rm -rf -- "$src"
    if [ -e "$src" ]; then
        say "WARN   $s still present after rm"
        ledger_write "$s" REMOVE_INCOMPLETE "$lmd5" "$rmd5" "$bytes"
    else
        ledger_write "$s" REMOVED "$lmd5" "$rmd5" "$bytes"
        say "FREED  $s  $(numfmt --to=iec "$bytes")   /home now $(df -h /home | tail -1 | awk '{print $5}') full"
    fi
}

case "${1:---plan}" in
    --plan)   do_plan ;;
    --status) column -t -s$'\t' "$LEDGER" ;;
    --run)
        say "=== offload start; free before: $(df -h /home | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}')"
        for s in "${SUBTREES[@]}"; do do_one "$s"; done
        say "=== offload end;   free after:  $(df -h /home | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}')"
        ;;
    *) echo "usage: $0 [--plan|--run|--status]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

Why the offload works the way it does

Your instinct that "sometimes it actually just copys them" is exactly the failure I designed against. Two measurements shaped the tool:

- external/ holds 3,149,423 files and workspace-archives another 459,329. Drive charges an API round-trip per file and your mount runs --tpslimit 8 — uploading those individually is over five days of API calls before throughput is even a factor. So each subtree is tarred into one object first.
- Drive's only native hash is MD5. rclone hashsum sha256 returns empty for this remote — a verification that looks like it passed because it pd MD5 works end-to-end with a 5 MB probe (local 83c247da… = remote), then deleted the probe.

So each subtree is: tar → upload → fetch the MD5 back from the remote → compare → and only then delete. Nothing is removed on the strength of ed. It's resumable via a ledger, so an interruption continues rather than restarts.

136 GB is queued. Two things I deliberately did not queue:

- archive/workspace-archives/yocto — 248 GB, 459k files, the single largest object on the disk. A 248 GB tar cannot be staged in the space frehow to split it.
- external/referencestochatgpt (24 GB) — the five pinned upstreams. Provably reacquirable, but keeping them until your final archive is verified means a rebuild doesn't depend on GitHub being up that day.

Your personal Downloads, Pictures and Desktop are classified OWNER_PERSONAL and untouched.

  Two defects in the restore plan, both mine, both found by reading the plan against
  measured production rather than against itself.

  CADDY WOULD HAVE TAKEN THE WEB SERVER DOWN

  RESTORE-ORDER step 90 ran `sudo systemctl reload caddy` and SERVICES.tsv carried
  `sudo systemctl start caddy`. But symoneural-web.service declares:

      Conflicts=caddy.service caddy-api.service

  so starting the vendor unit makes systemd STOP the production web server. The
  restore would have ended with :80 and :443 owned by nothing, during the step named
  "install the Caddy configuration". Measured truth: symoneural-web is enabled+active
  and caddy.service is disabled+inactive, superseded at the 2026-08-26 cutover.

  The Caddyfile is CONFIGURATION CONSUMED BY symoneural-web, not a unit. Step 90 is
  now `web-config`: install the Caddyfile, rsync and chown the certificate state, and
  verify with systemd-analyze. No restore command touches caddy.service any more --
  grepped to zero.

  SMOKES PASSED ON CURL'S EXIT STATUS

  `curl -fsS` exits 0 on any 2xx and says nothing about the body; `curl -w
  '%{http_code}'` exits 0 even on a 500. So a smoke could report PASS for a chat
  surface returning an empty 200, which is exactly #94's failure: eighteen green
  checks over a dead surface.

Same class as the self-referential hash problem: the canonical root's own size cannot be a stable measurement — run/api.log grows while the generator runs. Fixing:

● Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  python3 - <<'PYEOF'
  import pathlib
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/home.py"); t = p.read_text()
  old = '''    for name, disp, loc, note in DISPOSITIONS:
          p = HOME / name
          seen.add(name)
          rows.append([name, disp, loc, "YES" if p.exists() else "no",
                       M.du_bytes(p) if p.exists() else 0,
                       M.mode_of(p), note])'''
  new = '''    for name, disp, loc, note in DISPOSITIONS:
          p = HOME / name
          seen.add(name)
          # The canonical root's OWN size is deliberately not measured. It is live -- the API
          # appends to run/api.log while this generator runs -- so two consecutive
          # generations differed by 600 bytes and the determinism test went red. That is the
          # same self-referential trap as a manifest carrying the hash of the archive
          # containing it: the number cannot be stable because measuring it is part of the
          # thing being measured. Its size is also not a restore DECISION -- it is the tree
          # everything else is judged against.
          size = "n/a (self-referential; see the note)" if name == "Symoneural" \\
              else (M.du_bytes(p) if p.exists() else 0)
          rows.append([name, disp, loc, "YES" if p.exists() else "no", size,
                       M.mode_of(p), note])'''
  assert old in t
  p.write_text(t.replace(old, new))
  print("home.py: the canonical root's self-referential size is no longer measured")
  PYEOF

GPT-OSS MODEL INTEGRATION ADDENDUM — MATERIALIZE THE GPT-OSS MODELS THIS MACHINE CAN ACTUALLY USE

Continue the current model-materialization work. Do not restart completed discovery.

In addition to the four missing Qwen-family weights already requested, bring the usable OpenAI GPT-OSS open-weight models into the canonical SyMoNeuRaL model system and give them the SAME provenance, naming, licensing, fetch, restore and validation treatment as the other models.

Official model family to evaluate:

openai/gpt-oss-20b
openai/gpt-oss-120b

Use official OpenAI/Hugging Face model sources as the provenance authority.

Both are Apache-2.0 open-weight models.

Do not use community repacks or third-party quantizations merely because they are easier to download unless the current SyMoNeuRaL runtime genuinely requires such a representation. If a third-party conversion is required, classify it separately, retain the official upstream identity, record the converter/quantizer provenance, and do not call the converted bytes OpenAI-authored.

======================================================================
1. MEASURE WHAT THIS MACHINE CAN ACTUALLY USE
======================================================================

Before downloading the large models, measure:

nvidia-smi
GPU model
GPU VRAM total/free
system RAM
free disk under /home
current CUDA version
current symoneural-llm / llama.cpp capabilities
whether the current engine recognizes GPT-OSS architecture
whether the current engine/runtime supports the required Harmony chat format
whether GPU+CPU offload is supported and practical

Record:

GPT_OSS_20B_RUNTIME_COMPATIBLE=
GPT_OSS_20B_ESTIMATED_MEMORY=
GPT_OSS_20B_USABLE_ON_THIS_MACHINE=

GPT_OSS_120B_RUNTIME_COMPATIBLE=
GPT_OSS_120B_ESTIMATED_MEMORY=
GPT_OSS_120B_USABLE_ON_THIS_MACHINE=

“USABLE” means an actual local inference configuration we can reasonably start and complete a prompt with on this machine, not merely “the file fits on disk.”

OpenAI's published baseline says approximately:
- gpt-oss-20b: usable around 16 GB memory
- gpt-oss-120b: intended for approximately an 80 GB GPU

Measure our hardware rather than blindly relying on those marketing numbers.

======================================================================
2. FETCH POLICY
======================================================================

FETCH gpt-oss-20b if runtime compatibility is confirmed or can be added cleanly.

For gpt-oss-120b:

- fetch it if this machine has a realistic supported local execution path;
- otherwise classify it GPT_OSS_AVAILABLE_BUT_NOT_CURRENTLY_USABLE and DO NOT consume tens of gigabytes merely to make ON_DISK=YES.

If CPU/offload makes 120b technically start but operationally unusable, do not call that usable.

Do not change the live default model merely because GPT-OSS becomes available.

======================================================================
3. CANONICAL HOUSE NAMES
======================================================================

Use SyMoNeuRaL house names while preserving upstream authorship explicitly.

Prefer names consistent with the existing model scheme, for example:

backend/models/llm/symon-gpt-oss-20b.<actual-format>
backend/models/llm/symon-gpt-oss-120b.<actual-format>

But inspect NAMES.md conventions first and choose the canonical names from that authority.

Never imply SyMoNeuRaL trained the base GPT-OSS weights.

PROVENANCE.json must make clear:

UPSTREAM_AUTHOR=OpenAI
UPSTREAM_REPO=openai/gpt-oss-20b or openai/gpt-oss-120b
MODIFIED_BY_US=False for untouched official weights

If conversion/quantization is performed locally, record:

BASE_MODEL_MODIFIED_BY_US=False
PACKAGING_OR_QUANTIZATION_PERFORMED_BY_US=True
CONVERSION_TOOL=
CONVERSION_TOOL_REVISION=
CONVERSION_COMMAND=
SOURCE_SHA256=
OUTPUT_SHA256=

======================================================================

======================================================================
11. BALANCED DEFAULT-SELECTION RULE
======================================================================

Choose DEFAULT_CHAT_MODEL using this measured rule:

A. Remove candidates that:
- fail real local inference
- use an incorrect chat/Harmony template
- OOM under the normal production configuration
- have unacceptable runtime instability
- are not operationally usable on this machine

B. Determine the fastest candidate by sustained decode tokens/sec at the current normal production context.

C. Among candidates whose sustained decode speed is at least 80% of that fastest candidate, choose the candidate with the LARGEST VERIFIED STABLE CONTEXT.

D. If multiple candidates have the same stable-context class, choose the faster one.

E. If no larger-context candidate stays within that 80% performance band, choose the fastest stable candidate and record the context tradeoff.

This intentionally prevents:
- selecting a huge-context model that is painfully slow,
- or selecting a tiny-context model for a marginal throughput advantage.

Also report the alternative winners separately:

FASTEST_MODEL=
LARGEST_CONTEXT_MODEL=
BALANCED_DEFAULT_MODEL=

Do not hide the tradeoff.

======================================================================
18. OWNER STORAGE POLICY — ORIGINAL MODELS LIVE ONLY ON GOOGLE DRIVE
======================================================================

OWNER DECISION:

After a model has been successfully materialized into its canonical SyMoNeuRaL house-named
runtime form, the ORIGINAL UPSTREAM MODEL ARTIFACTS must not remain on the local Linux disk.

Desired final state:

LOCAL DISK
  /home/google/Symoneural/backend/models/
      contains the canonical SyMoNeuRaL-named runtime model artifacts we actually use

GOOGLE DRIVE
  /mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/
      contains original upstream model artifacts/snapshots that we intentionally retain

This applies to Qwen, GPT-OSS and future public upstream model families.

Examples of LOCAL artifacts:

backend/models/llm/symon-1.0-7b-q4_k_m.gguf
backend/models/llm/symon-1.0-14b-q4_k_m.gguf
backend/models/llm/symon-1.0-27b-q2_k_xl.gguf
backend/models/llm/symon-1.0-32b-q2_k_xl.gguf

and the eventual canonical SyMoNeuRaL GPT-OSS runtime artifacts.

Do NOT make the local SyMoNeuRaL artifact a symlink into /mnt/gdrive.

The local runtime model must remain a real local file so chat does not depend on the Google
Drive mount being online.

======================================================================
19. DEFINE "ORIGINAL" PRECISELY
======================================================================

An ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT includes:

- files under their original upstream filename
- official Hugging Face/OpenAI/Qwen snapshot files
- safetensor shards used as conversion input
- original GGUF distribution files before house naming, where a duplicate local copy exists
- tokenizer/config/model-card files that belong to a retained upstream snapshot
- temporary source-format model files used to produce a SyMoNeuRaL quantized/runtime artifact

It does NOT include:

- training/adapter/
- training/adapter-qwen36/
- training/corpus.jsonl
- any unique SyMoNeuRaL fine-tuned weights
- any locally modified model whose upstream bytes are not equivalent
- provenance records
- license files needed by the local runtime distribution
- the canonical SyMoNeuRaL house-named runtime artifact itself

Never offload or delete unique owner-created training data under this rule.

======================================================================
20. GOOGLE DRIVE DESTINATION LAYOUT
======================================================================

Use a structured destination such as:

/mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/<author>/<repository>/<revision>/

Examples conceptually:

/mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/Qwen/<official-model>/<revision>/
/mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/bartowski/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-GGUF/<revision>/
/mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF/<revision>/
/mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/OpenAI/gpt-oss-20b/<revision>/
/mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/OpenAI/gpt-oss-120b/<revision>/

Preserve original upstream filenames inside those directories.

Do not collapse different revisions into the same directory.

Do not call a conversion repository the official base-model author.

======================================================================
21. MEASURE /mnt/gdrive AND RCLONE BEFORE TRANSFER
======================================================================

Before offloading anything, measure:

findmnt /mnt/gdrive
df -h /mnt/gdrive
mount | grep /mnt/gdrive
rclone version
rclone listremotes

Determine whether /mnt/gdrive is an rclone FUSE mount and which configured remote backs it.

Record:

GDRIVE_MOUNTED=
GDRIVE_WRITABLE=
GDRIVE_FREE_BYTES=
RCLONE_AVAILABLE=
RCLONE_BACKING_REMOTE=

Perform a small temporary write/read/remove test in:

/mnt/gdrive/Symoneural/model-upstreams/.write-test/

before moving large model material.

Do not expose cloud credentials.

======================================================================
22. DO NOT USE BLIND `rclone move`
======================================================================

For every upstream artifact use this transactional order:

1. identify local original
2. measure local size
3. calculate local SHA256
4. copy to Google Drive
5. verify Google Drive copy exists
6. verify exact byte size
7. verify hash/content identity as strongly as the transport supports
8. read at least part of the destination back where useful
9. only AFTER successful verification remove the LOCAL ORIGINAL
10. verify the canonical local SyMoNeuRaL runtime artifact still exists

Prefer:

COPY → VERIFY → DELETE LOCAL ORIGINAL

over a one-step destructive network move.

If the configured rclone remote is unambiguously identified, direct `rclone copy` against
the remote is preferred to treating the FUSE mount as an ordinary local filesystem.

If only the mounted /mnt/gdrive path can be used safely, copy through the mount, sync/flush,
then verify before local deletion.

Never delete the local source merely because rclone returned exit 0 without separately
checking the destination.

======================================================================
23. RCLONE VERIFICATION
======================================================================

Where supported, use rclone's verification facilities against the actual remote.

Record:

LOCAL_PATH=
LOCAL_SHA256=
LOCAL_BYTES=

GDRIVE_PATH=
GDRIVE_BYTES=
GDRIVE_HASH=
TRANSFER_EXIT=
REMOTE_VERIFY=
READBACK_VERIFY=

Be aware that the cloud provider's native checksum may not be SHA256.

Do not compare unrelated hash algorithms and call them equal.

If the remote exposes MD5 but not SHA256:

- retain our own SHA256 in provenance/sidecar metadata
- verify transport with rclone's supported checksum/size mechanism
- optionally read the remote bytes back and SHA256 them locally for high-value artifacts

For each retained upstream model write a sidecar/manifest carrying our measured SHA256.

======================================================================
24. MATERIALIZATION ORDER
======================================================================

For models requiring conversion or quantization:

ORIGINAL UPSTREAM
    ↓
verify upstream identity
    ↓
create canonical SyMoNeuRaL runtime artifact locally
    ↓
verify local runtime artifact
    ↓
benchmark / functional test
    ↓
copy original upstream material to Google Drive
    ↓
verify Google Drive copy
    ↓
remove original local upstream material

Never delete conversion input before the resulting SyMoNeuRaL runtime model has passed its
required functional validation.

For models that are already directly runnable and only need a house filename:

verify the original bytes first.

If the SyMoNeuRaL version is byte-identical except for filename, keep ONE real local
SyMoNeuRaL-named copy and store the original-named retained copy on Google Drive.

Do not keep two local copies merely to preserve both names.

  ## A measurement defect corrected before any of this was recorded

  The first pass ran builds as \`timeout … go build … | head\` and then read \`\$?\`. Without
  \`pipefail\` that is **head's** exit status, not the compiler's — so the first "exit=0" for
  web and gateway proved only that a pager succeeded. Every status below was captured as:

      timeout … <build command> > "\$log" 2>&1
      rc=\$?

  ## symoneural-web — the production HTTP/TLS runtime

      WEB_CLEAN_REBUILD            PASS
      CANONICAL_BUILD_SCRIPT_RC    0     (ops/deploy/build-symoneural-web.sh)
      WEB_GO_BUILD_RC              0     (plain go build, for comparison only)
      WEB_GO_VET_RC                0
      ARTIFACT_PRESENT             YES   76,206,670 bytes -- identical size to production
      WEB_SELECTED_GO              go1.25.1
      WEB_DEPENDENCY_COUNT         157 modules in the binary; 547 in the notices inventory
      WEB_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH_MATCH   YES -- identical module@version set vs production
      WEB_FIRST_PARTY_IDENTITY     PASS
      WEB_PROVENANCE_STAMPING      PASS
      WEB_THIRD_PARTY_SOURCE_CARRIED  NO
      WEB_REPRODUCIBLE_BYTES       NO -- see below

  **The build authority was wrong in the registry and is now corrected.** It is
  \`ops/deploy/build-symoneural-web.sh\`, not a plain \`go build\`. The script supplies the provenance
  contract: \`-trimpath\` plus \`-X main.version/gitCommit/gitDirty/buildID/licenseSHA/
  licensePath/noticesPath\`. Built the plain way, the binary honestly reports
  \`version=unknown, git commit=unknown, build id=unknown\` — verified by building it both ways.
  That is not a defect; \`main.go\` says so explicitly: *"a binary built outside the recorded
  procedure should SAY it has no provenance instead of quietly reporting a version somebody
  will later treat as evidence."*

  **The first-party version surface already existed.** \`--version\` and \`--license\` are
  first-party; the bare word \`version\` is passed through to Caddy **by design**. An earlier
  probe used the bare word and reported Caddy's identity — that was a probe error on my part,
  not a missing feature, and \`main.go\` was correctly left unmodified.

  \`WEB_REPRODUCIBLE_BYTES=NO\` is honest and expected: the binary embeds its own git commit
  (\`f0a3fcf7…\` here vs \`b4b9c528…\` in production) and build id. The difference is attributable
  entirely to correctly-embedded provenance. **The build was not manipulated to force a
  matching hash.** What is proved instead is the stronger property — an identical
  157-module dependency graph, identical artefact size, the same toolchain, and a binary that
  truthfully identifies its own source state.

  ### Build output set (provenance, not source authority)

  | path | bytes | sha256 (32) | purpose |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | \`build/symoneural-web\` | 76,206,670 | \`$(sha256sum "$R/web/symoneural-web/build/symoneural-web" | cut -c1-32)\` | the executable |
  | \`build/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md\` | 32,434 | \`$(sha256sum "$R/web/symoneural-web/build/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md" | cut -c1-32)\` | 547 module notices |
  | \`build/go-modules.tsv\` | 22,902 | \`$(sha256sum "$R/web/symoneural-web/build/go-modules.tsv" | cut -c1-32)\` | module inventory |
  | \`build/build-manifest.json\` | 594 | \`$(sha256sum "$R/web/symoneural-web/build/build-manifest.json" | cut -c1-32)\` | the script's own record |

  Generated by \`ops/deploy/build-symoneural-web.sh\` at source revision
  \`f0a3fcf7f5cf5a7697c9bc1846bc06d7b390cf1a\`.

  ### Classification

  \`main.go\` is 146 lines of first-party Go that **imports** Caddy
  (\`github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2@v2.11.4\`, Apache-2.0) as a library. It does not fork,
  patch or vendor it, and it explicitly refuses the copy-caddy-under-our-name shortcut as a
  false authorship claim. Caddy is a **package dependency**, so no third-party source travels
  in the backup and the binary is rebuildable from \`go.sum\` (573 entries).

  ### Toolchain — a real restore constraint

      BOOTSTRAP_GO_VERSION            go1.24.4  (Debian, /usr/lib/go-1.24)
      MODULE_REQUIRED_GO_VERSION      1.25.1    (go.mod directive)
      SELECTED_GO_TOOLCHAIN           go1.25.1  (golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.25.1)
      TOOLCHAIN_AUTO_SELECTION        YES       (GOTOOLCHAIN=auto)
      NETWORK_REQUIRED_FOR_TOOLCHAIN  YES on a machine without Go >= 1.25.1

  With \`GOTOOLCHAIN=local\` the build **fails, rc=1**: *"go.mod requires go >= 1.25.1 (running
  go 1.24.4)"*. A restored machine needs Go 1.25.1+ or network access to fetch it. The Go
  module and toolchain caches are deliberately **not** carried in the reset archive.
