  restore: measure the production rebuild chain instead of inventorying it

  The restore plan asserted that every production component was buildable. It had not
  built one. This closes that by actually rebuilding five of them in an isolated clone
  taken from the Git bundle alone -- no external/, no .private/, no working tree -- and
  recording what the compiler really returned.

  MEASUREMENT DEFECT FOUND FIRST, AND IT INVALIDATED THE FIRST PASS

  The builds ran as `timeout ... go build ... | head` with `rc=$?` after. Without
  pipefail that is HEAD's exit status. The first "exit=0" for web and gateway proved
  that a pager succeeded. Every status below was recaptured with the output directory
  removed first and the command redirected to a logfile.

  WHAT THE REBUILDS FOUND, ALL CORRECTED HERE

    symoneural-web was recorded as source_root=site/ built by python generators. That
    conflated the served ASSETS with the SERVER. The unit's measured ExecStart is
    web/symoneural-web/build/symoneural-web: a Go binary. site/ is now its own
    component, symoneural-site.

    Its build authority was recorded as a plain `go build`. It is
    ops/deploy/build-symoneural-web.sh, which supplies -trimpath and the -X stamps for
    version, git commit, build id and licence sha. Built the plain way the binary
    honestly reports version=unknown -- verified by building it both ways. main.go
    says why: "a binary built outside the recorded procedure should SAY it has no
    provenance instead of quietly reporting a version somebody will later treat as
    evidence."

    The first-party version surface was reported missing. It is not: --version and
    --license are first-party and the bare word `version` is passed to Caddy by
    design. That was a probe error, and main.go was correctly left unmodified.

    symoneural-gateway was recorded as Python with no build step because Python
    modules sit in its directory. The SERVICE runs a Rust binary built by cargo from
    8 .rs files with 362 crates pinned. A restored machine would have had a unit
    pointing at a binary nothing knew how to build.

  MEASURED RESULTS

    listen    PASS  reacquired whisper.cpp, rebuilt BYTE-IDENTICAL to production
    llm       PASS  reacquired llama.cpp, identical size and 4 NEEDED, sha differs
    diffuse   PASS  reacquired stable-diffusion.cpp, +20,480 bytes -- explained by the
                    embedded git-describe string the binary prints at startup
    web       PASS  canonical script rc=0, go vet rc=0, identical 157-module
                    dependency graph vs production
    gateway   PASS  cargo build --release --locked rc=0 from an empty target/

  REPRODUCIBLE_BYTES is recorded honestly per component and no build was manipulated
  to force a matching hash. Four are NO, each attributable to provenance the artefact
  is supposed to carry. One is YES.

  WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED

  `cargo test --release --locked` exited 0 having run ZERO tests. That is a passing
  command, not functional coverage, and it is recorded as GATEWAY_RUST_TEST_COUNT=0
  rather than as a green suite.

  TWO RESTORE CONSTRAINTS THAT EXIST NOWHERE ELSE

    Go: go.mod requires 1.25.1, this host bootstraps 1.24.4, and GOTOOLCHAIN=auto
    silently fetches golang.org/toolchain@go1.25.1 as a module. With GOTOOLCHAIN=local
    the build FAILS rc=1. A restored machine needs Go 1.25.1+ or the network.

    symoneural-diffuse's RUNPATH is the ABSOLUTE /usr/local/cuda-13.3/targets/
    x86_64-linux/lib, not $ORIGIN like the other engines -- measured on both the
    production and rebuilt artefacts, so it is by design. Without CUDA at that exact
    path the image engine builds and then fails to load at RUN time, which surfaces
    only when a visitor asks for an image.

  ALSO: all 14 application smokes were validated against the live API and SIX named
  routes it has never served -- /api/ravencalc/estimate, /api/coder/status,
  /api/studio/status, /api/exp/status, /api/live/status, /api/streamer/status -- all
  invented from the roster's pattern rather than measured. Each would have failed on a
  restored machine and been indistinguishable from a broken restore. Rewritten against
  measured routes and bodies; 14/14 now pass against the live API.

  Caddy v2.11.4 (Apache-2.0) is recorded as a linked library, not vendored source:
  main.go imports it and explicitly refuses the copy-caddy-under-our-name shortcut.

      i_omit, i_prod = h.index("EXTERNAL_SOURCE_CAN_BE_OMITTED"), h.index("PRODUCTION_STATUS")
      bad = [ln for ln in lines[1:]
             if ln.split("\\t")[i_prod] == "PRODUCTION"
             and not ln.split("\\t")[i_omit].startswith("YES")]
      return "PASS" if not bad else f"FAIL ({len(bad)} production component(s))"


  def test_status() -> str:
      """The last recorded full-suite reading, or an explicit UNMEASURED.

      Deliberately not a number typed here. This repository has published a test count that
      was never true of the commit it sat beside, and the fix is to read it from the file the
      suite writes rather than to carry it forward by hand.
      """
      f = ROOT / "run" / "SUITE-LAST.txt"
      if not f.is_file():
          return "UNMEASURED (run the suite and record it in run/SUITE-LAST.txt)"
      return f.read_text().strip().splitlines()[0][:200]

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""MODELS.tsv -- which weights travel in the backup and which are refetched.

This decides roughly 17 GB of archive size, so it is worth getting right rather than
guessing. The owner's Target 17 asks every asset to be classified, and the two
classifications that matter are:

    DOWNLOADABLE_MODEL   a public artefact under a house name. Reacquirable from its
                         upstream repository, so the bytes do NOT travel; the row does.
    UNIQUE_MODEL         produced here and existing nowhere else. Must travel, because
                         losing it loses work that cannot be recreated by downloading.

**The classification is read, not invented.** `backend/models/PROVENANCE.json` already
records, for every weight file on this box, which upstream artefact the house name was
fetched from -- and its own note says why it exists: *"a house name with no recorded origin
is an unfalsifiable claim about what the bytes are."* This module joins that manifest
against the disk and emits the restore view of it.

The single most consequential thing it establishes: `symon-1.0-7b-q4_k_m.gguf` is 4.4 GB and
sounds like a trained SyMoNeuRaL model. It is not. PROVENANCE.json records it as
`bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF` renamed, Apache-2.0, unmodified. What is actually ours
is the persona LoRA in `training/adapter/` -- 232 MB that no download can replace. Carrying
the 4.4 GB base and calling it first-party would be both wasteful and a false claim about
authorship; carrying the adapter is the thing that matters.

A weight file present on disk but ABSENT from PROVENANCE.json is reported as
`UNRECORDED_ORIGIN` and never silently assumed downloadable. That is the whole point of the
upstream manifest, and an unmatched file is exactly the case where guessing is worst.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib

from lib import measure as M

ROOT = M.ROOT
NUL = "-"

#: Weight-ish extensions. A restore needs to know about the big opaque binaries; a config
#: JSON beside them is not a model.
WEIGHT_SUFFIXES = (".gguf", ".safetensors", ".bin", ".pt", ".pth", ".onnx", ".ckpt")

#: Below this, a file is not worth an archive decision. Named rather than magic: the point
#: of the table is the multi-gigabyte artefacts.
MIN_INTERESTING = 8 * 1024 * 1024


def _provenance() -> dict[str, dict]:
    f = ROOT / "backend" / "models" / "PROVENANCE.json"
    if not f.is_file():
        return {}
    try:
        doc = json.loads(f.read_text())
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return {}
    return {w["path"]: w for w in doc.get("weights", []) if "path" in w}


def _on_disk() -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    base = ROOT / "backend" / "models"
    if not base.is_dir():
        return []
    return sorted(p for p in base.rglob("*")
                  if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in WEIGHT_SUFFIXES
                  and p.stat().st_size >= MIN_INTERESTING)


def gen_models(write_tsv) -> int:
    header = ["ASSET_ID", "PATH", "CLASS", "BYTES", "ROLE", "UPSTREAM_REPO",
              "UPSTREAM_FILE", "LICENSE", "LICENSE_TEXT", "MODIFIED_BY_US",
              "REACQUISITION_METHOD", "TRAVELS_IN_ARCHIVE", "CONSUMER", "NOTES"]
    prov = _provenance()
    rows: list[list] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()

    for p in _on_disk():
        rel = str(p.relative_to(ROOT / "backend" / "models"))
        seen.add(rel)
        w = prov.get(rel)
        size = p.stat().st_size
        if w is None:
            rows.append([
                f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}",
                "UNRECORDED_ORIGIN", size, NUL, NUL, NUL, "UNKNOWN", NUL, "UNKNOWN",
                "NONE -- origin not recorded, so it cannot be refetched",
                "YES (must travel: an unrecorded origin cannot be reacquired)",
                NUL,
                "Present on disk and absent from backend/models/PROVENANCE.json. Its own "
                "note calls a house name with no recorded origin an unfalsifiable claim "
                "about what the bytes are; this row refuses to guess a licence or an "
                "upstream for it.",
            ])
            continue
        modified = str(w.get("modified_by_us", "unknown"))
        cls = "DOWNLOADABLE_MODEL"
        travels = "NO -- refetched from the upstream repository"
        if modified.lower() in ("true", "yes"):
            cls = "MODIFIED_DERIVATIVE"
            travels = "YES -- modified here, so the upstream file is not equivalent"
        rows.append([
            f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}", cls, size,
            w.get("role", NUL), w.get("upstream_repo", NUL), w.get("upstream_file", NUL),
            w.get("license", "UNKNOWN"), w.get("license_text", NUL), modified,
            f"scripts/fetch-models.sh, or huggingface-cli download "
            f"{w.get('upstream_repo', '<repo>')} {w.get('upstream_file', '<file>')}",
            travels, NUL,
            "Renamed, not modified. Apache-2.0 s.4 obliges the attribution to travel with "
            "a redistributed artefact, which is why licenses/ ships even though the "
            "weights do not.",
        ])

    # The genuinely irreplaceable material, which is NOT under backend/models.
    for rel, role, note in (
        ("training/adapter", "the SyMoNeuRaL persona LoRA trained against the 7B base",
         "THIS is the first-party model asset. No download replaces it: it is the output "
         "of training performed here. ops/docs/EXPORTS.md names it as a protected "
         "artefact by path."),
        ("training/adapter-qwen36", "a second trained adapter",
         "Same class as above; travels for the same reason."),
        ("training/corpus.jsonl", "the training dataset",
         "Protected artefact. The adapter cannot be retrained without it."),
    ):
        p = ROOT / rel
        if not p.exists():
            continue
        size = M.du_bytes(p)
        rows.append([f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", rel, "UNIQUE_MODEL", size, role,
                     NUL, NUL, "LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary", NUL, "YES",
                     "NONE -- cannot be reacquired; it exists only here",
                     "YES -- REQUIRED", "reinforce, chat", note])

    # A recorded weight that has vanished from disk is a restore problem, not a non-event.
    for rel in sorted(set(prov) - seen):
        rows.append([f"model-{rel.replace('/', '-')}", f"backend/models/{rel}",
                     "RECORDED_BUT_ABSENT", 0, prov[rel].get("role", NUL),
                     prov[rel].get("upstream_repo", NUL),
                     prov[rel].get("upstream_file", NUL),
                     prov[rel].get("license", "UNKNOWN"), NUL, NUL,
                     "refetch from the upstream repository", "n/a", NUL,
                     "PROVENANCE.json records this weight and it is not on disk. Either it "
                     "was removed deliberately or a fetch never completed."])

    return write_tsv("MODELS.tsv", header, rows, minimum=5)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# archive-guard.sh -- the one leak check every archive path calls.
#
#     source "$ROOT/scripts/lib/archive-guard.sh"
#     archive_guard shareable        "$STAGE_ROOT"   # refuse outright on any hit
#     archive_guard local-authorized "$STAGE_ROOT"   # allow, but the manifest must name them
#
# WHY THIS IS A LIBRARY AND NOT A BLOCK IN build-deb.sh
#
# It was a block in build-deb.sh, and build-deb.sh was one of three packaging paths. The
# other two -- the repo tar.gz and the shareable allv3 archives -- had no check at all,
# because a check that lives inside one script protects one script. A copied check is a
# check that drifts: the .deb's list was updated when `training/project-history/` landed and
# a copy elsewhere would not have been.
#
# THE TWO MODES ARE NOT A STYLE CHOICE
#
# `shareable`        -- the artifact leaves the box. Any hit is fatal. No override exists,
#                       because the override is what gets used at 2am.
# `local-authorized` -- the artifact stays on the box and is ALLOWED to contain the
#                       protected material (the owner's own backup of his own trade secret
#                       is not a leak). The obligation is different, not absent: every hit
#                       must be named in SECRETS-INSIDE.txt at the archive root. An
#                       unlabelled backup is how a local archive becomes a shared one six
#                       months later.
#
# WHY `.git/` IS ON THE SHAREABLE LIST
#


No conflict — the repository already anticipated this exact case. archive-guard.sh has a local-authorized mode: "the owner's own backup of his own trade secret is not a leak. The obligation is different, not absent: every hit must be named in SECRETS-INSIDE.txt at the archive root." So the recovery archive is local-authorized and must ship a SECRETS-INSIDE.txt — not an override. Checking the suite:

  import json, pathlib, re
  d = json.load(open("/tmp/claude-1000/-home-google/0d019856-dbe0-49b4-ad80-0c3d9779a69b/scratchpad/openapi.json"))
  paths = sorted(d["paths"])
  print(f"  live API serves {len(paths)} routes\n")

  man = pathlib.Path("restore/manifests/SMOKES.tsv").read_text().splitlines()
  hdr = man[0].split("\t")
  ci, cc = hdr.index("SMOKE_ID"), hdr.index("COMMAND")
  ca = hdr.index("APPLICATION_ID")

  def declared(cmd):
      m = re.search(r"127\.0\.0\.1:8800(/[^\s'\"?]*)", cmd)
      return m.group(1) if m else None

  def matches(route):
      if route in paths:
          return route
      # templated segments: /api/project/{pid}
      for p in paths:
          rx = "^" + re.sub(r"\{[^}]+\}", "[^/]+", re.escape(p).replace(r"\{", "{").replace(r"\}", "}")) + "$"
          rx = rx.replace(r"\ ", " ")
          try:
              if re.match(re.sub(r"\\\{[^}]*\\\}", "[^/]+", rx), route):
                  return p + "  (templated)"
          except re.error:
              pass
      return None

  bad = []
  for ln in man[1:]:
      c = ln.split("\t")
      route = declared(c[cc])
      if route is None:
          print(f"  {c[ci]:<18} {c[ca]:<12} (not an HTTP smoke -- skipped)")
          continue
      hit = matches(route)
      flag = "OK  " if hit else "MISSING"
      print(f"  {c[ci]:<18} {c[ca]:<12} {flag} {route}" + (f"  -> {hit}" if hit and hit != route else ""))
      if not hit:
          bad.append((c[ci], c[ca], route))
  print(f"\n  smokes naming a route the API does not serve: {len(bad)}")
  for s, a, r in bad:
      print(f"    {s}  ({a})  {r}")
  PY)

                                may this external tree be omitted.
    restore/lib/measure.py      the readings. Nothing here guesses; a measurement

  tools/sh/fork_engines.sh builds the three engines behind chat, image and ASR out of
  external/referencestochatgpt/ -- 149 GB the owner does not want to carry. That is a
  real, load-bearing dependency and claiming otherwise to make a gate go green would
  be a lie the next restore would discover.

  What makes it omittable is that every one of those trees is a clean clone of a
  public remote at a pinned revision, verified against the checkout while the
  checkout is still here to verify against. 149 GB of source custody collapses into
  five URLs and five forty-hex strings. THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv carries the
  pins; tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh fetches them and refuses on a mismatch.

  kawpowminer is the exception that proves the rule: three uncommitted local edits,
  including a real #include <cstdint> fix for gcc 13+. A revision pin cannot restore
  work nobody committed, so the patch is preserved separately and the manifest says
  the pin alone is not sufficient for that one.

  WHAT IT REFUSES TO SAY

  No component is called first-party because it was renamed. symoneural-llm, -diffuse
  and -listen are MIT forks and are recorded as THIRD_PARTY_DERIVATIVE_PERMISSIVE.
  symoneural-miner and symoneural-ui are GPL-3.0 and are DISABLED rather than
  relabelled, which is what fork_engines.sh's licence stamping has always refused to
  do. symoneural-adaptive-fabric is README and LICENCE with no implementation and
  says DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, so the plan cannot appear to restore something that
  was never built.

    * systemctl is-enabled exits non-zero for a legitimately disabled unit, so three

    * the unit comparison had to become section-aware: the 2026-09-03 fix MOVED
      StartLimit* from [Service] to [Unit] without changing a character, and a
      set comparison of directive text called that a match.
    * a recipe named backend/requirements.lock.txt, which has never existed. The
      serving path is the Debian system interpreter; restore/locks/ now carries a
      real pinned lock per environment, 594 pins across seven.
    * the state table named run/accounts.db and run/api.env. Neither exists.
    * the first-party source bundle for the API was 97% vendored Anthropic and
      OpenAI SDK -- 15,704 files, now 407.
    * symoneural-ui was recorded as having no rebuild path. tools/sh/fork_render_ui.sh
      builds it. Buildable and disabled are different facts; both are now recorded.

  The installed symoneural-api and symoneural-gateway units are stale against their

The manifests are stable; only RELEASE.json's created_at moves. Two consequences: the earlier failure was stale pre-commit manifests, and created_at makes every regeneration dirty the tree forever. Deriving it from the HEAD commit date makes it deterministic and more meaningful:

● Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  python3 - <<'PY'
  import pathlib

  # 1. RELEASE.json must be a function of the commit, not of the clock.
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/generate.py"); t = p.read_text()
  old = '''    doc = {
          "schema_version": 1,
          "release_id": release_id,
          "created_at": extra.get("created_at") if extra else None,'''
  new = '''    # `created_at` is the COMMIT date of repository_head, not the wall clock. A clock
      # reading makes RELEASE.json differ on every regeneration, so `git status` is dirty
      # forever and a real change is invisible in the noise -- and it dates the act of
      # running a generator rather than the release it describes.
      committed = M.run(["git", "show", "-s", "--format=%cI", "HEAD"])
      doc = {
          "schema_version": 1,
          "release_id": release_id,
          "created_at": committed if committed not in ("UNMEASURED", "") else None,
          "generated_at_note": "created_at is the commit date of repository_head, so this "
                               "document is a function of the commit and not of when the "
                               "generator happened to run",'''
  assert old in t
  t = t.replace(old, new)
  # extra{} must not overwrite it
  t = t.replace('''    if extra:
          doc.update(extra)''',
  '''    if extra:
          # `created_at` is derived above and is deliberately not overridable: a caller
          # passing a clock reading would reintroduce exactly the non-determinism this
          # avoids.
          doc.update({k: v for k, v in extra.items() if k != "created_at"})''')
  p.write_text(t)
  print("generate.py: RELEASE.json created_at is now the HEAD commit date")

  # 2. An exclusion list is a protection rule, not a dependency -- the archive-guard case.
  p = pathlib.Path("backend/apps/test_no_external_source_dependency.py"); t = p.read_text()
  t = t.replace('''    "training/project-history/",             # the history CORPUS: recorded question and''',
  '''    "tools/build/build_recovery_root.py",          # its "external/" is an EXCLUSION list -- the
                                               # rule that keeps vendored trees OUT of a
                                               # first-party source bundle. Deleting it
                                               # because the detector fired would put
                                               # somebody else's SDK back in the bundle.
      "training/project-history/",             # the history CORPUS: recorded question and''')
  p.write_text(t)
  print("detector: exclusion list exempted as a protection rule")
  PY
  python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py >/dev/null
  echo
  echo "############ RELEASE.json now stable across two runs? ############"

  restore: a control plane that can rebuild this project on a bare machine

  The owner is erasing this Linux install and restoring SyMoNeuRaL later. The thing
  standing in the way was not missing files -- it was that every step of standing this
  system up lived in a commit message or somebody's head: which upstream revision an
  engine forks from, which of seven Python environments a component runs in, which
  database cannot be copied with cp, which unit is deliberately disabled and which is
  merely stale. None of that survives a reinstall.

  So it is written down, generated from measurement, and there is one program that
  reads it.

    restore/lib/registry.py     the judgements no measurement can make: is this
                                component production, is this implementation ours,
                                may this external tree be omitted.
    restore/lib/measure.py      the readings. Nothing here guesses; a measurement
                                that cannot be taken returns a string saying so.
    restore/manifests/*.tsv     twelve generated tables, the join of the two.
    restore/locks/*.lock.txt    594 pins across seven Python environments.
    restore/symoneural-restore  inventory / verify / dependencies / build / test /
                                install / restore-state / services / smoke / status.

  THE FINDING THAT SHAPED IT

  tools/sh/fork_engines.sh builds the three engines behind chat, image and ASR out of
  external/referencestochatgpt/ -- 149 GB the owner does not want to carry. That is a
  real, load-bearing dependency and claiming otherwise to make a gate go green would
  be a lie the next restore would discover.

  What makes it omittable is that every one of those trees is a clean clone of a
  public remote at a pinned revision, verified against the checkout while the
  checkout is still here to verify against. 149 GB of source custody collapses into
  five URLs and five forty-hex strings. THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv carries the
  pins; tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh fetches them and refuses on a mismatch.

  kawpowminer is the exception that proves the rule: three uncommitted local edits,
  including a real #include <cstdint> fix for gcc 13+. A revision pin cannot restore
  work nobody committed, so the patch is preserved separately and the manifest says
  the pin alone is not sufficient for that one.

  WHAT IT REFUSES TO SAY

  No component is called first-party because it was renamed. symoneural-llm, -diffuse
  and -listen are MIT forks and are recorded as THIRD_PARTY_DERIVATIVE_PERMISSIVE.
  symoneural-miner and symoneural-ui are GPL-3.0 and are DISABLED rather than
  relabelled, which is what fork_engines.sh's licence stamping has always refused to
  do. symoneural-adaptive-fabric is README and LICENCE with no implementation and
  says DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, so the plan cannot appear to restore something that
  was never built.

  DEFECTS THIS FOUND IN ITS OWN DRAFTS, ALL FIXED

    * systemctl is-enabled exits non-zero for a legitimately disabled unit, so three
      services read UNMEASURED when systemd had answered.
    * the unit comparison had to become section-aware: the 2026-09-03 fix MOVED
      StartLimit* from [Service] to [Unit] without changing a character, and a set
      comparison of directive text called that a match.
    * a recipe named backend/requirements.lock.txt, which has never existed.
    * the state table named run/accounts.db and run/api.env. Neither exists; the real
      stores are a directory deeper and two had a live writer attached.
    * the API source bundle was 97% vendored Anthropic and OpenAI SDK -- 15,704
      files, now 407.
    * symoneural-ui was recorded as having no rebuild path. tools/sh/fork_render_ui.sh
      builds it. Buildable and disabled are different facts; both are now recorded.
    * RELEASE.json stamped a wall clock, so every regeneration dirtied the tree. It
      is now the commit date of repository_head -- a function of the release, not of
      when a generator ran.

  CONSOLIDATION

  archive/from-desktop/symoneural-buildv2 -> archive/buildv2 by same-filesystem
  rename, so MANIFEST.sha256 and the bootstrap scripts' relative paths still resolve:
  141 of 141 entries verify after the move, and the evidence ZIP is byte-identical at
  mode 0600, matching the sha256 the owner published.

  A PRODUCTION FINDING, NOT FIXED HERE

  The installed symoneural-api and symoneural-gateway units are stale against their
  templates: StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst still sit in [Service] where
  systemd silently ignores them, so the crash-loop protection their own comments
  describe has never applied, and Before=symoneural-web.service is absent so the API
  has no boot ordering against the process that actually serves. Reinstalling a unit
  alters a production service and that authority was not granted, so it is recorded
  in SERVICES.tsv as DIVERGED and left for the owner.

  Verified: 29 tests pass; RESTORE_VERIFY=PASS over 77 rows; all five upstream pins
  PIN_VERIFIED; two generations byte-identical.

A genuine circularity, and I've hit this exact class before: a generated file cannot record the hash of the commit that contains it. Amending changed HEAD, so the committed manifests now name the pre-amend revision. My test conflated two different things — generator determinism, and manifests being current. Separating them:

● Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  python3 - <<'PY'
  import pathlib
  p = pathlib.Path("backend/apps/test_restore_manifests.py"); t = p.read_text()

  old = '''class Idempotent(unittest.TestCase):

      def test_generating_twice_changes_nothing(self):
          """Three generators in this repository have accumulated a copy per run."""
          before = {name: (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes() for name in REQUIRED}
          r = subprocess.run(
              [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "build_restore_manifests.py")],
              cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
          self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0,
                           f"the generator failed:\\n{r.stdout}\\n{r.stderr}")
          for name in REQUIRED:
              with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                  self.assertEqual(
                      before[name], (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes(),
                      f"{name} changed on a second generation with no source change. "
                      f"Either a measurement is non-deterministic or the generator is "
                      f"re-reading its own output.")'''

  new = '''class Idempotent(unittest.TestCase):
      """Generator determinism, kept separate from manifest freshness.

      These were one test and should not have been. A generated manifest records the
      revision it was generated FROM, and committing it produces a new revision -- so the
      committed copy can never name the commit that contains it. That is the same
      impossibility as a file containing its own checksum, which this project already hit
      once when BACKUP.json carried the hash of the ZIP it was inside.

      Conflating the two made a real property (the generator does not accumulate output)
      fail for an unrelated and unavoidable reason (HEAD moved). So determinism is tested by
      generating twice and comparing THOSE two runs, and freshness is tested separately with
      the revision columns excluded.
      """

      @staticmethod
      def _generate() -> dict[str, bytes]:
          r = subprocess.run(
              [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "build_restore_manifests.py")],
              cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
          if r.returncode != 0:
              raise AssertionError(f"the generator failed:\\n{r.stdout}\\n{r.stderr}")
          return {name: (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes() for name in REQUIRED}

      def test_generating_twice_changes_nothing(self):
          """Three generators in this repository have accumulated a copy per run."""
          first = self._generate()
          second = self._generate()
          for name in REQUIRED:
              with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                  self.assertEqual(
                      first[name], second[name],
                      f"{name} differs between two consecutive generations. Either a "
                      f"measurement is non-deterministic or the generator is re-reading "
                      f"its own output.")

      def test_committed_manifests_match_the_working_tree_apart_from_the_revision(self):
          """Freshness. Revision columns are excluded for the reason in the class docstring."""
          committed = {}
          for name in REQUIRED:
              r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "show", f"HEAD:restore/manifests/{name}"],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True)
              if r.returncode == 0:
                  committed[name] = r.stdout
          self.assertTrue(committed, "no manifests are committed yet")

          self._generate()

          def strip_rev(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
              lines = text.splitlines()
              header = lines[0].split("\\t")
              drop = {i for i, h in enumerate(header)
                      if h in ("SOURCE_REVISION", "PIN_VERIFIED")}
              return [[c for i, c in enumerate(ln.split("\\t")) if i not in drop]
                      for ln in lines]

          for name, old_text in committed.items():
              with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                  self.assertEqual(
                      strip_rev(old_text),
                      strip_rev((MANIFESTS / name).read_text()),
                      f"{name} in HEAD differs from what the registry generates now "
                      f"(revision columns excluded). Regenerate and commit: "
                      f"python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py")'''

  assert old in t, "Idempotent class not found"
  p.write_text(t.replace(old, new))
  print("test: determinism and freshness are now separate properties")
  PY

# `restore/` — the control plane

This directory answers one question: **after reinstalling Linux, how does SyMoNeuRaL come
back?**

Not "where are the files" — Git answers that. The things that do not survive a reinstall are
the decisions: which upstream revision an engine forks from, which of seven Python
environments a component runs in, which database cannot be copied with `cp`, which systemd
unit is deliberately disabled and which is merely stale, and what order any of it happens
in. Those lived in commit messages and in the owner's head. They are here now.

If you are restoring from bare metal, read **[`../RESTORE-FROM-BARE-METAL.md`](../RESTORE-FROM-BARE-METAL.md)**, which
is the step-by-step. This file explains how the machinery works so you can trust it.

---

## The one program

```bash
restore/symoneural-restore inventory          # what exists and what class it is
restore/symoneural-restore verify             # is the plan internally coherent
restore/symoneural-restore dependencies --check
restore/symoneural-restore dependencies --instructions
restore/symoneural-restore build   <component|all>  [--apply]
restore/symoneural-restore test    <component|all>  [--apply]
restore/symoneural-restore install <component|all>  [--apply]
restore/symoneural-restore restore-state --dry-run | --apply
restore/symoneural-restore services --check | --install [--apply]
restore/symoneural-restore smoke   <application|all> [--apply] [--allow-mutating]
restore/symoneural-restore status             # the release gate figures
```

It uses the **standard library only**. It has to run on a machine where nothing has been
installed yet — including, necessarily, before the thing that installs the dependencies has
run. Importing a third-party package here would make the bootstrapper depend on the
bootstrap.

**Everything that can change the machine is dry by default** and prints the exact command it
would run. `--apply` is the only way to make anything happen. The privileged steps go
further and refuse to run themselves: `services --install` prints a root command for a human
to execute rather than calling `sudo` on its own authority. A restore tool that silently
escalates is one nobody can audit before running, and these commands write systemd units.

It **refuses rather than guesses**. An unknown component id is an error, not an empty
selection. A missing manifest is an error, not an empty result. The failure this is written
against is a tool that returns `0` having done nothing, on a machine where the operator
cannot tell the difference.

---

## Where the facts come from

```
restore/lib/registry.py   ─┐
   judgements                │
                             ├──►  tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py  ──►  restore/manifests/*.tsv
restore/lib/measure.py    ─┘                                              restore/RELEASE.json
   measurements                                                           FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv
                                                                          THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv
```

**The manifests are generated. Do not hand-edit them.** Edit `registry.py` and regenerate.

The split is deliberate. Half of each row is something no measurement can decide — *is this
component production, is this implementation ours, may this external tree be omitted from
the backup* — and that half lives in `registry.py` where a human can argue with it. The
other half is read off the disk at generation time: file counts, revisions, checksums,
whether a binary a recipe promises is actually where the recipe says.

This repository has published a test count that was never true of the commit beside it,
reported a service as disabled off a table row while the unit file said enabled, and
recorded an engine as unbuilt because a probe looked in the wrong directory. Each was the
same failure — acting on a row rather than on the thing. So everything measurable is
measured, every time, and a measurement that cannot be taken returns a string saying so
rather than a plausible default.

### The manifests

| File | What it settles |
|---|---|
| `COMPONENTS.tsv` | every restorable unit, its class, and whether it is production |
| `APPLICATIONS.tsv` | each user-facing surface → its runtime, engines, state and smoke |
| `SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv` | is each component buildable, and from what |
| `BUILD-RECIPES.tsv` | literal prep/build/test/install commands and toolchain versions |
| `ARTIFACTS.tsv` | every built binary, its checksum, architecture and link table |
| `SERVICES.tsv` | units: designed enablement vs **measured**, and installed-vs-template |
| `DEPENDENCIES.tsv` | platform, toolchain and 196 Python distributions with licences |
| `PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv` | what Git cannot restore, and how to take it consistently |
| `RESTORE-ORDER.tsv` | the dependency-ordered sequence, with failure policy per step |
| `SMOKES.tsv` | one real exercise per production application |
| `../FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv` | implementation class per component; is external source omittable |
| `../THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv` | the upstream pins that replace 149 GB of source |

`restore/locks/` holds one pinned dependency lock per Python environment — 594 pins across
seven. There is deliberately no single `requirements.txt`: the API runs on the Debian system
interpreter with no virtualenv, and six applications have their own. Pretending there is one
environment would make the file wrong.

---

## The thing most worth understanding

**`external/` is 149 GB and is not in the backup, but three production engines are built out
of it.** That is not a contradiction and it is not hidden.

`tools/sh/fork_engines.sh` builds `symoneural-llm`, `symoneural-diffuse` and `symoneural-listen`
from upstream source in `external/referencestochatgpt/`. It is a real, load-bearing
build-time dependency. Claiming otherwise to make a gate go green would be a lie the next
restore would discover.

What makes the tree omittable is that every one of those checkouts is a **clean clone of a
public remote at a pinned revision** — verified against the checkout while the checkout was
still there to verify against. So the dependency is on an *upstream*, which is reacquirable,
not on a *local directory*, which is not:

```bash
tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh --check     # what is here, what is missing, at which revision
tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh all         # fetch the three MIT engines at their exact pins
```

This was rehearsed, not assumed. A clone taken from the Git bundle alone — no `external/`,
no `.private/`, no working tree — reacquired `whisper.cpp` from GitHub at
`1fe009caeda75f69bc864d6370b10674e45a92bd` and rebuilt the engine from it.

`backend/apps/test_no_external_source_dependency.py` keeps this honest: no production
runtime may resolve a path into a tree that will not survive the reset, and it catches the
split form `ROOT / "external" / "contrib"` as well as the string form, because a substring
search once missed nine files spelled that way and the shims everyone believed were dead
turned out to be load-bearing.

### The exception

`kawpowminer` carries three uncommitted local modifications — including a real
`#include <cstdint>` fix for gcc 13+ no longer leaking `uint8_t` via `<cstring>`. A revision
pin cannot restore work that was never committed anywhere, so the patch is preserved at
`.private/upstream-patches/` and the manifest says the pin alone is not sufficient for that
one. `restore-upstream.sh` applies it and **fails loudly** if it is missing rather than
building something subtly different.

---

## What is deliberately not first-party

No component is called first-party because it was renamed. The classification is:

| Component | Class | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `symoneural-llm`, `-diffuse`, `-listen` | `THIRD_PARTY_DERIVATIVE_PERMISSIVE` | MIT forks. Our patches are ours; the upstream notice travels with the code. |
| `symoneural-miner`, `symoneural-ui` | `THIRD_PARTY_DERIVATIVE_COPYLEFT` | GPL-3.0. **DISABLED**, not relabelled — a licence is a grant from the copyright holders, not a string in a file. |
| `symoneural-miner-core` | `CLEAN_ROOM_FROM_PUBLIC_SPEC` | Keccak written from FIPS PUB 202, round constants *computed* from the standard's LFSR rather than pasted. Incomplete and says so. |
| `symoneural-adaptive-fabric` | `DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` | README and LICENCE, no code. The plan must not appear to restore something that was never built. |
| the rest | `FIRST_PARTY` | ours |

`tools/sh/fork_engines.sh` already refuses to stamp the SyMoNeuRaL licence on a copyleft
upstream. Nothing here may undo that refusal by writing a friendlier word in a column.

---

## Regenerating

```bash
python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py     # then run it AGAIN and diff
python3 tools/build/build_dependency_locks.py      # or --check
cd backend && python3 -m pytest apps/test_restore_manifests.py \
                                apps/test_no_external_source_dependency.py -q
```

Run the generator twice and diff. Three separate generators in this repository have re-read
their own output and accumulated a copy per run, which is why two clean runs is the check
rather than a courtesy.

One consequence worth knowing: **a generated manifest can never name the commit that
contains it.** It records the revision it was generated from, and committing it produces a
new revision. The tests treat determinism and freshness as separate properties for exactly
this reason — the same impossibility that once had `BACKUP.json` carrying the hash of the
ZIP it was inside.

---

## `.private/` — what Git cannot hold

Not source. Recovery state, `0700` throughout with every file `0600`:

```
.private/application-state/<release>/   consistent SQLite images + env + ledgers
.private/source-bundles/<release>/      one tar.gz per first-party component
.private/runtime-artifacts/<release>/   built binaries as FALLBACK, never authority
.private/git-backup/                    Symoneural-all.bundle, all 31 refs
.private/host-snapshot/rootfs/          installed units and Caddy config
.private/upstream-patches/              edits a revision pin cannot restore
.private/claude-backups/                the owner's retirement backup (hard-linked)
```

Two rules that are easy to get wrong:

**A live SQLite database must not be copied byte-for-byte.** Two of these stores had a `-wal`
and `-shm` beside them when the backup was taken, meaning a writer was attached; a plain copy
mid-transaction produces a file that passes a checksum, restores without error, and is
corrupt. Every one goes through `sqlite3 .backup` and is then proved with
`PRAGMA integrity_check` — a backup that has not been opened is a hope.

**The preferred restore is always a rebuild.** `runtime-artifacts/` exists for the case where
that fails, and for comparing what you built against what ran. It is evidence, never source
authority.

# Source 6: `symoneuraldiverged.md`

> Original attached content preserved below so commands, measurements, corrections, and historical wording remain intact.

The DIVERGED has two layers, and separating them matters.

My measurement bug: the tracked units are templates containing @@ROOT@@, substituted at install time. A raw SHA comparison can only ever say DIVERGED. That's my error and I'll fix the comparison to substitute first.

A genuine production defect underneath it, which the corrected comparison must still catch: the installed symoneural-api.service (2026-09-01) predates the template fix (2026-09-03) and is missing two real changes —

- StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst still sit in [Service], where systemd silently ignores them. The template moved them to [Unit]. So the crash-loop protection the running unit's own comment describes has never once applied.
- Before=symoneural-web.service is absent, so the API has no boot ordering against the process that actually serves — Before=caddy.service is a no-op on this host since caddy was superseded in the 2026-08-26 cutover.

Same on the gateway unit. I am not reinstalling these — that is altering a production service and the authority for it wasn't granted. Recording it as a blocker and making the restore plan install the corrected template.

  python3 - <<'PY'
  import pathlib
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/measure.py")
  t = p.read_text()

  old_unit = '''def unit_state(unit: str, user: bool = False) -> tuple[str, str]:
      """(enabled-state, active-state) as systemd reports them right now.

      Read from systemd, never from a table. A service-map row reading 'defined but disabled'
      was reported as an anomaly three times about a unit that was enabled and active and is
      the public web server -- the row was wrong and nobody had opened the unit.
      """
      base = ["systemctl", "--user"] if user else ["systemctl"]
      en = run(base + ["is-enabled", unit], timeout=30)
      ac = run(base + ["is-active", unit], timeout=30)
      return (en or "UNMEASURED", ac or "UNMEASURED")'''

  new_unit = '''def _systemctl_state(args: list[str]) -> str:
      """`systemctl is-enabled` / `is-active` answer on STDOUT and exit NON-ZERO for the
      perfectly ordinary answers `disabled`, `inactive` and `static`.

      The generic `run()` above maps a non-zero exit to `UNMEASURED`, which is right for a
      command that failed and wrong for a command that answered. Routing these two through
      `run()` reported three units as UNMEASURED when systemd had told us exactly what they
      were -- publishing "we did not look" about a thing we had looked at, which is the same
      class of error as publishing a row instead of a reading.
      """
      try:
          p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
      except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
          return "UNMEASURED"
      out = p.stdout.strip()
      if out:
          return out
      return "not-found" if p.returncode else "UNMEASURED"


  def unit_state(unit: str, user: bool = False) -> tuple[str, str]:
      """(enabled-state, active-state) as systemd reports them right now.

      Read from systemd, never from a table. A service-map row reading 'defined but disabled'
      was reported as an anomaly three times about a unit that was enabled and active and is
      the public web server -- the row was wrong and nobody had opened the unit.
      """
      base = ["systemctl", "--user"] if user else ["systemctl"]
      return (_systemctl_state(base + ["is-enabled", unit]),
              _systemctl_state(base + ["is-active", unit]))'''

  assert old_unit in t, "unit_state block not found verbatim"
  t = t.replace(old_unit, new_unit)

  old_match = '''def installed_unit_matches(source_rel: str, installed: str) -> str:
      """Does the installed unit still match the tracked template it came from?"""
      src = ROOT / source_rel
      dst = pathlib.Path(os.path.expanduser(installed))
      if not src.is_file():
          return "SOURCE_ABSENT"
      if not dst.exists():
          return "NOT_INSTALLED"
      a, b = sha256(src), sha256(dst)
      if b.startswith("UNREADABLE"):
          return "UNREADABLE(root-owned)"
      return "MATCH" if a == b else "DIVERGED"'''

  new_match = '''def installed_unit_matches(source_rel: str, installed: str) -> str:
      """Does the installed unit still match the tracked template it came from?

      The tracked units are TEMPLATES carrying the literal `@@ROOT@@`, which the installers
      substitute for the repository root because systemd has no notion of a relative path. A
      raw checksum therefore says DIVERGED for a perfectly current install, every time, and a
      check that always fires tells you nothing. So the template is rendered the way the
      installer renders it and THEN compared.

      What survives that substitution is the difference that matters. Measured 2026-09-08:
      the installed API and gateway units still差 differ after rendering, because they were
      installed before the 2026-09-03 fix that moved StartLimit* out of `[Service]` -- where
      systemd was silently ignoring them -- into `[Unit]`.
      """
      src = ROOT / source_rel
      dst = pathlib.Path(os.path.expanduser(installed))
      if not src.is_file():
          return "SOURCE_ABSENT"
      if not dst.exists():
          return "NOT_INSTALLED"
      try:
          rendered = src.read_text(errors="replace").replace("@@ROOT@@", str(ROOT))
          on_disk = dst.read_text(errors="replace")
      except OSError as e:
          return f"UNREADABLE({e.errno})"
      if rendered == on_disk:
          return "MATCH"
      a = [l for l in rendered.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")]
      b = [l for l in on_disk.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")]
      if a == b:
          return "MATCH (comments differ only)"
      only_src = len([l for l in a if l not in b])
      only_dst = len([l for l in b if l not in a])
      return (f"DIVERGED (installed is STALE: {only_src} directive(s) in the template are "
              f"missing from the installed unit, {only_dst} present only on disk)")'''

  assert old_match in t, "installed_unit_matches block not found verbatim"
  t = t.replace(old_match, new_match)
  p.write_text(t)
  print("measure.py: fixed unit_state (non-zero exit is an answer) and installed_unit_matches (render template first)")
  PY)

  python3 - <<'PY'
  import pathlib

  # 1. stray character in measure.py
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/measure.py"); t = p.read_text()
  bad = "the installed API and gateway units still差 differ after rendering"
  good = "the installed API and gateway units still differ after rendering"
  assert bad in t, "typo not found"
  p.write_text(t.replace(bad, good))
  print("measure.py: repaired stray character")

  # 2. caddy: its unit is caddy.service; /etc/caddy/Caddyfile is a CONFIG FILE. Asking
  #    systemd about a unit named 'Caddyfile' returns not-found, which is a measurement of
  #    the wrong thing rather than a measurement of nothing.
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/registry.py"); t = p.read_text()
  old = '''    service_id: str
      component_id: str
      source_unit: str
      installed_unit: str'''
  new = '''    service_id: str
      component_id: str
      source_unit: str
      installed_unit: str
      # The systemd unit to interrogate. Usually the basename of `installed_unit`, but not
      # always: Caddy's tracked artefact is a Caddyfile, which is configuration, not a unit.
      # Deriving the unit name from the installed path asked systemd about a unit called
      # "Caddyfile" and got `not-found` -- a confident measurement of the wrong object.
      unit_name: str = "-"'''
  assert old in t
  t = t.replace(old, new, 1)

  # Service() is constructed positionally; unit_name has a default so append by keyword.
  t = t.replace('''        "sudo systemctl start caddy",
          "curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://symoneural.com/",''',
  '''        "sudo systemctl start caddy",
          "curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://symoneural.com/",
          unit_name="caddy.service",''')

  # 3. symoneural-ui claims a rebuild path it does not have: there is no fork_ui() in
  #    fork_engines.sh, so "buildable" must not read YES off the presence of a revision pin.
  t = t.replace('''        build_authority="manual fork; NOT built by tools/sh/fork_engines.sh",''',
  '''        build_authority="NONE -- there is no fork_ui() in tools/sh/fork_engines.sh",''')
  p.write_text(t)
  print("registry.py: added Service.unit_name, pinned caddy.service, corrected UI build authority")

  # 4. generate.py: use unit_name when given; and buildable must consult build authority.
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/generate.py"); t = p.read_text()
  old = '''        user_scope = s.installed_unit.startswith("~")
          unit_name = pathlib.Path(s.installed_unit).name'''
  new = '''        user_scope = s.installed_unit.startswith("~")
          unit_name = s.unit_name if s.unit_name != NUL \\
              else pathlib.Path(s.installed_unit).name'''
  assert old in t
  t = t.replace(old, new)

  old = '''            canonical = "UPSTREAM_PIN + tracked fork script"
              buildable = "YES" if c.upstream_rev != NUL else "NO"'''
  new = '''            canonical = "UPSTREAM_PIN + tracked fork script"
              # A revision pin alone does not make a tree buildable. symoneural-ui is pinned
              # and has NO scripted build path -- no fork_ui() exists -- so reading YES off
              # the pin would promise a rebuild that nothing can perform.
              scripted = c.build_authority.startswith("tools/sh/fork_engines.sh")
              if c.upstream_rev == NUL:
                  buildable = "NO (no upstream pin)"
              elif not scripted:
                  buildable = "NO (pinned, but no scripted build authority)"
              else:
                  buildable = "YES"'''
  assert old in t
  t = t.replace(old, new)
  p.write_text(t)
  print("generate.py: unit_name honoured; buildable now requires a build authority, not just a pin")
  PY)

One weakness in my own comparison I should not leave: it compares directives as a set, so the StartLimit fix — which moved lines from [Service] to [Unit] without changing their text — is invisible to it. That's precisely the defect that mattered most. Making the comparison section-aware:

  import pathlib
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/measure.py"); t = p.read_text()

  old = '''    if rendered == on_disk:

      a = [l for l in rendered.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")]
      b = [l for l in on_disk.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")]
      if a == b:
          return "MATCH (comments differ only)"
      only_src = len([l for l in a if l not in b])
      only_dst = len([l for l in b if l not in a])
      return (f"DIVERGED (installed is STALE: {only_src} directive(s) in the template are "
              f"missing from the installed unit, {only_dst} present only on disk)")'''

  new = '''    if rendered == on_disk:
          return "MATCH"

      # Section-aware, and that is not pedantry. The 2026-09-03 fix to these units MOVED
      # StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst from [Service] to [Unit] without changing a
      # character of either line -- systemd silently ignores them in [Service], so the
      # crash-loop protection had never applied. A set comparison of directive text calls
      # that MATCH, which would have reported the single most consequential difference
      # between the template and the installed unit as no difference at all.
      def directives(text: str) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
          section, out = "", set()
          for ln in text.splitlines():
              s = ln.strip()
              if not s or s.startswith("#"):
                  continue
              if s.startswith("[") and s.endswith("]"):
                  section = s
                  continue
              out.add((section, s))
          return out

      a, b = directives(rendered), directives(on_disk)
      if a == b:
          return "MATCH (comments differ only)"
      missing = sorted(a - b)
      extra = sorted(b - a)
      detail = "; ".join(f"{sec}{key.split('=')[0]}" for sec, key in (missing + extra)[:4])
      return (f"DIVERGED (installed is STALE: {len(missing)} directive(s) from the template "
              f"absent, {len(extra)} present only on disk: {detail})")'''

  t = t.replace(old, new)

# Dependencies — what each one does, what replacing it would cost, and the decision

Task #74 item 5. Garrett's standard, 2026-08-20: *"we should have the goal of rebranding
and/or writing fresh code for everything. You better have a really good and justified reason
for not doing so and this includes what is in the requirements.txt for python modules"*, with
the boundary drawn at *"nvidia sources i understand being locked down as of right now i see
no other sources as 'locked down' and they should be recreated"*.

So **recreate is the default and keeping is what needs an argument.** This file is where the
argument goes. A row with no reason is the failure this document exists to prevent.

**Read the three verdicts as different jobs, because they are.**

- **Recreate** — write ours, delete theirs. Reserved for what is small enough to own and
  central enough to matter.
- **Facade** — the package stays, but no application module names it. The import moves behind
  a module of ours so the vendor name appears in exactly one file per dependency and swapping
  it later is a one-file change. This is the honest answer to "rebrand a library you install
  from PyPI": the import name **is** the package's identity, so the rebranding actually
  available to us is the boundary, not the name.
- **Keep** — named directly, with the cost of replacement written down. Two of these would
  take the site's measured numbers *down*, which is the opposite of the point.

**What no verdict here can do is drop a notice.** MIT, BSD-3-Clause and Apache-2.0 all permit
renaming what we present; none permits removing the copyright notice from the accompanying
materials. `LICENSES.md` is that material. A `recreate` verdict retires a notice legitimately,
because we stop distributing the work; a `facade` verdict does not, because the package is
still installed and still shipped. Do not confuse the two.

## How the versions below were read

Every version is `importlib.metadata.version` on the interpreter that actually runs that
code, read 2026-08-21 at `f3ed5ab`. There is no single environment here and pretending there
is would make the table wrong: the serving path is the **system** interpreter (Debian, 212
packages, no virtualenv on purpose), and training, sigils, asicminer, studio and bento each
have their own venv. The interpreter is named in every row. Nothing in this table was copied
from a lockfile or carried forward.

> **Staleness boundary, audited 2026-08-26.** These are dated host readings, not the current
> install contract. Several requirement lower bounds now differ, training still has no

  third-party: ['asicminer', 'coder', 'cryptominer', 'fastapi', 'gateway', 'licensing', 'pydantic', 'ravencalc', 'runtimeconfig', 'starlette', 'symoneuralenv', 'uvicorn']
  local: ['apps']


A fabricated path in my own recipe — I wrote backend/requirements.lock.txt as the API's dependency lock and that file does not exist. backend/DEPENDENCIES.md explains why: the serving path is the system Debian interpreter, 212 packages, no virtualenv on purpose. So the lock has to be produced, not referenced. That is Target 11's requirement exactly: "Do not archive a venv as the only way to restore it... require a deterministic pinned dependency representation."

Generating a real lock from the interpreter that actually serves:

● Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  echo "############ which interpreter serves? (from the running unit) ############"
  ps -o pid,user,args -p 143775 2>/dev/null | tail -1
  echo
  echo "############ direct third-party imports across backend/ first-party code ############"
  python3 - <<'PY'
  import ast, pathlib, sys, importlib.metadata as md
  ROOT = pathlib.Path(".")
  std = set(sys.stdlib_module_names)
  # Only first-party backend code: skip vendored SDKs and third-party sub-trees.
  SKIP = ("backend/vendor/", "backend/apps/gateway/target", "__pycache__",
          "backend/models", "backend/output")
  mods = set()
  files = 0
  for p in ROOT.glob("backend/**/*.py"):
      s = str(p)
      if any(k in s for k in SKIP):
          continue
      try:
          tree = ast.parse(p.read_text(errors="replace"))
      except SyntaxError:
          continue
      files += 1
      for n in ast.walk(tree):
          if isinstance(n, ast.Import):
              for a in n.names: mods.add(a.name.split(".")[0])
          elif isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module and n.level == 0:
              mods.add(n.module.split(".")[0])

  # Anything importable from our own tree is first-party, not a dependency.
  local = {p.name for p in ROOT.glob("backend/*")} | {p.name for p in ROOT.glob("backend/apps/*")}
  local |= {p.stem for p in ROOT.glob("backend/*.py")} | {p.stem for p in ROOT.glob("backend/apps/*.py")}
  third = sorted(m for m in mods if m not in std and m not in local and not m.startswith("_"))
  print(f"  scanned {files} first-party python files")
  resolved = []
  for m in third:
      try:
          dist = md.distribution(m)
          resolved.append((m, dist.metadata["Name"], dist.version))
      except Exception:
          # importlib cannot map every import name to a distribution name.
          try:
              names = md.packages_distributions().get(m, [])
              if names:
                  v = md.version(names[0]); resolved.append((m, names[0], v))
              else:
                  resolved.append((m, "UNRESOLVED", "-"))
          except Exception:
              resolved.append((m, "UNRESOLVED", "-"))
  for imp, dist, ver in resolved:
      print(f"    {imp:<24} {dist:<28} {ver}")
  PY)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""Write one pinned dependency lock per Python environment on this box.

`backend/DEPENDENCIES.md` states the constraint this tool exists to respect:

    "There is no single environment here and pretending there is would make the table
     wrong: the serving path is the system interpreter (Debian, 212 packages, no
     virtualenv on purpose), and training, sigils, asicminer, studio and bento each have
     their own venv."

So there is no such thing as *the* lock file for this project, and a single
`requirements.lock.txt` at the repository root would be a confident description of an
environment that does not exist. This writes one lock per environment, each naming the
interpreter it was read from.

## Why a lock at all, when the venvs are sitting right there

The owner's restore spec, Target 11: *"Do not archive a venv as the only way to restore
it."* A venv is a directory of compiled artefacts built against one interpreter, one libc
and one CPU; it is evidence of what was installed, not a means of reinstalling it. The lock
is the means. The venv may still be preserved privately as fallback, and it is -- but the
service must be reconstructable without it, and that is what these files make true.

## What is pinned, and what is honestly not

Every distribution found in the environment is pinned to an exact `==` version. What is NOT
recorded is a hash for each artefact: these environments were populated over months from
PyPI and Debian both, and a hash line that was never verified against the wheel it claims to
pin is decoration. `pip install --require-hashes` would reject the file anyway unless every
transitive dependency carried one. Where hashes exist they come from the package manager, and
the manifest says which manager -- rather than this tool inventing a column it cannot fill.

    python3 tools/build/build_dependency_locks.py            # write the locks
    python3 tools/build/build_dependency_locks.py --check    # fail if any lock is out of date
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys


def find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise SystemExit("build_dependency_locks: no repository root found")


ROOT = find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
OUT = ROOT / "restore" / "locks"

# (lock name, interpreter, what this environment is for).
#
# The serving interpreter is FIRST and is the one that matters most: it is what
# `ops/units/symoneural-api.service` execs, measured from the running unit as
# `/usr/bin/python3 /home/google/Symoneural/backend/server.py`.
ENVIRONMENTS: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = [
    ("serving-system", "/usr/bin/python3",
     "The API. Debian system interpreter, deliberately not a virtualenv -- "
     "ops/units/symoneural-api.service execs it directly."),
    ("training", "training/.venv/bin/python3",
     "LoRA training and evaluation (torch, transformers, peft, trl, datasets)."),
    ("sigils", "backend/apps/sigils/.venv/bin/python3", "The Sigils render path."),
    ("studio", "backend/apps/studio/.venv/bin/python3",
     "Studio and its reinforce/exp/discovery plugins."),
    ("asicminer", "backend/apps/asicminer/.venv/bin/python3",
     "ASIC-side miner telemetry (pyasic)."),
    ("bento", "deploy/bento/.venv/bin/python3", "Bento packaging/deploy path."),
    ("symoneural-ui", "symoneural-ui/.venv/bin/python3",
     "The GPL-3.0 ComfyUI fork. DISABLED for the reset; the lock is recorded for "
     "completeness, not because the component is being carried."),
]

PROBE = (
    "import importlib.metadata as m, sys;"
    "print('#PY', sys.version.split()[0]);"
    "print('\\n'.join(sorted(f'{d.metadata[\"Name\"]}=={d.version}'"
    " for d in m.distributions() if d.metadata['Name'])))"
)


def read_environment(interp: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[str, list[str]] | None:
    if not interp.exists():
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([str(interp), "-c", PROBE], capture_output=True, text=True,
                           timeout=120)
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return None
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return None
    lines = [ln for ln in p.stdout.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("#PY"):
        return None
    version = lines[0].split(None, 1)[1]
    # De-duplicate: a name can appear twice when a dist-info and an egg-info coexist,
    # which happens on a box where pip and apt have both installed the same package.
    seen, pins = set(), []
    for ln in lines[1:]:
        name = ln.split("==")[0].lower().replace("_", "-")
        if name in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(name)
        pins.append(ln)
    return version, pins


def render(name: str, interp: str, purpose: str, version: str, pins: list[str]) -> str:
    stamp = datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    head = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "rev-parse", "--short=8", "HEAD"],
                          capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip() or "unknown"
    return (
        f"# SyMoNeuRaL dependency lock -- {name}\n"
        f"#\n"
        f"# {purpose}\n"
        f"#\n"
        f"# Interpreter : {interp}\n"
        f"# Python      : {version}\n"
        f"# Distributions: {len(pins)}\n"
        f"# Measured    : {stamp} at HEAD {head}\n"
        f"#\n"
        f"# GENERATED by tools/build/build_dependency_locks.py -- do not hand-edit. This is a\n"
        f"# reading of an environment, not a wish list: every line was read from the\n"
        f"# interpreter above with importlib.metadata, not copied from another file.\n"
        f"#\n"
        f"# Restore:\n"
        f"#     python3 -m venv <path>/.venv\n"
        f"#     <path>/.venv/bin/pip install -r restore/locks/{name}.lock.txt\n"
        f"#\n"
        f"# The serving environment is the exception -- it is the Debian system\n"
        f"# interpreter on purpose, so its lock is installed into the system interpreter\n"
        f"# (or a venv the unit is repointed at), never into a venv that nothing execs.\n"
        f"#\n"
        f"# No hashes: these environments were populated from PyPI and apt both over\n"
        f"# months, and a hash never verified against the wheel it claims to pin is\n"
        f"# decoration. See the module docstring.\n"
        + "".join(f"{p}\n" for p in pins)
    )


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    check = "--check" in argv
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stale, written, missing = [], [], []

    for name, interp_rel, purpose in ENVIRONMENTS:
        interp = pathlib.Path(interp_rel) if interp_rel.startswith("/") \
            else ROOT / interp_rel
        got = read_environment(interp)
        if got is None:
            missing.append((name, str(interp)))
            print(f"  {name:<16} ABSENT ({interp})")
            continue
        version, pins = got
        body = render(name, str(interp), purpose, version, pins)
        target = OUT / f"{name}.lock.txt"

        if check:
            # Compare the PIN LINES only. The header carries a timestamp, so a whole-file
            # comparison would report every lock as stale one second after writing it --
            # a check that always fires is a check nobody reads.
            def pins_of(text: str) -> list[str]:
                return [ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln and not ln.startswith("#")]
            if not target.exists() or pins_of(target.read_text()) != pins:
                stale.append(name)
                print(f"  {name:<16} STALE ({len(pins)} distributions in the environment)")
            else:
                print(f"  {name:<16} OK ({len(pins)} distributions)")
            continue

        target.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
        written.append((name, len(pins)))
        print(f"  {name:<16} wrote {len(pins):>3} pins  <- {interp}")

    if check:
        if stale:
            print(f"\nSTALE: {', '.join(stale)}")
            print("Run: python3 tools/build/build_dependency_locks.py")
            return 1
        print("\nall locks match their environments")
        return 0

    print(f"\nwrote {len(written)} lock file(s) to restore/locks/")
    if missing:
        print("environments not present on this host (recorded as absent, not guessed):")
        for name, interp in missing:
            print(f"  {name}: {interp}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""DEPENDENCIES.tsv and THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv.

The owner's rule for the reset is that external things are described, not carried:

    "For dependencies that are legally and technically external but reinstallable, store
     metadata, not source."

So this emits two tables.

`THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv` is the one that replaces 149 GB of `external/`. Each row
is an upstream that a first-party component is BUILT from, pinned to an exact revision on a
public remote. `SOURCE_COPY_REQUIRED=NO` on those rows is the claim that makes the tree
omittable, and it is only true because the pin is real -- which the generator verifies
against the checkout while the checkout is still here.

`DEPENDENCIES.tsv` is everything else: the platform, the toolchain, and the Python
distributions.

## Two honesty decisions, both visible in the output

**Licences are read, not assumed.** A Python distribution's licence comes from its own
metadata -- the `License` field, or the `License ::` trove classifier when the field is the
useless `UNKNOWN` that setuptools writes by default. Where neither exists the cell says
`UNDECLARED`, which is a fact about the package. Guessing "MIT" because most things are MIT
would put a legal claim in a manifest on the strength of a base rate.

**Per-package rows for the serving environment only.** The serving interpreter is what
`ops/units/symoneural-api.service` execs, so its 196 distributions each get a row. The six
per-application venvs get one row each pointing at their lock file, because 594 rows whose
licence column was filled by the same weak inference would look like more diligence and be
less. The locks carry the exact pins either way, and `REINSTALL_METHOD` names them.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import re
import subprocess

from lib import measure as M
from lib import registry as R

ROOT = M.ROOT
NUL = "-"

LOCKS = ROOT / "restore" / "locks"

# Host-level things a fresh Debian install needs before anything here builds. Versions are
# MEASURED at generation time; the package names are what apt actually calls them, checked
# against this host rather than remembered.
PLATFORM: list[tuple[str, str, str, str, str, str]] = [
    # (dep_id, name, tool_probe, apt package, class, used_by)
