def _classifier_licence(meta) -> str:
    """Licence from metadata, or an explicit UNDECLARED. Never a guess."""
    lic = (meta.get("License") or "").strip()
    if lic and lic.upper() not in ("UNKNOWN", "UNDECLARED", ""):
        # Some packages paste an entire licence text into this field.
        first = lic.splitlines()[0].strip()
        return (first[:60] + "…") if len(first) > 60 else first
    for c in meta.get_all("Classifier") or []:
        if c.startswith("License ::"):
            return c.rsplit("::", 1)[-1].strip()
    expr = (meta.get("License-Expression") or "").strip()
    return expr or "UNDECLARED"


def serving_distributions() -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """(name, version, licence) from the interpreter the API unit actually execs."""
    code = (
        "import importlib.metadata as m, json\n"
        "out=[]\n"
        "for d in m.distributions():\n"
        "    md=d.metadata\n"
        "    n=md['Name']\n"
        "    if not n: continue\n"
        "    lic=(md.get('License') or '').strip()\n"
        "    if not lic or lic.upper()=='UNKNOWN':\n"
        "        lic=''\n"
        "        for c in (md.get_all('Classifier') or []):\n"
        "            if c.startswith('License ::'):\n"
        "                lic=c.rsplit('::',1)[-1].strip(); break\n"
        "        if not lic:\n"
        "            lic=(md.get('License-Expression') or '').strip()\n"
        "    lic=(lic.splitlines() or [''])[0].strip() or 'UNDECLARED'\n"
        "    out.append([n, d.version, lic[:60]])\n"
        "print(json.dumps(out))\n"
    )
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/python3", "-c", code], capture_output=True,
                           text=True, timeout=180)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            return []
        import json
        rows = json.loads(p.stdout)
    except Exception:
        return []
    seen, out = set(), []
    for n, v, lic in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r[0].lower()):
        k = n.lower().replace("_", "-")
        if k in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(k)
        out.append((n, v, lic))
    return out


def lock_summary() -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    out = []
    if not LOCKS.is_dir():
        return out
    for f in sorted(LOCKS.glob("*.lock.txt")):
        pins = len([ln for ln in f.read_text().splitlines()
                    if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")])
        out.append((f.name.replace(".lock.txt", ""), pins))
    return out


def verify_pin(c: R.Component) -> str:
    """Is the recorded upstream revision actually what is checked out right now?

    Recorded pins are the whole basis for omitting `external/`. While that tree is still on
    this disk the claim is checkable, so it gets checked -- once it is gone, nobody can.
    """
    if c.upstream_rev == NUL or c.upstream_local_path == NUL:
        return "n/a"
    p = ROOT / c.upstream_local_path
    if not p.is_dir():
        return "UPSTREAM_TREE_ABSENT (pin unverifiable from this host)"
    actual = M.repo_rev_of(p)
    if actual == c.upstream_rev:
        dirty = M.repo_dirty_count(p)
        if isinstance(dirty, int) and dirty:
            return f"PIN_VERIFIED but tree has {dirty} uncommitted change(s)"
        return "PIN_VERIFIED"
    return f"PIN_MISMATCH (registry={c.upstream_rev[:12]} disk={str(actual)[:12]})"


def gen_third_party_rebuild(write_tsv_root) -> int:
    header = ["DEPENDENCY_ID", "NAME", "CLASS", "VERSION", "LICENSE", "PACKAGE_MANAGER",
              "PACKAGE_NAME", "UPSTREAM_PROJECT", "PINNED_REVISION", "PIN_VERIFIED",
              "LOCAL_PATCH", "USED_BY", "BUILD_OR_RUNTIME", "REQUIRED",
              "REINSTALL_COMMAND_OR_METHOD", "SOURCE_COPY_REQUIRED", "NOTES"]
    rows = []
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        if c.upstream == NUL:
            continue
        required = "YES" if c.production_status == R.PRODUCTION else \
            f"NO ({c.production_status})"
        reinstall = (f"git clone {c.upstream} <dir> && git -C <dir> checkout "
                     f"{c.upstream_rev}")
        # A tree with uncommitted local edits cannot be restored by a pin alone. Saying
        # SOURCE_COPY_REQUIRED=NO for it would be true of the upstream and false of what
        # is actually built here, so the patch is named instead.
        copy_required = "NO"
        note = "Reacquired at the pinned revision; no source copy travels in the backup."
        if c.local_patch != NUL:
            note = ("Upstream carries UNCOMMITTED local modifications. The pin restores "
                    "the upstream; the preserved patch restores our changes. Both are "
                    "required, and neither is the source tree.")
        rows.append([
            f"upstream-{c.component_id}", c.upstream_local_path.split("/")[-1],
            "UPSTREAM_SOURCE", c.upstream_rev[:12], c.upstream_license, "git",
            c.upstream.rsplit("/", 1)[-1].replace(".git", ""), c.upstream,
            c.upstream_rev, verify_pin(c), c.local_patch, c.component_id, "BUILD",
            required, reinstall, copy_required, note,
        ])
    out = ROOT / "THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv"
    out.write_text("\t".join(header) + "\n" +
                   "".join("\t".join(write_tsv_root(x) for x in r) + "\n" for r in rows),
                   encoding="utf-8")
    return len(rows)


def gen_dependencies(write_tsv) -> int:
    header = ["DEPENDENCY_ID", "NAME", "VERSION", "LICENSE", "CLASS", "PACKAGE_MANAGER",
              "PACKAGE_NAME", "UPSTREAM", "CHECKSUM", "USED_BY", "BUILD_OR_RUNTIME",
              "REQUIRED", "REINSTALL_METHOD", "OFFLINE_COPY_PRESENT",
              "SOURCE_TREE_REQUIRED"]
    rows: list[list] = []

    # ---- platform and toolchain, versions measured now
    for dep_id, name, probe, pkg, cls, used in PLATFORM:
        ver = M.tool_version(probe)
        rows.append([dep_id, name, ver, "see distribution", cls, "apt", pkg,
                     "Debian" if "NVIDIA" not in pkg else "NVIDIA",
                     NUL, used, "BUILD" if cls == "BUILD_TOOL" else "RUNTIME",
                     "YES" if ver != "ABSENT" else "YES (ABSENT on this host)",
                     f"sudo apt-get install -y {pkg}", "NO", "NO"])

    # ---- the GPU driver: not apt on this host, and saying so is the point
    rows.append(["dep-nvidia-driver", "NVIDIA driver", M.gpu(), "proprietary",
                 "PLATFORM_RUNTIME", "vendor installer", "nvidia-driver", "NVIDIA",
                 NUL, "all GPU components", "RUNTIME", "YES",
                 "Install the driver matching the CUDA toolkit above from NVIDIA. Not "
                 "redistributable; not carried in the backup.", "NO", "NO"])

    # ---- python distributions on the serving interpreter, one row each
    for name, ver, lic in serving_distributions():
        rows.append([f"py-serving-{name.lower()}", name, ver, lic, "PYTHON_PACKAGE",
                     "pip/apt", name, "PyPI", NUL, "symoneural-api", "RUNTIME", "YES",
                     "pip install -r restore/locks/serving-system.lock.txt",
                     "NO", "NO"])

    # ---- the other environments, one row each pointing at their lock
    for env, pins in lock_summary():
        if env == "serving-system":
            continue
        rows.append([f"pyenv-{env}", f"{env} virtualenv", f"{pins} pinned distributions",
                     "per-package; see the lock", "PYTHON_ENVIRONMENT", "pip", NUL,
                     "PyPI", NUL, env, "RUNTIME",
                     "YES" if env != "symoneural-ui" else "NO (component DISABLED)",
                     f"python3 -m venv <path>/.venv && <path>/.venv/bin/pip install -r "
                     f"restore/locks/{env}.lock.txt",
                     "NO", "NO"])

    return write_tsv("DEPENDENCIES.tsv", header, rows, minimum=100)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""Take a consistent backup of every persistent state store into `.private/`.

Git restores source. It cannot restore the account database, the project store, the
operator's ledgers, the trained adapter, or the environment file the API reads its
configuration out of. This is the half of a restore that source control has no opinion
about, and it is the half that is actually irreplaceable.

## The one rule that makes this different from `cp -a run/`

**A live SQLite database must not be copied byte-for-byte.** Two of these stores had a `-wal`
and `-shm` file beside them when this was written, which means a writer was attached; a
plain copy of a database mid-transaction produces a file that passes a checksum, restores
without error, and is corrupt. So every SQLite store goes through `sqlite3 .backup`, which
takes the database's own read lock and writes a consistent image, and the result is then
proved with `PRAGMA integrity_check` before it is recorded. A backup that has not been
opened is a hope.

## Modes

`.private/` is 0700 and every file written into it is 0600, without exception -- these are
session databases, an env file and the owner's private ledgers. The archive that eventually
carries them is 0600 too. The one thing this script will not do is widen a mode to make a
copy easier.

    python3 tools/build/build_private_state.py --release r20260908 --dry-run
    python3 tools/build/build_private_state.py --release r20260908
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys


def find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise SystemExit("build_private_state: no repository root found")


ROOT = find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "restore"))
from lib import registry as R          # noqa: E402


def sha256(p: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with p.open("rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def dir_digest(d: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """A stable digest over a directory: sorted relative paths and their content hashes.

    Not a tar checksum -- tar embeds mtimes and ordering, so two identical trees hash
    differently and the value proves nothing about the content.
    """
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    n = 0
    for f in sorted(d.rglob("*")):
        if f.is_file() and not f.is_symlink():
            h.update(str(f.relative_to(d)).encode())
            h.update(sha256(f).encode())
            n += 1
    return h.hexdigest(), n


def secure_dir(p: pathlib.Path) -> None:
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(p, 0o700)


def backup_sqlite(src: pathlib.Path, dst: pathlib.Path, dry: bool) -> dict:
    """Consistent SQLite image via the engine, then prove it opens and passes integrity."""
    if dry:
        return {"method": "sqlite3 .backup", "would_write": str(dst), "status": "DRY_RUN"}
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(dst.parent, 0o700)
    if dst.exists():
        dst.unlink()
    # `.backup` rather than VACUUM INTO: it copes with a concurrent writer, which is the
    # situation actually observed here, and it does not rewrite page layout.
    p = subprocess.run(["sqlite3", str(src), f".backup '{dst}'"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return {"method": "sqlite3 .backup", "status": "FAILED",
                "error": p.stderr.strip()[:200]}
    os.chmod(dst, 0o600)
    chk = subprocess.run(["sqlite3", str(dst), "PRAGMA integrity_check;"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    ok = chk.stdout.strip() == "ok"
    return {"method": "sqlite3 .backup", "status": "OK" if ok else "INTEGRITY_FAILED",
            "integrity_check": chk.stdout.strip()[:100],
            "sha256": sha256(dst), "bytes": dst.stat().st_size}


def backup_file(src: pathlib.Path, dst: pathlib.Path, dry: bool) -> dict:
    if dry:
        return {"method": "cp -p", "would_write": str(dst), "status": "DRY_RUN"}
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(dst.parent, 0o700)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)
    os.chmod(dst, 0o600)
    return {"method": "cp -p", "status": "OK", "sha256": sha256(dst),
            "bytes": dst.stat().st_size, "source_mode": oct(src.stat().st_mode & 0o777)}


def backup_dir(src: pathlib.Path, dst: pathlib.Path, dry: bool) -> dict:
    if dry:
        return {"method": "rsync -a", "would_write": str(dst), "status": "DRY_RUN"}
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(dst.parent, 0o700)
    # -a implies -l, so symlinks are preserved as symlinks. `--no-dereference` does NOT
    # exist in rsync 3.4.1 and passing it silently archived 212 files instead of 68,278
    # because the error went to a suppressed stderr. Do not add it.
    p = subprocess.run(["rsync", "-a", "--delete", f"{src}/", f"{dst}/"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=7200)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return {"method": "rsync -a", "status": "FAILED",
                "error": p.stderr.strip()[:300]}
    digest, n = dir_digest(dst)
    return {"method": "rsync -a", "status": "OK", "content_digest": digest,
            "file_count": n}


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--release", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--skip-large", action="store_true",
                    help="skip backend/models and training/adapter (bulk weights)")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    base = ROOT / ".private" / "application-state" / a.release
    if not a.dry_run:
        secure_dir(ROOT / ".private")
        secure_dir(base)

    report: dict[str, dict] = {}
    print(f"{'store':<20} {'method':<18} {'status':<18} detail")
    print("-" * 88)

    for s in R.STATE_STORES:
        paths = [x.strip() for x in s.live_path.split(",") if x.strip()]
        results = []
        for rel in paths:
            src = ROOT / rel
            if not src.exists():
                results.append({"path": rel, "status": "SOURCE_ABSENT"})
                continue
            if a.skip_large and s.state_id in ("models", "training-adapters"):
                results.append({"path": rel, "status": "SKIPPED (--skip-large)"})
                continue
            dst = base / s.state_id / pathlib.Path(rel).name
            if src.is_dir():
                r = backup_dir(src, base / s.state_id / pathlib.Path(rel).name, a.dry_run)
            elif "sqlite" in s.type_.lower():
                r = backup_sqlite(src, dst, a.dry_run)
            else:
                r = backup_file(src, dst, a.dry_run)
            r["path"] = rel
            r["source_bytes"] = src.stat().st_size if src.is_file() else None
            results.append(r)

        report[s.state_id] = {
            "application": s.application,
            "consistency_method": s.consistency_method,
            "contains_secrets": s.contains_secrets,
            "required_for_restore": s.required_for_restore,
            "restore_destination": s.restore_destination,
            "restore_command": s.restore_command,
            "validation_command": s.validation_command,
            "results": results,
        }
        for r in results:
            detail = r.get("integrity_check") or r.get("error") or \
                (f"{r.get('file_count')} files" if r.get("file_count") is not None else "")
            if r.get("sha256"):
                detail = f"sha256 {r['sha256'][:16]}… {detail}".strip()
            print(f"  {s.state_id:<18} {r.get('method','-'):<18} "
                  f"{r.get('status','-'):<18} {detail}")

    if a.dry_run:
        print("\nDRY RUN -- nothing was written.")
        return 0

    manifest = base / "STATE-MANIFEST.json"
    manifest.write_text(json.dumps({
        "release_id": a.release,
        "created_at": datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "repository_head": subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip(),
        # No secret VALUES here, ever -- only which stores contain secrets, so a restorer
        # knows which files to place with care. Names, not contents.
        "stores": report,
    }, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    os.chmod(manifest, 0o600)

    failed = [k for k, v in report.items()
              if any(r.get("status") not in ("OK", "SOURCE_ABSENT")
                     and not str(r.get("status", "")).startswith("SKIPPED")
                     for r in v["results"])]
    print(f"\nwrote {manifest.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    if failed:
        print(f"FAILED stores: {', '.join(failed)}")
        return 1
    print("all stores backed up and verified")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""Take a consistent backup of every persistent state store into `.private/`.

Git restores source. It cannot restore the account database, the project store, the
operator's ledgers, the trained adapter, or the environment file the API reads its
configuration out of. This is the half of a restore that source control has no opinion
about, and it is the half that is actually irreplaceable.

## The one rule that makes this different from `cp -a run/`

**A live SQLite database must not be copied byte-for-byte.** Two of these stores had a `-wal`
and `-shm` file beside them when this was written, which means a writer was attached; a
plain copy of a database mid-transaction produces a file that passes a checksum, restores
without error, and is corrupt. So every SQLite store goes through `sqlite3 .backup`, which
takes the database's own read lock and writes a consistent image, and the result is then
proved with `PRAGMA integrity_check` before it is recorded. A backup that has not been
opened is a hope.

## Modes

`.private/` is 0700 and every file written into it is 0600, without exception -- these are
session databases, an env file and the owner's private ledgers. The archive that eventually
carries them is 0600 too. The one thing this script will not do is widen a mode to make a
copy easier.

    python3 tools/build/build_private_state.py --release r20260908 --dry-run
    python3 tools/build/build_private_state.py --release r20260908
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys


def find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise SystemExit("build_private_state: no repository root found")


ROOT = find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "restore"))
from lib import registry as R          # noqa: E402


def sha256(p: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with p.open("rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def dir_digest(d: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """A stable digest over a directory: sorted relative paths and their content hashes.

    Not a tar checksum -- tar embeds mtimes and ordering, so two identical trees hash
    differently and the value proves nothing about the content.
    """
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    n = 0
    for f in sorted(d.rglob("*")):
        if f.is_file() and not f.is_symlink():
            h.update(str(f.relative_to(d)).encode())
            h.update(sha256(f).encode())
            n += 1
    return h.hexdigest(), n


def secure_dir(p: pathlib.Path) -> None:
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(p, 0o700)


def backup_sqlite(src: pathlib.Path, dst: pathlib.Path, dry: bool) -> dict:
    """Consistent SQLite image via the engine, then prove it opens and passes integrity."""
    if dry:
        return {"method": "sqlite3 .backup", "would_write": str(dst), "status": "DRY_RUN"}
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(dst.parent, 0o700)
    if dst.exists():
        dst.unlink()
    # `.backup` rather than VACUUM INTO: it copes with a concurrent writer, which is the
    # situation actually observed here, and it does not rewrite page layout.
    p = subprocess.run(["sqlite3", str(src), f".backup '{dst}'"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return {"method": "sqlite3 .backup", "status": "FAILED",
                "error": p.stderr.strip()[:200]}
    os.chmod(dst, 0o600)
    chk = subprocess.run(["sqlite3", str(dst), "PRAGMA integrity_check;"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    ok = chk.stdout.strip() == "ok"
    return {"method": "sqlite3 .backup", "status": "OK" if ok else "INTEGRITY_FAILED",
            "integrity_check": chk.stdout.strip()[:100],
            "sha256": sha256(dst), "bytes": dst.stat().st_size}


def backup_file(src: pathlib.Path, dst: pathlib.Path, dry: bool) -> dict:
    if dry:
        return {"method": "cp -p", "would_write": str(dst), "status": "DRY_RUN"}
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(dst.parent, 0o700)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)
    os.chmod(dst, 0o600)
    return {"method": "cp -p", "status": "OK", "sha256": sha256(dst),
            "bytes": dst.stat().st_size, "source_mode": oct(src.stat().st_mode & 0o777)}


def backup_dir(src: pathlib.Path, dst: pathlib.Path, dry: bool) -> dict:
    if dry:
        return {"method": "rsync -a", "would_write": str(dst), "status": "DRY_RUN"}
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(dst.parent, 0o700)
    # -a implies -l, so symlinks are preserved as symlinks. `--no-dereference` does NOT
    # exist in rsync 3.4.1 and passing it silently archived 212 files instead of 68,278
    # because the error went to a suppressed stderr. Do not add it.
    p = subprocess.run(["rsync", "-a", "--delete", f"{src}/", f"{dst}/"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=7200)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return {"method": "rsync -a", "status": "FAILED",
                "error": p.stderr.strip()[:300]}
    digest, n = dir_digest(dst)
    return {"method": "rsync -a", "status": "OK", "content_digest": digest,
            "file_count": n}


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--release", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--skip-large", action="store_true",
                    help="skip backend/models and training/adapter (bulk weights)")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    base = ROOT / ".private" / "application-state" / a.release
    if not a.dry_run:
        secure_dir(ROOT / ".private")
        secure_dir(base)

    report: dict[str, dict] = {}
    print(f"{'store':<20} {'method':<18} {'status':<18} detail")
    print("-" * 88)

    for s in R.STATE_STORES:
        paths = [x.strip() for x in s.live_path.split(",") if x.strip()]
        results = []
        for rel in paths:
            src = ROOT / rel
            if not src.exists():
                results.append({"path": rel, "status": "SOURCE_ABSENT"})
                continue
            if a.skip_large and s.state_id in ("models", "training-adapters"):
                results.append({"path": rel, "status": "SKIPPED (--skip-large)"})
                continue
            dst = base / s.state_id / pathlib.Path(rel).name
            if src.is_dir():
                r = backup_dir(src, base / s.state_id / pathlib.Path(rel).name, a.dry_run)
            elif "sqlite" in s.type_.lower():
                r = backup_sqlite(src, dst, a.dry_run)
            else:
                r = backup_file(src, dst, a.dry_run)
            r["path"] = rel
            r["source_bytes"] = src.stat().st_size if src.is_file() else None
            results.append(r)

        report[s.state_id] = {
            "application": s.application,
            "consistency_method": s.consistency_method,
            "contains_secrets": s.contains_secrets,
            "required_for_restore": s.required_for_restore,
            "restore_destination": s.restore_destination,
            "restore_command": s.restore_command,
            "validation_command": s.validation_command,
            "results": results,
        }
        for r in results:
            detail = r.get("integrity_check") or r.get("error") or \
                (f"{r.get('file_count')} files" if r.get("file_count") is not None else "")
            if r.get("sha256"):
                detail = f"sha256 {r['sha256'][:16]}… {detail}".strip()
            print(f"  {s.state_id:<18} {r.get('method','-'):<18} "
                  f"{r.get('status','-'):<18} {detail}")

    if a.dry_run:
        print("\nDRY RUN -- nothing was written.")
        return 0

    manifest = base / "STATE-MANIFEST.json"
    manifest.write_text(json.dumps({
        "release_id": a.release,
        "created_at": datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "repository_head": subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip(),
        # No secret VALUES here, ever -- only which stores contain secrets, so a restorer
        # knows which files to place with care. Names, not contents.
        "stores": report,
    }, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    os.chmod(manifest, 0o600)

    failed = [k for k, v in report.items()
              if any(r.get("status") not in ("OK", "SOURCE_ABSENT")
                     and not str(r.get("status", "")).startswith("SKIPPED")
                     for r in v["results"])]
    print(f"\nwrote {manifest.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    if failed:
        print(f"FAILED stores: {', '.join(failed)}")
        return 1
    print("all stores backed up and verified")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""Populate `.private/` -- the half of a bare-metal restore that Git cannot hold.

Six jobs, each of which fails loudly rather than partially:

    upstream-patches   uncommitted local changes to a pinned upstream. A revision pin
                       restores the upstream; it cannot restore edits nobody committed.
    host-snapshot      the installed systemd units, the Caddy configuration and the
                       root-owned helpers. Configuration, NOT first-party source -- and
                       labelling it source would be the relabelling this project refuses.
    git-bundle         every ref in one verifiable file, so history survives a working
                       tree that restores badly.
    source-bundles     one tar.gz per first-party component. Redundancy only: Git stays
                       the source authority, and these exist for the case where it does
                       not survive.
    runtime-artifacts  the built binaries actually running today, with their checksums,
                       architectures and link tables. Fallback and evidence, never
                       source authority -- the preferred restore is always a rebuild.
    claude-backups     a second PATH to the owner's retirement backup, by hard link.

## Why the Claude backup is linked and not copied

The standing instruction on that checkpoint is: *preserve unchanged; never delete,
overwrite, rename, reuse or mutate it.* A move renames it and breaks the finalizer's
preserve list, which references the original path. A copy duplicates 11.7 GB for no
recovery benefit. `/home/google` and the repository are the same filesystem (device 66308,
measured), so a hard link gives `.private/claude-backups/` a real path to the identical
inode: the original is untouched, no space is consumed, and GNU tar stores the second path
as a link rather than a second copy. If the link cannot be made the script COPIES and says
so, rather than silently doing something else.

    python3 tools/build/build_recovery_root.py --release r20260908 --dry-run
    python3 tools/build/build_recovery_root.py --release r20260908 --only git-bundle
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys


def find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise SystemExit("build_recovery_root: no repository root found")


ROOT = find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "restore"))
from lib import registry as R          # noqa: E402
from lib import measure as M           # noqa: E402

PRIVATE = ROOT / ".private"


def sha256(p: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with p.open("rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def secure(p: pathlib.Path, mode: int = 0o700) -> pathlib.Path:
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.chmod(p, mode)
    return p


def sh(args: list[str], cwd: pathlib.Path | None = None, timeout: int = 3600):
    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd or ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          timeout=timeout)


# =========================================================================================
def job_upstream_patches(dry: bool) -> dict:
    out = secure(PRIVATE / "upstream-patches")
    result = {}
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        if c.upstream_local_path == "-":
            continue
        tree = ROOT / c.upstream_local_path
        if not (tree / ".git").exists():
            result[c.component_id] = {"status": "NOT_A_GIT_REPO"}
            continue
        dirty = sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=tree).stdout.strip()
        if not dirty:
            result[c.component_id] = {"status": "CLEAN (pin alone restores it)"}
            continue
        # `git diff` covers TRACKED modifications only. Untracked build directories
        # (.hunter/, build-stockarch/) are deliberately NOT captured: they are build
        # output, not source, and carrying them would be exactly the "installed-only
        # artefact standing in for source" the reset is trying to eliminate.
        diff = sh(["git", "diff"], cwd=tree).stdout
        modified = [ln for ln in dirty.splitlines() if ln[:2].strip() in ("M", "MM")]
        untracked = [ln for ln in dirty.splitlines() if ln.startswith("??")]
        name = f"{tree.name}-local.patch"
        if not dry:
            f = out / name
            f.write_text(diff, encoding="utf-8")
            os.chmod(f, 0o600)
        result[c.component_id] = {
            "status": "PATCH_WRITTEN" if not dry else "DRY_RUN",
            "patch": f".private/upstream-patches/{name}",
            "sha256": sha256(out / name) if not dry else None,
            "tracked_modifications": len(modified),
            "untracked_paths_NOT_captured": [u[3:] for u in untracked],
            "note": "Untracked entries are build output, not source; they are named here "
                    "so their omission is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.",
        }
    return result


# =========================================================================================
HOST_PATHS = [
    "/etc/systemd/system/symoneural-api.service",
    "/etc/systemd/system/symoneural-web.service",
    "/etc/systemd/system/symoneural-gateway.service",
    "/etc/caddy/Caddyfile",
    "/usr/local/sbin/symoneural-root",
    "/etc/symoneural",
]


def job_host_snapshot(dry: bool) -> dict:
    out = secure(PRIVATE / "host-snapshot" / "rootfs")
    result = {}
    for src_s in HOST_PATHS:
        src = pathlib.Path(src_s)
        if not src.exists():
            result[src_s] = {"status": "ABSENT"}
            continue
        dst = out / src_s.lstrip("/")
        try:
            if not dry:
                dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                if src.is_dir():
                    shutil.copytree(src, dst, dirs_exist_ok=True)
                else:
                    shutil.copy2(src, dst)
                    os.chmod(dst, 0o600)
            st = src.stat()
            result[src_s] = {
                "status": "CAPTURED" if not dry else "DRY_RUN",
                "source_mode": oct(st.st_mode & 0o777),
                "source_uid": st.st_uid, "source_gid": st.st_gid,
                "sha256": sha256(src) if src.is_file() else "DIRECTORY",
                "restored_as": f".private/host-snapshot/rootfs{src_s}",
            }
        except PermissionError:
            result[src_s] = {"status": "UNREADABLE (root-owned; needs sudo to capture)"}
    # User-scope units live in the owner's own config and are readable.
    user_units = pathlib.Path.home() / ".config/systemd/user"
    if user_units.is_dir():
        found = sorted(p.name for p in user_units.glob("symoneural-*"))
        if not dry and found:
            d = out / "home/google/.config/systemd/user"
            d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            for n in found:
                shutil.copy2(user_units / n, d / n)
        result["~/.config/systemd/user/symoneural-*"] = {
            "status": "CAPTURED" if not dry else "DRY_RUN", "units": found}
    return result


# =========================================================================================
def job_git_bundle(dry: bool) -> dict:
    out = secure(PRIVATE / "git-backup")
    bundle = out / "Symoneural-all.bundle"
    if dry:
        return {"status": "DRY_RUN", "would_write": str(bundle)}

    fsck = sh(["git", "fsck", "--full"], timeout=3600)
    # git fsck writes progress and "dangling" notices to stderr and still exits 0. Only a
    # non-zero exit is a failure; treating any stderr as failure would report a healthy
    # repository as broken.
    fsck_ok = fsck.returncode == 0

    b = sh(["git", "bundle", "create", str(bundle), "--all"], timeout=3600)
    if b.returncode != 0:
        return {"status": "BUNDLE_FAILED", "error": b.stderr.strip()[:400],
                "git_fsck": "PASS" if fsck_ok else "FAIL"}
    os.chmod(bundle, 0o600)
    v = sh(["git", "bundle", "verify", str(bundle)], timeout=1800)
    refs = sh(["git", "bundle", "list-heads", str(bundle)], timeout=600).stdout
    return {
        "status": "OK" if v.returncode == 0 else "VERIFY_FAILED",
        "path": ".private/git-backup/Symoneural-all.bundle",
        "sha256": sha256(bundle),
        "bytes": bundle.stat().st_size,
        "mode": oct(bundle.stat().st_mode & 0o777),
        "git_fsck": "PASS" if fsck_ok else "FAIL",
        "git_fsck_detail": (fsck.stderr.strip().splitlines() or ["clean"])[-1][:200],
        "bundle_verify": (v.stdout + v.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-1][:200]
        if (v.stdout or v.stderr) else "-",
        "ref_count": len([ln for ln in refs.splitlines() if ln.strip()]),
        "refs": [ln.split(None, 1)[-1] for ln in refs.splitlines() if ln.strip()][:40],
    }


# =========================================================================================
def job_source_bundles(release: str, dry: bool) -> dict:
    """One source-only tar.gz per first-party component.

    Only components whose source is genuinely OURS get a bundle. A "source bundle" of a
    GPL-3.0 fork would be redistribution of somebody else's code under our recovery
    directory, and the pin plus the patch already restore those trees properly.
    """
    out = secure(PRIVATE / "source-bundles" / release)
    result = {}
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        if c.first_party_status not in (R.FIRST_PARTY, R.CLEAN_ROOM):
            result[c.component_id] = {
                "status": "SKIPPED",
                "reason": f"{c.first_party_status} -- restored from its upstream pin, not "
                          f"from a bundle of somebody else's source"}
            continue
        files = sh(["git", "ls-files", "-z", "--", c.source_root]).stdout.split("\0")
        files = [f for f in files if f]
        if not files:
            result[c.component_id] = {"status": "NO_TRACKED_FILES",
                                      "source_root": c.source_root}
            continue
        tgz = out / f"{c.component_id}.tar.gz"
        if dry:
            result[c.component_id] = {"status": "DRY_RUN", "file_count": len(files)}
            continue
        listfile = out / f".{c.component_id}.files"
        listfile.write_text("\0".join(files), encoding="utf-8")
        # --null -T reads NUL-separated names, so a path with a space or a newline in it
        # cannot split into two arguments.
        t = sh(["tar", "-czf", str(tgz), "--null", "-T", str(listfile),
                "--owner=0", "--group=0", "--mtime=@0"], timeout=1800)
        listfile.unlink()
        if t.returncode != 0:
            result[c.component_id] = {"status": "TAR_FAILED",
                                      "error": t.stderr.strip()[:300]}
            continue
        os.chmod(tgz, 0o600)
        digest = sha256(tgz)
        side = out / f"{c.component_id}.tar.gz.sha256"
        side.write_text(f"{digest}  {tgz.name}\n", encoding="utf-8")
        os.chmod(side, 0o600)
        result[c.component_id] = {
            "status": "OK", "bundle": f".private/source-bundles/{release}/{tgz.name}",
            "sha256": digest, "bytes": tgz.stat().st_size, "file_count": len(files),
            "source_root": c.source_root, "source_revision": M.head(),
        }
    return result


# =========================================================================================
def job_runtime_artifacts(release: str, dry: bool) -> dict:
    """Preserve the built binaries as FALLBACK. Rebuild from source stays the restore."""
    out = secure(PRIVATE / "runtime-artifacts" / release)
    result = {}
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        if c.primary_artifact == "-":
            continue
        src = ROOT / c.primary_artifact
        if not src.is_file():
            result[c.component_id] = {"status": "NOT_A_FILE", "path": c.primary_artifact}
            continue
        if not (src.stat().st_mode & 0o111):
            result[c.component_id] = {"status": "NOT_EXECUTABLE (nothing to preserve as a "
                                                "runtime artefact)", "path": c.primary_artifact}
            continue
        dst = out / c.component_id / src.name
        if not dry:
            secure(dst.parent)
            shutil.copy2(src, dst)
            os.chmod(dst, 0o600)
        result[c.component_id] = {
            "status": "PRESERVED" if not dry else "DRY_RUN",
            "build_output": c.primary_artifact,
            "sha256": sha256(src),
            "bytes": src.stat().st_size,
            "file_type": M.file_type(src),
            "arch": M.elf_arch(src),
            "dynamic_dependencies": M.dynamic_deps(src, limit=40),
            "source_revision": M.head(),
            "build_recipe": c.build_command,
            "toolchain": c.toolchain,
            "preferred_restore": "REBUILD FROM SOURCE -- this copy is fallback and "
                                 "evidence, never the source authority",
        }
    return result


# =========================================================================================
CLAUDE_BACKUPS = [
    "/home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip",
    "/home/google/claude-backup-20260908-035459.zip.sha256",
]


def job_claude_backups(dry: bool) -> dict:
    out = secure(PRIVATE / "claude-backups" / "20260908-035459")
    result = {}
    for s in CLAUDE_BACKUPS:
        src = pathlib.Path(s)
        if not src.exists():
            result[s] = {"status": "ABSENT"}
            continue
        dst = out / src.name
        if dry:
            result[s] = {"status": "DRY_RUN", "would_link": str(dst)}
            continue
        if dst.exists():
            if dst.stat().st_ino == src.stat().st_ino:
                result[s] = {"status": "ALREADY_LINKED", "inode": src.stat().st_ino}
                continue
            dst.unlink()
        method = "hardlink"
        try:
            os.link(src, dst)
        except OSError:
            shutil.copy2(src, dst)
            os.chmod(dst, 0o600)
            method = "copy (hard link refused -- different filesystem)"
        result[s] = {
            "status": "LINKED", "method": method,
            "path": f".private/claude-backups/20260908-035459/{src.name}",
            "inode": src.stat().st_ino,
            "bytes": src.stat().st_size,
            "mode": oct(src.stat().st_mode & 0o777),
            "sha256": sha256(src) if src.stat().st_size < (200 << 20) else
                      "NOT_RECOMPUTED (11.7 GB; the original sidecar carries the digest "
                      "and the inode is identical, so a re-hash would prove only that "
                      "hashing is deterministic)",
            "note": "Original left in place and unmodified, as instructed.",
        }
    return result


# =========================================================================================
JOBS = {
    "upstream-patches": lambda rel, dry: job_upstream_patches(dry),
    "host-snapshot": lambda rel, dry: job_host_snapshot(dry),
    "git-bundle": lambda rel, dry: job_git_bundle(dry),
    "source-bundles": job_source_bundles,
    "runtime-artifacts": job_runtime_artifacts,
    "claude-backups": lambda rel, dry: job_claude_backups(dry),
}


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--release", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--only", action="append", choices=sorted(JOBS))
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not a.dry_run:
        secure(PRIVATE)

    report = {"release_id": a.release,
              "created_at": datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(
                  timespec="seconds"),
              "repository_head": M.head()}

    for name in (a.only or list(JOBS)):
        print(f"\n=== {name} " + "=" * (70 - len(name)))
        res = JOBS[name](a.release, a.dry_run)
        report[name] = res
        for k, v in res.items():
            st = v.get("status", "?") if isinstance(v, dict) else str(v)
            extra = ""
            if isinstance(v, dict):
                if v.get("sha256") and len(str(v["sha256"])) == 64:
                    extra = f"sha256 {v['sha256'][:16]}…"
                elif v.get("file_count") is not None:
                    extra = f"{v['file_count']} files"
                elif v.get("reason"):
                    extra = v["reason"][:70]
                elif v.get("ref_count") is not None:
                    extra = f"{v['ref_count']} refs"
            print(f"  {str(k)[:52]:<52} {st:<22} {extra}")

    if a.dry_run:
        print("\nDRY RUN -- nothing was written.")
        return 0

    man = PRIVATE / f"RECOVERY-ROOT-{a.release}.json"
    man.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str) + "\n",
                   encoding="utf-8")
    os.chmod(man, 0o600)
    print(f"\nwrote {man.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

Three confirmations and one defect.

Hard link proven: identical inode 15896551, link count 2, mode 600 preserved on the original, and free space is unchanged at 233 G — an 11.7 GB second path for zero bytes.

The kawpowminer patch is real work, not noise — it carries a genuine #include <cstdint> fix for gcc 13+ no longer leaking uint8_t via <cstring>. That would have been lost to a revision pin.

Defect: mode violations. mkdir(parents=True) created intermediate directories at 775 under the umask, and two user-unit files copied in at 664. The standing rule is 0700 dirs / 0600 files, never 0644. .private itself being 0700 means nothing is actually reachable, but the rule is explicit and defence-in-depth is the point of it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""SyMoNeuRaL Restore -- bring this project back on a machine that has never seen it.

The problem this solves is not "where are the files". It is that every step of standing
this system up currently lives in somebody's head or in a commit message: which upstream
revision an engine forks from, which of seven Python environments a component runs in,
which database cannot be copied with `cp`, which systemd unit is deliberately disabled and
which is stale, and what order any of it has to happen in. After a bare-metal reinstall
none of that is recoverable by looking at a directory listing.

So it is written down in `restore/manifests/`, generated from measurement, and this is the
program that reads it.

    symoneural-restore inventory                what exists, and what class it is
    symoneural-restore verify                   is this tree internally consistent
    symoneural-restore dependencies --check     what is missing on THIS host
    symoneural-restore dependencies --instructions
    symoneural-restore build <component|all>
    symoneural-restore test <component|all>
    symoneural-restore install <component|all>
    symoneural-restore restore-state --dry-run | --apply
    symoneural-restore services --check | --install
    symoneural-restore smoke <application|all>
    symoneural-restore status

## Safety, and why it is structural rather than a warning in the README

Every subcommand that can change this machine is **dry by default and prints the exact
command it would run**. `--apply` is the only way to make anything happen, and the
privileged steps additionally refuse to run themselves: `services --install` and the Caddy
step PRINT a root command for a human to execute rather than invoking `sudo` on their own
authority. A restore tool that silently escalates is a restore tool nobody can safely run
twice.

It also refuses rather than guesses. An unknown component id is an error, not a no-op. A
missing manifest is an error, not an empty result. A dependency that is absent is named
exactly, with the command that installs it, instead of being reported as "some deps
missing". The failure mode this is written against is a tool that returns 0 having done
nothing, on a machine where the operator cannot tell the difference.

## Standard library only

This runs on a freshly installed Linux box before anything has been pip-installed --
including, necessarily, before the thing that installs the dependencies has run. Importing
a third-party package here would make the bootstrapper depend on the bootstrap.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- location
def find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Marker walk. Never `parents[2]` -- that encodes this file's depth in the tree."""
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "restore" / "manifests").is_dir() and (cand / "backend").is_dir():
            return cand
    raise SystemExit(
        "symoneural-restore: could not find the repository root above "
        f"{start}.\nExpected a directory containing both restore/manifests/ and backend/.")


ROOT = find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
MANIFESTS = ROOT / "restore" / "manifests"
RELEASE = ROOT / "restore" / "RELEASE.json"

BOLD, DIM, RED, GREEN, YELLOW, OFF = (
    ("\033[1m", "\033[2m", "\033[31m", "\033[32m", "\033[33m", "\033[0m")
    if sys.stdout.isatty() else ("",) * 6)


def die(msg: str, code: int = 2) -> "never":          # noqa: F821
    print(f"{RED}symoneural-restore: {msg}{OFF}", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(code)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- manifests
REQUIRED = ["COMPONENTS.tsv", "APPLICATIONS.tsv", "SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv",
            "BUILD-RECIPES.tsv", "ARTIFACTS.tsv", "SERVICES.tsv", "DEPENDENCIES.tsv",
            "PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv", "RESTORE-ORDER.tsv", "SMOKES.tsv"]


def load(name: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Read one manifest. A missing manifest is fatal, never an empty list.

    Returning [] for an absent file would make every downstream check pass: no components
    means no components failed. That is the vacuous-success failure this whole control
    plane is built to avoid, so it is refused at the point of reading.
    """
    p = MANIFESTS / name
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"required manifest {name} is missing from {MANIFESTS}.\n"
            f"  Regenerate with: python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py\n"
            f"  Refusing to continue: an absent manifest would make every check below "
            f"pass for the wrong reason.")
    lines = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    if len(lines) < 2:
        die(f"manifest {name} has a header and no rows.")
    header = lines[0].split("\t")
    rows = []
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines[1:], start=2):
        cells = ln.split("\t")
        if len(cells) != len(header):
            die(f"{name}:{i} has {len(cells)} cells, header has {len(header)}.")
        rows.append(dict(zip(header, cells)))
    return rows


def release() -> dict:
    if not RELEASE.is_file():
        die(f"restore/RELEASE.json is missing. Regenerate the manifests first.")
    return json.loads(RELEASE.read_text())


def pick(rows: list[dict], key: str, value: str, what: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Select by id, or `all`. An unknown id is an ERROR -- never an empty selection."""
    if value == "all":
        return rows
    got = [r for r in rows if r.get(key) == value]
    if not got:
        known = ", ".join(sorted(r[key] for r in rows)[:40])
        die(f"unknown {what} '{value}'.\n  Known ids: {known}")
    return got


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def show_command(cmd: str, would: bool, root: bool = False) -> None:
    tag = f"{YELLOW}[would run]{OFF}" if would else f"{GREEN}[run]{OFF}"
    pre = f"{RED}(needs root){OFF} " if root else ""
    print(f"    {tag} {pre}{cmd}")


def run_shell(cmd: str, cwd: pathlib.Path | None = None, timeout: int = 7200) -> int:
    p = subprocess.run(["bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c", cmd], cwd=cwd or ROOT)
    return p.returncode


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- commands
def cmd_inventory(a) -> int:
    comps, apps = load("COMPONENTS.tsv"), load("APPLICATIONS.tsv")
    rel = release()
    print(f"{BOLD}SyMoNeuRaL release {rel['release_id']}{OFF}  "
          f"head {rel['repository_head'][:12]}  branch {rel['branch']}")
    print(f"\n{BOLD}Components ({len(comps)}){OFF}")
    for c in comps:
        colour = GREEN if c["PRODUCTION_STATUS"] == "PRODUCTION" else DIM
        print(f"  {colour}{c['COMPONENT_ID']:<28}{OFF} {c['PRODUCTION_STATUS']:<24} "
              f"{c['FIRST_PARTY_STATUS']:<34} {c['SOURCE_ROOT_PRESENT']}")
        if c["BLOCKER"] != "-" and a.verbose:
            print(f"      {DIM}{c['BLOCKER'][:150]}{OFF}")
    print(f"\n{BOLD}Applications ({len(apps)}){OFF}")
    for x in apps:
        colour = GREEN if x["PRODUCTION_STATUS"] == "PRODUCTION" else DIM
        parent = f"  (under {x['PARENT_APPLICATION_ID']})" \
            if x["PARENT_APPLICATION_ID"] != "-" else ""
        print(f"  {colour}{x['APPLICATION_ID']:<14}{OFF} {x['ROUTE']:<24} "
              f"-> {x['PRIMARY_RUNTIME_COMPONENT']:<20} {x['PRODUCTION_STATUS']}{parent}")
    return 0


def cmd_verify(a) -> int:
    """Internal consistency. This does NOT prove the system works -- `smoke` does that."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    notes: list[str] = []

    for name in REQUIRED:
        if not (MANIFESTS / name).is_file():
            problems.append(f"manifest missing: {name}")
    if problems:
        for p in problems:
            print(f"  {RED}FAIL{OFF} {p}")
        return 1

    comps = load("COMPONENTS.tsv")
    apps = load("APPLICATIONS.tsv")
    recipes = load("BUILD-RECIPES.tsv")
    smokes = load("SMOKES.tsv")
    states = load("PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv")
    order = load("RESTORE-ORDER.tsv")
    closure = load("SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv")

    cids = {c["COMPONENT_ID"] for c in comps}
    aids = {x["APPLICATION_ID"] for x in apps}
    sids = {s["SMOKE_ID"] for s in smokes}
    stids = {s["STATE_ID"] for s in states}

    # ---- referential integrity: every join must resolve
    for x in apps:
        if x["PRIMARY_RUNTIME_COMPONENT"] not in cids:
            problems.append(f"{x['APPLICATION_ID']}: runtime component "
                            f"'{x['PRIMARY_RUNTIME_COMPONENT']}' is not a component")
        if x["RESTORE_SMOKE_ID"] not in ("-",) and x["RESTORE_SMOKE_ID"] not in sids:
            problems.append(f"{x['APPLICATION_ID']}: smoke "
                            f"'{x['RESTORE_SMOKE_ID']}' does not exist")
        if x["PARENT_APPLICATION_ID"] not in ("-",) and \
                x["PARENT_APPLICATION_ID"] not in aids:
            problems.append(f"{x['APPLICATION_ID']}: parent "
                            f"'{x['PARENT_APPLICATION_ID']}' is not an application")
        for st in (s.strip() for s in x["PERSISTENT_STATE_IDS"].split(",")):
            if st and st != "-" and st not in stids:
                problems.append(f"{x['APPLICATION_ID']}: state '{st}' is not in "
                                f"PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv")
    for s in smokes:
        if s["APPLICATION_ID"] not in aids:
            problems.append(f"smoke {s['SMOKE_ID']}: application "
                            f"'{s['APPLICATION_ID']}' does not exist")
    for r in recipes:
        if r["COMPONENT_ID"] not in cids:
            problems.append(f"recipe for unknown component {r['COMPONENT_ID']}")
    if {r["COMPONENT_ID"] for r in recipes} != cids:
        missing = cids - {r["COMPONENT_ID"] for r in recipes}
        problems.append(f"components with no build recipe: {sorted(missing)}")

    # ---- restore order must be a DAG with satisfied prerequisites
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for st in sorted(order, key=lambda r: int(r["ORDER"])):
        for req in (x.strip() for x in st["REQUIRES"].split(",")):
            if req and req != "-" and req not in seen:
                problems.append(f"restore step {st['STEP_ID']} requires '{req}', which "
                                f"does not come earlier")
        seen.add(st["STEP_ID"])

    # ---- every PRODUCTION application must have a real smoke
    for x in apps:
        if x["PRODUCTION_STATUS"] == "PRODUCTION" and x["RESTORE_SMOKE_ID"] == "-":
            problems.append(f"{x['APPLICATION_ID']} is PRODUCTION with no restore smoke")

    # ---- every PRODUCTION component must be buildable and testable
    for c in comps:
        if c["PRODUCTION_STATUS"] != "PRODUCTION":
            continue
        rec = next(r for r in recipes if r["COMPONENT_ID"] == c["COMPONENT_ID"])
        if rec["BUILD_COMMAND"] == "-":
            problems.append(f"{c['COMPONENT_ID']} is PRODUCTION with no build command")
        if rec["TEST_COMMAND"] == "-":
            problems.append(f"{c['COMPONENT_ID']} is PRODUCTION with no test command")
        cl = next(r for r in closure if r["COMPONENT_ID"] == c["COMPONENT_ID"])
        if not cl["BUILDABLE_FROM_TRACKED_SOURCE"].startswith("YES"):
            problems.append(f"{c['COMPONENT_ID']} is PRODUCTION and not buildable: "
                            f"{cl['BUILDABLE_FROM_TRACKED_SOURCE']}")
        if cl["UNTRACKED_SOURCE_COUNT"].isdigit() and int(cl["UNTRACKED_SOURCE_COUNT"]):
            problems.append(f"{c['COMPONENT_ID']} has "
                            f"{cl['UNTRACKED_SOURCE_COUNT']} untracked source files")

    # ---- anti-vacuity: a verifier that checked nothing must not report success
    checks = len(apps) + len(smokes) + len(recipes) + len(order) + len(comps)
    if checks < 50:
        problems.append(f"only {checks} rows were examined; the manifests look truncated "
                        f"and a PASS here would mean nothing")

    if a.release_check:
        rel = release()
        head = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
        if head and head != rel["repository_head"]:
            notes.append(f"working tree is at {head[:12]}, RELEASE.json records "
                         f"{rel['repository_head'][:12]} -- regenerate the manifests")

    for n in notes:
        print(f"  {YELLOW}NOTE{OFF} {n}")
    if problems:
        for p in problems:
            print(f"  {RED}FAIL{OFF} {p}")
        print(f"\n{RED}RESTORE_VERIFY=FAIL{OFF}  ({len(problems)} problem(s), "
              f"{checks} rows examined)")
        return 1
    print(f"  {GREEN}OK{OFF} referential integrity across "
          f"{len(comps)} components, {len(apps)} applications, {len(smokes)} smokes")
    print(f"  {GREEN}OK{OFF} restore order is acyclic with satisfied prerequisites "
          f"({len(order)} steps)")
    print(f"  {GREEN}OK{OFF} every production component has a build and a test command")
    print(f"  {GREEN}OK{OFF} every production application has a restore smoke")
    print(f"\n{GREEN}RESTORE_VERIFY=PASS{OFF}  ({checks} rows examined)")
    return 0


def cmd_dependencies(a) -> int:
    deps = load("DEPENDENCIES.tsv")
    host = [d for d in deps if d["CLASS"] in
            ("TOOLCHAIN", "BUILD_TOOL", "PLATFORM_RUNTIME", "RUNTIME")]
    if a.instructions:
        print(f"{BOLD}Host packages{OFF}")
        pkgs = sorted({d["PACKAGE_NAME"] for d in host
                       if d["PACKAGE_MANAGER"] == "apt" and d["PACKAGE_NAME"] != "-"
                       and "(" not in d["PACKAGE_NAME"]})
        print(f"    sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y {' '.join(pkgs)}")
        print(f"\n{BOLD}NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit{OFF}")
        for d in host:
            if "NVIDIA" in d["UPSTREAM"] or "NVIDIA" in d["PACKAGE_NAME"]:
                print(f"    {d['NAME']}: {d['REINSTALL_METHOD']}")
                print(f"      {DIM}last measured here: {d['VERSION']}{OFF}")
        print(f"\n{BOLD}Python environments{OFF}")
        for d in deps:
            if d["CLASS"] == "PYTHON_ENVIRONMENT":
                print(f"    {d['NAME']}: {d['REINSTALL_METHOD']}")
        print(f"    serving interpreter: pip install -r "
              f"restore/locks/serving-system.lock.txt")
        print(f"\n{BOLD}Engine upstreams{OFF}  (see THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv)")
        print(f"    tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh all")
        return 0

    missing, present = [], []
    for d in host:
        probe = d["NAME"].split()[0].lower()
        binmap = {"gnu": "gcc", "cmake": "cmake", "git": "git", "cpython": "python3",
                  "node.js": "node", "npm": "npm", "rsync": "rsync", "sqlite": "sqlite3",
                  "cuda": "nvcc", "ccache": "ccache", "ninja": "ninja", "nvidia": "nvidia-smi"}
        exe = binmap.get(probe, probe)
        if d["NAME"] == "GNU C++ compiler":
            exe = "g++"
        (present if shutil.which(exe) else missing).append((d, exe))

    for d, exe in present:
        print(f"  {GREEN}OK{OFF}      {d['NAME']:<24} {d['VERSION'][:60]}")
    for d, exe in missing:
        print(f"  {RED}MISSING{OFF} {d['NAME']:<24} (no '{exe}' on PATH)")
        print(f"          install: {d['REINSTALL_METHOD']}")
    print(f"\n{len(present)} present, {len(missing)} missing")
    return 1 if missing else 0


def _recipes_for(value: str) -> list[dict]:
    return pick(load("BUILD-RECIPES.tsv"), "COMPONENT_ID", value, "component")


def cmd_build(a) -> int:
    rows = _recipes_for(a.component)
    comps = {c["COMPONENT_ID"]: c for c in load("COMPONENTS.tsv")}
    rc = 0
    for r in rows:
        c = comps[r["COMPONENT_ID"]]
        if a.component == "all" and c["PRODUCTION_STATUS"] not in \
                ("PRODUCTION", "INFRASTRUCTURE"):
            print(f"  {DIM}skip {r['COMPONENT_ID']} ({c['PRODUCTION_STATUS']}){OFF}")
            continue
        if r["BUILD_COMMAND"] in ("-", "(interpreted -- no build step)"):
            print(f"  {DIM}{r['COMPONENT_ID']}: nothing to build "
                  f"({r['BUILD_COMMAND']}){OFF}")
            continue
        print(f"\n{BOLD}{r['COMPONENT_ID']}{OFF}  [{r['BUILD_SYSTEM']}] "
              f"{r['TARGET_ARCH']}")
        if r["PREP_COMMAND"] != "-":
            show_command(r["PREP_COMMAND"], not a.apply)
        show_command(r["BUILD_COMMAND"], not a.apply)
        if a.apply:
            if r["PREP_COMMAND"] != "-" and run_shell(r["PREP_COMMAND"]):
                print(f"  {RED}prep failed{OFF}"); rc = 1; continue
            if run_shell(r["BUILD_COMMAND"]):
                print(f"  {RED}build failed{OFF}"); rc = 1; continue
            out = ROOT / r["OUTPUT_ARTIFACT"] if r["OUTPUT_ARTIFACT"] != "-" else None
            if out and not out.exists():
                print(f"  {RED}build reported success but {r['OUTPUT_ARTIFACT']} "
                      f"is not there{OFF}")
                rc = 1
            else:
                print(f"  {GREEN}built{OFF} {r['OUTPUT_ARTIFACT']}")
    if not a.apply:
        print(f"\n{YELLOW}Nothing was built. Re-run with --apply.{OFF}")
    return rc


def cmd_test(a) -> int:
    rows = _recipes_for(a.component)
    rc = 0
    for r in rows:
        if r["TEST_COMMAND"] == "-":
            print(f"  {DIM}{r['COMPONENT_ID']}: no test command{OFF}")
            continue
        print(f"\n{BOLD}{r['COMPONENT_ID']}{OFF}")
        show_command(r["TEST_COMMAND"], not a.apply)
        if a.apply and run_shell(r["TEST_COMMAND"]):
            print(f"  {RED}tests failed{OFF}")
            rc = 1
    if not a.apply:
        print(f"\n{YELLOW}Nothing was run. Re-run with --apply.{OFF}")
    return rc


def cmd_install(a) -> int:
    rows = _recipes_for(a.component)
    for r in rows:
        if r["INSTALL_COMMAND"] in ("-",) or r["INSTALL_COMMAND"].startswith("("):
            print(f"  {DIM}{r['COMPONENT_ID']}: {r['INSTALL_COMMAND']}{OFF}")
            continue
        needs_root = "sudo" in r["INSTALL_COMMAND"]
        print(f"\n{BOLD}{r['COMPONENT_ID']}{OFF} -> {r['INSTALL_PATH']}")
        show_command(r["INSTALL_COMMAND"], not a.apply, root=needs_root)
        if a.apply:
            if needs_root:
                # Deliberate: this tool does not invoke sudo. A restore program that
                # escalates on its own authority is one an operator cannot audit before
                # running, and these commands write systemd units.
                print(f"  {YELLOW}not run -- copy the command above and run it "
                      f"yourself.{OFF}")
            elif run_shell(r["INSTALL_COMMAND"]):
                print(f"  {RED}install failed{OFF}")
    if not a.apply:
        print(f"\n{YELLOW}Nothing was installed. Re-run with --apply.{OFF}")
    return 0


def cmd_restore_state(a) -> int:
    states = load("PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv")
    rel = release()
    base = ROOT / ".private" / "application-state" / rel["release_id"]
    print(f"{BOLD}Persistent state{OFF}  source: {base.relative_to(ROOT)}\n")
    missing = 0
    for s in states:
        tag = f"{RED}REQUIRED{OFF}" if s["REQUIRED_FOR_RESTORE"].startswith("YES") \
            else f"{DIM}optional{OFF}"
        print(f"  {s['STATE_ID']:<20} {tag}  {s['TYPE']}")
        if s["CONTAINS_SECRETS"].startswith("YES"):
            # Named, never printed. Knowing WHICH file holds secrets is what a restorer
            # needs; the contents are exactly what must not appear in a terminal.
            print(f"      {YELLOW}contains secrets -- restore with mode 0600, "
                  f"never echo its contents{OFF}")
        src = base / s["STATE_ID"]
        if s["BACKUP_PATH"].startswith("carried") or "CARRIED" in s["CONSISTENCY_METHOD"]:
            print(f"      {DIM}carried in the repository tree; nothing to copy{OFF}")
            continue
        if not src.exists():
            print(f"      {RED}backup absent: {src.relative_to(ROOT)}{OFF}")
            missing += 1
            continue
        show_command(s["RESTORE_COMMAND"].replace("<backup>", str(src)), not a.apply)
        print(f"      verify: {s['VALIDATION_COMMAND']}")
    if missing:
        print(f"\n{RED}{missing} required backup(s) missing.{OFF}")
        return 1
    if not a.apply:
        print(f"\n{YELLOW}Dry run. Re-run with --apply to restore.{OFF}")
    return 0


def cmd_services(a) -> int:
    svcs = load("SERVICES.tsv")
    rc = 0
    for s in svcs:
        print(f"\n{BOLD}{s['SERVICE_ID']}{OFF}  {s['SOURCE_UNIT']} -> "
              f"{s['INSTALLED_UNIT']}")
        print(f"    designed: {s['ENABLEMENT_DESIGNED']}")
        print(f"    measured: enabled={s['ENABLEMENT_MEASURED']} "
              f"active={s['ACTIVE_MEASURED']}")
        print(f"    installed vs source: {s['INSTALLED_MATCHES_SOURCE']}")
        if s["INSTALLED_MATCHES_SOURCE"].startswith("DIVERGED"):
            rc = 1
        if s["ENV_FILES"] != "-":
            print(f"    {DIM}env: {s['ENV_FILES']}{OFF}")
        if a.install:
            show_command(s["INSTALL_COMMAND"], not a.apply, root=True)
            print(f"    healthcheck: {s['HEALTHCHECK']}")
    if a.install and not a.apply:
        print(f"\n{YELLOW}Dry run. These write systemd units and need root; run them "
              f"yourself.{OFF}")
    return rc


def cmd_smoke(a) -> int:
    smokes = pick(load("SMOKES.tsv"), "APPLICATION_ID", a.application, "application") \
        if a.application != "all" else load("SMOKES.tsv")
    rc = 0
    for s in smokes:
        print(f"\n{BOLD}{s['SMOKE_ID']}{OFF}  ({s['APPLICATION_ID']})")
        print(f"    expects: {s['EXPECTED_RESULT']}")
        print(f"    network: {s['NETWORK_SCOPE']}   mutating: {s['MUTATING']}")
        if s["MUTATING"] == "YES" and not a.allow_mutating and a.apply:
            print(f"    {YELLOW}skipped -- mutating; pass --allow-mutating{OFF}")
            continue
        show_command(s["COMMAND"], not a.apply)
        if a.apply:
            if run_shell(s["COMMAND"], timeout=900):
                print(f"    {RED}FAIL{OFF}")
                rc = 1
            else:
                print(f"    {GREEN}PASS{OFF}")
    if not a.apply:
        print(f"\n{YELLOW}Nothing was run. Re-run with --apply.{OFF}")
    return rc


def cmd_status(a) -> int:
    rel = release()
    comps = load("COMPONENTS.tsv")
    apps = load("APPLICATIONS.tsv")
    svcs = load("SERVICES.tsv")
    closure = load("SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv")
    prod = [c for c in comps if c["PRODUCTION_STATUS"] == "PRODUCTION"]
    fails = [c for c in closure if c["STATUS"].startswith("FAIL")]

    print(f"{BOLD}RELEASE_ID{OFF}                     {rel['release_id']}")
    print(f"{BOLD}REPOSITORY_HEAD{OFF}                {rel['repository_head']}")
    print(f"{BOLD}BRANCH{OFF}                         {rel['branch']}")
    print(f"{BOLD}COMPONENTS_TOTAL{OFF}               {len(comps)}")
    print(f"{BOLD}PRODUCTION_COMPONENTS{OFF}          {len(prod)}")
    print(f"{BOLD}APPLICATIONS_TOTAL{OFF}             {len(apps)}")
    print(f"{BOLD}PRODUCTION_APPLICATIONS{OFF}        "
          f"{sum(1 for x in apps if x['PRODUCTION_STATUS'] == 'PRODUCTION')}")
    print(f"{BOLD}SOURCE_CLOSURE{OFF}                 "
          f"{'FAIL' if fails else 'PASS'}"
          + (f"  ({len(fails)} failing)" if fails else ""))
    diverged = [s for s in svcs if s["INSTALLED_MATCHES_SOURCE"].startswith("DIVERGED")]
    print(f"{BOLD}SERVICES_INSTALLED_STALE{OFF}       {len(diverged)}"
          + (f"  ({', '.join(s['SERVICE_ID'] for s in diverged)})" if diverged else ""))
    bundle = ROOT / rel["git_bundle_path"]
    print(f"{BOLD}GIT_BUNDLE{OFF}                     "
          f"{'present' if bundle.is_file() else 'ABSENT'}"
          + (f"  {bundle.stat().st_size} bytes" if bundle.is_file() else ""))
    for key in ("source_bundle_root", "runtime_artifact_root", "persistent_state_root",
                "host_snapshot_root", "claude_backup_root"):
        p = ROOT / rel[key]
        n = len(list(p.rglob("*"))) if p.is_dir() else 0
        print(f"{BOLD}{key.upper():<30}{OFF} "
              f"{'present' if p.is_dir() else 'ABSENT'}"
              + (f"  {n} entries" if p.is_dir() else ""))
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- cli
def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="symoneural-restore",
        description="Rebuild SyMoNeuRaL from source on a fresh machine.")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("inventory", help="what exists and what class it is")
    p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_inventory)

    p = sub.add_parser("verify", help="internal consistency of the restore plan")
    p.add_argument("--release", dest="release_check", action="store_true",
                   help="also check the working tree matches RELEASE.json")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_verify)

    p = sub.add_parser("dependencies", help="what this host is missing")
    g = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    g.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    g.add_argument("--instructions", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_dependencies)

    for name, fn, helptext in (("build", cmd_build, "build a component"),
                               ("test", cmd_test, "run a component's tests"),
                               ("install", cmd_install, "install a component")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=helptext)
        p.add_argument("component")
        p.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true",
                       help="actually run it (default is to print what would run)")
        p.set_defaults(fn=fn)

    p = sub.add_parser("restore-state", help="restore persistent application state")
    g = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    g.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    g.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_restore_state)

    p = sub.add_parser("services", help="check or install the systemd units")
    g = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    g.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    g.add_argument("--install", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_services)

    p = sub.add_parser("smoke", help="exercise an application's real path")
    p.add_argument("application")
    p.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--allow-mutating", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_smoke)

    p = sub.add_parser("status", help="the release gate figures")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_status)

    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    return a.fn(a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
