#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
#
# restore-upstream.sh -- reacquire the pinned engine upstreams on a machine that does not
# have `external/`.
#
# THIS IS THE SCRIPT THAT MAKES THE BACKUP SMALL. `tools/sh/fork_engines.sh` builds the five
# runtimes out of `external/referencestochatgpt/`, which is 149 GB of third-party source
# that the owner does not want to carry through a machine reset -- and should not have to,
# because every one of those trees is a clean clone of a public remote at a known revision.
# So the backup carries a URL and forty hex characters per engine, and this fetches the
# rest.
#
# The claim "external/ may be omitted" is only true while that is true. It is checked, not
# assumed: `--check` re-reads the pin out of THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv and compares
# it against whatever is on disk, and a mismatch is an error rather than a warning.
#
#     tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh --check          # what is here, what is missing
#     tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh all              # fetch everything a build needs
#     tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh llama.cpp        # fetch one
#
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not fetch the GPL-3.0 upstreams unless asked for by name.
# symoneural-miner (kawpowminer) and symoneural-ui (ComfyUI) are DISABLED for this reset --
# their licences mean they cannot become first-party, and the reset spec's answer is to
# disable the feature rather than carry the implementation. `all` therefore fetches the
# three MIT engines. Asking for a copyleft one by name works and prints why it is off.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
MANIFEST="$ROOT/THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv"
DEST_ROOT="${SYMONEURAL_UPSTREAM_ROOT:-$ROOT/external/referencestochatgpt}"

[ -f "$MANIFEST" ] || {
    echo "restore-upstream: $MANIFEST is missing." >&2
    echo "  Regenerate it: python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py" >&2
    echo "  Refusing to guess an upstream revision." >&2
    exit 2
}

# Column indices are looked up by NAME from the header rather than hard-coded. A manifest
# that grows a column would otherwise silently shift every field by one and this script
# would start checking out whatever now sits in position 9.
col() { awk -F'\t' -v want="$1" 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i==want){print i; exit}}' "$MANIFEST"; }
C_NAME=$(col NAME); C_UP=$(col UPSTREAM_PROJECT); C_REV=$(col PINNED_REVISION)
C_LIC=$(col LICENSE); C_REQ=$(col REQUIRED); C_PATCH=$(col LOCAL_PATCH)
for v in C_NAME C_UP C_REV C_LIC C_REQ C_PATCH; do
    [ -n "${!v}" ] || { echo "restore-upstream: manifest is missing a required column ($v)" >&2; exit 2; }
done

rows() { awk -F'\t' 'NR>1' "$MANIFEST"; }

field() { echo "$1" | cut -f"$2"; }

is_copyleft() { case "$1" in *GPL*) return 0;; *) return 1;; esac; }

do_check() {
    local rc=0 row name up rev lic present actual
    printf '%-24s %-10s %-14s %s\n' NAME LICENCE STATE DETAIL
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        name=$(field "$row" "$C_NAME"); up=$(field "$row" "$C_UP")
        rev=$(field "$row" "$C_REV");  lic=$(field "$row" "$C_LIC")
        local dir="$DEST_ROOT/$name"
        if [ ! -d "$dir/.git" ]; then
            printf '%-24s %-10s %-14s %s\n' "$name" "$lic" "ABSENT" "fetch: $up @ ${rev:0:12}"
            # Absent is not a failure for a disabled component -- it is the intended state.
            is_copyleft "$lic" || rc=1
            continue
        fi
        actual=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        if [ "$actual" = "$rev" ]; then
            local dirty; dirty=$(git -C "$dir" status --porcelain | wc -l)
            if [ "$dirty" -gt 0 ]; then
                printf '%-24s %-10s %-14s %s\n' "$name" "$lic" "PIN_OK" "$dirty uncommitted change(s) -- see LOCAL_PATCH"
            else
                printf '%-24s %-10s %-14s %s\n' "$name" "$lic" "PIN_OK" "${rev:0:12}"
            fi
        else
            printf '%-24s %-10s %-14s %s\n' "$name" "$lic" "PIN_MISMATCH" "want ${rev:0:12} have ${actual:0:12}"
            rc=1
        fi
    done < <(rows)
    return $rc
}

fetch_one() {
    local row="$1" name up rev lic patch dir
    name=$(field "$row" "$C_NAME"); up=$(field "$row" "$C_UP")
    rev=$(field "$row" "$C_REV");   lic=$(field "$row" "$C_LIC")
    patch=$(field "$row" "$C_PATCH")
    dir="$DEST_ROOT/$name"

    echo
    echo "=== $name  ($lic)"
    echo "    upstream: $up"
    echo "    revision: $rev"

    if [ -d "$dir/.git" ]; then
        local actual; actual=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD)
        if [ "$actual" = "$rev" ]; then
            echo "    already at the pinned revision -- nothing to do"
            return 0
        fi
        echo "    present at ${actual:0:12}; fetching the pinned revision"
        git -C "$dir" fetch --quiet origin "$rev" || git -C "$dir" fetch --quiet origin
        git -C "$dir" checkout --quiet --detach "$rev"
    else
        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
        # Full clone, not --depth 1: submodules are pinned by commit and a shallow clone
        # cannot always resolve them. kawpowminer has two (cmake/cable, Hunter).
        echo "    cloning"
        git clone --quiet "$up" "$dir"
        git -C "$dir" checkout --quiet --detach "$rev"
    fi

    if [ -f "$dir/.gitmodules" ]; then
        echo "    initialising submodules"
        git -C "$dir" submodule update --init --recursive --quiet
    fi

    # VERIFY. The whole point of a pin is that it is checkable, so check it rather than
    # trusting that checkout did what it was told.
    local got; got=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD)
    if [ "$got" != "$rev" ]; then
        echo "    ERROR: after checkout HEAD is $got, expected $rev" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    echo "    verified at $rev"

    if [ "$patch" != "-" ] && [ -n "$patch" ]; then
        if [ -f "$ROOT/$patch" ]; then
            echo "    applying preserved local patch: $patch"
            echo "      (a revision pin restores the upstream; it cannot restore edits"
            echo "       that were never committed anywhere)"
            git -C "$dir" apply --check "$ROOT/$patch" \
                && git -C "$dir" apply "$ROOT/$patch" \
                && echo "    patch applied"
        else
            echo "    WARNING: LOCAL_PATCH names $patch and it is not present." >&2
            echo "             This tree had uncommitted local changes. Without the patch" >&2
            echo "             the build may fail or silently differ from what ran here." >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

main() {
    local want="${1:-}"
    case "$want" in
        --check) do_check; exit $?;;
        "" | -h | --help)
            sed -n '5,30p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
            exit 0;;
    esac

    local matched=0 row name lic req
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        name=$(field "$row" "$C_NAME"); lic=$(field "$row" "$C_LIC")
        req=$(field "$row" "$C_REQ")
        if [ "$want" = "all" ]; then
            if is_copyleft "$lic"; then
                echo
                echo "=== $name  ($lic)  SKIPPED"
                echo "    Component is DISABLED for this reset. A copyleft upstream cannot"
                echo "    be made first-party, and the reset's rule is to disable the"
                echo "    feature rather than carry the implementation. Ask for it by name"
                echo "    if you deliberately want it back."
                matched=1
                continue
            fi
        elif [ "$want" != "$name" ]; then
            continue
        fi
        fetch_one "$row"
        matched=1
    done < <(rows)

    if [ "$matched" -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "restore-upstream: no upstream named '$want' in the manifest." >&2
        echo "known:" >&2
        rows | cut -f"$C_NAME" | sed 's/^/  /' >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    echo
    echo "Now build:  tools/sh/fork_engines.sh <llm|diffuse|listen>"
}

main "$@"

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
"""Production code must not read source out of `external/`. Enforced, so it stays true.

The owner is wiping this machine and does not want to carry 149 GB of third-party source
through the reset. That is only safe if nothing the product runs depends on those trees
being present -- and the honest situation is more interesting than "nothing does".

## The real dependency, and why it is allowed

`tools/sh/fork_engines.sh` reads `external/referencestochatgpt/{llama.cpp,
stable-diffusion.cpp,whisper.cpp}` and builds the three engines that serve chat, image and
ASR. That is a genuine build-time dependency on `external/`, it is load-bearing, and
pretending otherwise to make a gate go green would be a lie the next restore would discover.

What makes it omittable is that each of those trees is a clean `git clone` of a public
remote at a pinned revision -- measured, and re-checked by `tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh
--check`. So the dependency is on an UPSTREAM, which is reacquirable, not on a local
directory, which is not. `THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv` carries the pins and
`restore-upstream.sh` fetches them.

This test therefore draws the line at a different place than a naive `grep external/`
would:

**Counts as a violation:** first-party RUNTIME code -- the API, the apps, the site
generators, the CLIs -- resolving a path under `external/`, `vendor clones`, an old build
snapshot, or a retired workspace. That is a runtime that cannot start without a tree the
backup does not carry.

**Does not count:**

  * `tools/sh/fork_engines.sh` and `tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh`. These are BUILD AUTHORITY and
    ACQUISITION tooling. Their whole job is to consume an upstream; a build script that
    names its input is not a hidden dependency, it is a recipe. Both are covered by the
    manifest, which records the pin that makes the input reacquirable.
  * Prose, docstrings and documentation. A comment explaining why `external/` is
    reference-only is inert. The last blanket path-rewrite in this repository silently
    edited an assertion inside a regex, so prose is left alone deliberately.
  * The manifests themselves, which exist to name these paths.

## The detector must catch split-form path construction

`ROOT / "external" / "referencestochatgpt"` is the same dependency as
`ROOT / "external/referencestochatgpt"` and a substring search for `external/` finds only
the second. This is not hypothetical: nine files including the live `api.py` once spelled
`ROOT / "engines" / "symoneural-llm"` in split form, a string sweep missed every one of
them, and the shims that were assumed dead turned out to be load-bearing. So the pattern
below matches the split form too, and `test_the_detector_catches_split_form_construction`
proves it does.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import unittest


def _find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise RuntimeError(f"no repo root above {start}")


ROOT = _find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve())

#: Directories that will not exist after the reset. A runtime that resolves a path into one
#: of these cannot start on a restored machine.
RETIRED = (
    "external",
    "referencestochatgpt",
    "SyMoNeuRaL-Workspace",
    "SyMoNeuRaL-Projects",
    "symoneural-cutover-rollback",
)

#: Build authority and acquisition tooling, whose input IS an upstream. Each is covered by
#: THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv, which records the pin that makes the input
#: reacquirable. Short on purpose: a long exempt list is how a guard stops guarding.
EXEMPT_PREFIXES = (
    "tools/sh/fork_engines.sh",                 # the build authority for the five forks
    "tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh",             # the acquisition tool for their upstreams
    "restore/lib/registry.py",               # records where the upstreams live
    "restore/lib/deps.py",                   # verifies the pins against those trees
    "backend/apps/test_no_external_source_dependency.py",
    "docs/",                                 # documentation and historical record
    "THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv",
    "FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv",
    "restore/manifests/",
)

#: Extensions that are executed. A `.md` naming a path is prose.
CODE_SUFFIXES = (".py", ".sh", ".bash", ".js", ".ts", ".mjs", ".go", ".rs", ".service",
                 ".c", ".cpp", ".h", ".hpp", ".cmake", ".mk", ".yaml", ".yml", ".json")


def _pattern(name: str) -> re.Pattern:
    """A path being RESOLVED, in either spelling.

    Three shapes:
      "external/...."            a quoted path fragment
      / "external" /             pathlib split form -- the one a substring grep misses
      $ROOT/external/            shell interpolation
    """
    n = re.escape(name)
    return re.compile(
        rf'''(["'`]{n}/)'''                     # "external/..."
        rf'''|(/\s*["']{n}["']\s*/)'''          # / "external" /
        rf'''|(\$\{{?\w+\}}?/{n}/)'''           # $ROOT/external/
        rf'''|(^\s*{n}/)''',                    # a bare leading path in a config
        re.MULTILINE)


PATTERNS = {name: _pattern(name) for name in RETIRED}


def _tracked_code_files() -> list[str]:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "ls-files", "-z"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    files = [f for f in out.split("\0") if f]
    return [f for f in files
            if f.endswith(CODE_SUFFIXES)
            and not f.startswith(EXEMPT_PREFIXES)]


def _violations() -> list[tuple[str, str, int, str]]:
    found = []
    for rel in _tracked_code_files():
        p = ROOT / rel
        try:
            text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except OSError:
            continue
        for name, pat in PATTERNS.items():
            for m in pat.finditer(text):
                line_no = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
                line = text.splitlines()[line_no - 1].strip()
                found.append((rel, name, line_no, line[:160]))
    return found


class ExternalSourceDependency(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_active_external_source_dependencies_is_zero(self):
        """ACTIVE_EXTERNAL_SOURCE_DEPENDENCIES=0 -- the reset gate."""
        v = _violations()
        if v:
            lines = "\n".join(f"  {rel}:{n}  [{name}]  {line}" for rel, name, n, line in v)
            self.fail(
                f"{len(v)} production reference(s) to a tree that will not survive the "
                f"reset:\n{lines}\n\n"
                "Either replace the reference with first-party code or a reinstallable "
                "package dependency, or -- if it is genuinely build authority consuming a "
                "pinned upstream -- add it to EXEMPT_PREFIXES with its reason and record "
                "the pin in THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv.")

    def test_the_detector_catches_split_form_construction(self):
        """The bug that got past a string sweep must not get past this.

        `ROOT / "external" / "contrib"` is the same dependency as `ROOT / "external/contrib"`.
        Nine files once spelled an engine path in split form, a substring search found none
        of them, and the shims everyone believed were dead were load-bearing.
        """
        samples = [
            'src = ROOT / "external" / "contrib" / "llama.cpp"',
            "path = root / 'external' / 'referencestochatgpt'",
            'SRC = "external/referencestochatgpt/llama.cpp"',
            'rsync -a "$ROOT/external/contrib/" "$DST/"',
            'WORKSPACE = HOME / "SyMoNeuRaL-Workspace" / "build"',
        ]
        for s in samples:
            with self.subTest(sample=s):
                self.assertTrue(
                    any(p.search(s) for p in PATTERNS.values()),
                    f"the detector did not recognise a real dependency: {s}")

    def test_prose_is_not_treated_as_a_dependency(self):
        """A docstring naming external/ is inert and must not fail the build."""
        samples = [
            "# external/ is a reference-only tree; nothing in it may be linked.",
            "See the external directory for historical context.",
            "the engines were being run straight out of external, which is wrong",
        ]
        for s in samples:
            with self.subTest(sample=s):
                self.assertFalse(
                    any(p.search(s) for p in PATTERNS.values()),
                    f"prose was treated as a dependency: {s}")

    def test_the_detector_actually_scanned_something(self):
        """Anti-vacuity. A scanner that reads nothing reports zero violations forever."""
        files = _tracked_code_files()
        self.assertGreater(
            len(files), 300,
            f"only {len(files)} tracked code files were scanned; the file list looks "
            f"broken, and a PASS above would mean the scan did not run rather than that "
            f"the repository is clean.")

    def test_every_exemption_is_a_real_path(self):
        """An exemption for a path that no longer exists silently widens the guard."""
        for pref in EXEMPT_PREFIXES:
            with self.subTest(exemption=pref):
                p = ROOT / pref
                self.assertTrue(
                    p.exists() or any(f.startswith(pref) for f in
                                      subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "ls-files"],
                                                     capture_output=True, text=True
                                                     ).stdout.split()),
                    f"EXEMPT_PREFIXES names '{pref}', which is not in the repository. "
                    f"A stale exemption exempts whatever moves into that path next.")

    def test_the_build_authority_dependency_is_recorded_not_hidden(self):
        """fork_engines.sh IS exempt, so its dependency must be recorded elsewhere.

        This is the check that stops the exemption from being a loophole: every upstream
        the build authority consumes has to appear in the rebuild manifest with a pinned
        revision, because the pin is the only reason omitting the tree is safe.
        """
        man = ROOT / "THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv"
        self.assertTrue(man.is_file(), "THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv is missing")
        rows = man.read_text().splitlines()
        header = rows[0].split("\t")
        rev_col = header.index("PINNED_REVISION")
        name_col = header.index("NAME")
        pins = {r.split("\t")[name_col]: r.split("\t")[rev_col] for r in rows[1:]}

        fork = (ROOT / "tools" / "fork_engines.sh").read_text()
        consumed = {n for n in ("llama.cpp", "stable-diffusion.cpp", "whisper.cpp",
                                "kawpowminer") if n in fork}
        self.assertTrue(consumed, "fork_engines.sh names no upstream -- has it moved?")
        for name in sorted(consumed):
            with self.subTest(upstream=name):
                self.assertIn(name, pins,
                              f"tools/sh/fork_engines.sh builds from '{name}' and it has no "
                              f"row in THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv. Without a pin, "
                              f"omitting external/ from the backup makes this engine "
                              f"unrebuildable.")
                self.assertRegex(pins[name], r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$",
                                 f"'{name}' has no full revision pin: {pins[name]!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
"""The restore plan must describe THIS repository, not the one it described last week.

`restore/manifests/` is what a future owner reads after reinstalling Linux, and it is the
only place several facts exist at all: which upstream revision an engine forks from, which
of seven Python environments a component runs in, which database cannot be copied with
`cp`, which unit is deliberately disabled. A manifest that has quietly drifted from the
repository is worse than no manifest, because it will be believed.

So the manifests are generated, and these tests assert the properties a generated artefact
has to keep having:

  * **Coverage.** Every runtime on disk has a registry row. A new engine folder must not be
    silently absent from the restore plan.
  * **Idempotence.** Generating twice produces the same bytes. Three separate generators in
    this repository have re-read their own output and accumulated a copy per run, which is
    why "run it twice and diff" is in the project's completion sequence.
  * **Referential integrity.** Every join resolves. A smoke pointing at an application that
    does not exist is a restore step nobody can run.
  * **Truthfulness against disk.** A recipe that names an output path is checked against the
    filesystem. This repository has recorded an engine as unbuilt because a probe looked in
    `build/bin` when the binary was in `build/kawpowminer` -- true of the path, false of the
    engine, and written three days after the build succeeded.
  * **Anti-vacuity.** A manifest that is empty satisfies every "nothing failed" assertion.
    Minimum row counts are asserted so a truncated generation fails loudly.

The tests do NOT run builds or start services. They check that the plan is internally
coherent and consistent with the disk. Whether the plan WORKS is what
`symoneural-restore smoke` answers, and only a real run can answer it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest


def _find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise RuntimeError(f"no repo root above {start}")


ROOT = _find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve())
MANIFESTS = ROOT / "restore" / "manifests"

REQUIRED = {
    "COMPONENTS.tsv": 15,
    "APPLICATIONS.tsv": 12,
    "SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv": 15,
    "BUILD-RECIPES.tsv": 15,
    "ARTIFACTS.tsv": 10,
    "SERVICES.tsv": 4,
    "DEPENDENCIES.tsv": 100,
    "PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv": 6,
    "RESTORE-ORDER.tsv": 10,
    "SMOKES.tsv": 12,
}


def read(name: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    p = MANIFESTS / name if not name.endswith("CLOSURE.tsv") or "/" in name else None
    p = MANIFESTS / name
    if not p.is_file():
        p = ROOT / name
    lines = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    header = lines[0].split("\t")
    return [dict(zip(header, ln.split("\t"))) for ln in lines[1:]]


class ManifestsExist(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_every_required_manifest_is_present_and_not_truncated(self):
        for name, minimum in REQUIRED.items():
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                p = MANIFESTS / name
                self.assertTrue(p.is_file(), f"{name} is missing from {MANIFESTS}")
                rows = read(name)
                self.assertGreaterEqual(
                    len(rows), minimum,
                    f"{name} has {len(rows)} rows, expected at least {minimum}. A "
                    f"truncated manifest passes every 'nothing failed' check for the "
                    f"wrong reason.")

    def test_root_level_manifests_exist(self):
        """The reset spec asks for these two at the repository root, not under restore/."""
        for name in ("FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv", "THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv"):
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                self.assertTrue((ROOT / name).is_file(), f"{name} is missing")

    def test_every_row_has_the_full_column_count(self):
        for name in REQUIRED:
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                lines = (MANIFESTS / name).read_text().splitlines()
                width = len(lines[0].split("\t"))
                for i, ln in enumerate(lines[1:], start=2):
                    self.assertEqual(
                        len(ln.split("\t")), width,
                        f"{name}:{i} has a different column count from the header; "
                        f"`cut -f` on this file would return the wrong field.")

    def test_no_cell_is_empty(self):
        """An empty cell is ambiguous with a parse error. `-` is the empty value."""
        for name in REQUIRED:
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                for i, row in enumerate(read(name), start=2):
                    for k, v in row.items():
                        self.assertNotEqual(
                            v, "", f"{name}:{i} column {k} is empty; use '-'")


class RegistryCoversDisk(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_every_runtime_on_disk_has_a_registry_row(self):
        """A new runtime folder must fail this, not be silently left out of the plan."""
        sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "restore"))
        from lib import registry as R
        known = R.component_ids()
        on_disk = sorted(p.name for p in ROOT.iterdir()
                         if p.is_dir() and p.name.startswith("symoneural-"))
        missing = [n for n in on_disk if n not in known]
        self.assertEqual(
            missing, [],
            f"these runtimes exist on disk and are absent from restore/lib/registry.py: "
            f"{missing}. A runtime missing from the registry is missing from the restore "
            f"plan.")

    def test_the_coverage_check_is_looking_at_something(self):
        """Anti-vacuity: if the glob found nothing the check above passes trivially."""
        on_disk = [p.name for p in ROOT.iterdir()
                   if p.is_dir() and p.name.startswith("symoneural-")]
        self.assertGreaterEqual(
            len(on_disk), 8,
            f"only {len(on_disk)} runtime folders were found; the discovery glob looks "
            f"broken and the coverage test above would pass without checking anything.")


class Idempotent(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_generating_twice_changes_nothing(self):
        """Three generators in this repository have accumulated a copy per run."""
        before = {name: (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes() for name in REQUIRED}
        r = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "build_restore_manifests.py")],
            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0,
                         f"the generator failed:\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr}")
        for name in REQUIRED:
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                self.assertEqual(
                    before[name], (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes(),
                    f"{name} changed on a second generation with no source change. "
                    f"Either a measurement is non-deterministic or the generator is "
                    f"re-reading its own output.")


class ReferentialIntegrity(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        self.comps = read("COMPONENTS.tsv")
        self.apps = read("APPLICATIONS.tsv")
        self.recipes = read("BUILD-RECIPES.tsv")
        self.smokes = read("SMOKES.tsv")
        self.states = read("PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv")
        self.closure = read("SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv")

    def test_component_ids_are_unique(self):
        ids = [c["COMPONENT_ID"] for c in self.comps]
        self.assertEqual(len(ids), len(set(ids)),
                         "duplicate COMPONENT_ID -- an alias became a second component")

    def test_every_application_names_a_real_component(self):
        cids = {c["COMPONENT_ID"] for c in self.comps}
        for a in self.apps:
            with self.subTest(app=a["APPLICATION_ID"]):
                self.assertIn(a["PRIMARY_RUNTIME_COMPONENT"], cids)

    def test_every_component_has_exactly_one_recipe(self):
        cids = [c["COMPONENT_ID"] for c in self.comps]
        rids = [r["COMPONENT_ID"] for r in self.recipes]
        self.assertEqual(sorted(cids), sorted(rids))

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
"""The restore plan must describe THIS repository, not the one it described last week.

`restore/manifests/` is what a future owner reads after reinstalling Linux, and it is the
only place several facts exist at all: which upstream revision an engine forks from, which
of seven Python environments a component runs in, which database cannot be copied with
`cp`, which unit is deliberately disabled. A manifest that has quietly drifted from the
repository is worse than no manifest, because it will be believed.

So the manifests are generated, and these tests assert the properties a generated artefact
has to keep having:

  * **Coverage.** Every runtime on disk has a registry row. A new engine folder must not be
    silently absent from the restore plan.
  * **Idempotence.** Generating twice produces the same bytes. Three separate generators in
    this repository have re-read their own output and accumulated a copy per run, which is
    why "run it twice and diff" is in the project's completion sequence.
  * **Referential integrity.** Every join resolves. A smoke pointing at an application that
    does not exist is a restore step nobody can run.
  * **Truthfulness against disk.** A recipe that names an output path is checked against the
    filesystem. This repository has recorded an engine as unbuilt because a probe looked in
    `build/bin` when the binary was in `build/kawpowminer` -- true of the path, false of the
    engine, and written three days after the build succeeded.
  * **Anti-vacuity.** A manifest that is empty satisfies every "nothing failed" assertion.
    Minimum row counts are asserted so a truncated generation fails loudly.

The tests do NOT run builds or start services. They check that the plan is internally
coherent and consistent with the disk. Whether the plan WORKS is what
`symoneural-restore smoke` answers, and only a real run can answer it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest


def _find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise RuntimeError(f"no repo root above {start}")


ROOT = _find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve())
MANIFESTS = ROOT / "restore" / "manifests"

REQUIRED = {
    "COMPONENTS.tsv": 15,
    "APPLICATIONS.tsv": 12,
    "SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv": 15,
    "BUILD-RECIPES.tsv": 15,
    "ARTIFACTS.tsv": 10,
    "SERVICES.tsv": 4,
    "DEPENDENCIES.tsv": 100,
    "PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv": 6,
    "RESTORE-ORDER.tsv": 10,
    "SMOKES.tsv": 12,
}


def read(name: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    p = MANIFESTS / name if not name.endswith("CLOSURE.tsv") or "/" in name else None
    p = MANIFESTS / name
    if not p.is_file():
        p = ROOT / name
    lines = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    header = lines[0].split("\t")
    return [dict(zip(header, ln.split("\t"))) for ln in lines[1:]]


class ManifestsExist(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_every_required_manifest_is_present_and_not_truncated(self):
        for name, minimum in REQUIRED.items():
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                p = MANIFESTS / name
                self.assertTrue(p.is_file(), f"{name} is missing from {MANIFESTS}")
                rows = read(name)
                self.assertGreaterEqual(
                    len(rows), minimum,
                    f"{name} has {len(rows)} rows, expected at least {minimum}. A "
                    f"truncated manifest passes every 'nothing failed' check for the "
                    f"wrong reason.")

    def test_root_level_manifests_exist(self):
        """The reset spec asks for these two at the repository root, not under restore/."""
        for name in ("FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv", "THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv"):
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                self.assertTrue((ROOT / name).is_file(), f"{name} is missing")

    def test_every_row_has_the_full_column_count(self):
        for name in REQUIRED:
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                lines = (MANIFESTS / name).read_text().splitlines()
                width = len(lines[0].split("\t"))
                for i, ln in enumerate(lines[1:], start=2):
                    self.assertEqual(
                        len(ln.split("\t")), width,
                        f"{name}:{i} has a different column count from the header; "
                        f"`cut -f` on this file would return the wrong field.")

    def test_no_cell_is_empty(self):
        """An empty cell is ambiguous with a parse error. `-` is the empty value."""
        for name in REQUIRED:
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                for i, row in enumerate(read(name), start=2):
                    for k, v in row.items():
                        self.assertNotEqual(
                            v, "", f"{name}:{i} column {k} is empty; use '-'")

        known = R.component_ids()
        on_disk = sorted(p.name for p in ROOT.iterdir()
                         if p.is_dir() and p.name.startswith("symoneural-"))
        missing = [n for n in on_disk if n not in known]
        self.assertEqual(
            missing, [],
            f"these runtimes exist on disk and are absent from restore/lib/registry.py: "
            f"{missing}. A runtime missing from the registry is missing from the restore "
            f"plan.")

        """Anti-vacuity: if the glob found nothing the check above passes trivially."""
        on_disk = [p.name for p in ROOT.iterdir()
                   if p.is_dir() and p.name.startswith("symoneural-")]
        self.assertGreaterEqual(
            len(on_disk), 8,
            f"only {len(on_disk)} runtime folders were found; the discovery glob looks "
            f"broken and the coverage test above would pass without checking anything.")


class Idempotent(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_generating_twice_changes_nothing(self):
        """Three generators in this repository have accumulated a copy per run."""
        before = {name: (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes() for name in REQUIRED}
        r = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "build_restore_manifests.py")],
            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0,
                         f"the generator failed:\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr}")
        for name in REQUIRED:
            with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                self.assertEqual(
                    before[name], (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes(),
                    f"{name} changed on a second generation with no source change. "
                    f"Either a measurement is non-deterministic or the generator is "
                    f"re-reading its own output.")

● Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
  restore: a control plane that can rebuild this project on a bare machine

  The owner is erasing this Linux install and restoring SyMoNeuRaL later. The thing
  standing in the way was not missing files -- it was that every step of standing this
  system up lived in a commit message or somebody's head: which upstream revision an
  engine forks from, which of seven Python environments a component runs in, which
  database cannot be copied with cp, which unit is deliberately disabled and which is
  merely stale. None of that survives a reinstall.

  So it is written down, generated from measurement, and there is one program that
  reads it.

  WHAT THIS ANSWERS THAT NOTHING DID

    restore/lib/registry.py     the judgements no measurement can make: is this
                                component production, is this implementation ours,
                                may this external tree be omitted.
    restore/lib/measure.py      the readings. Nothing here guesses; a measurement
                                that cannot be taken returns a string saying so.
    restore/manifests/*.tsv     twelve generated tables, the join of the two.
    restore/symoneural-restore  inventory / verify / dependencies / build / test /
                                install / restore-state / services / smoke / status.

  THE FINDING THAT SHAPED IT

  tools/sh/fork_engines.sh builds the three engines behind chat, image and ASR out of
  external/referencestochatgpt/ -- 149 GB the owner does not want to carry. That is a
  real, load-bearing dependency and claiming otherwise to make a gate go green would
  be a lie the next restore would discover.

  What makes it omittable is that every one of those trees is a clean clone of a
  public remote at a pinned revision, verified against the checkout while the
  checkout is still here to verify against. 149 GB of source custody collapses into
  five URLs and five forty-hex strings. THIRD-PARTY-REBUILD-MANIFEST.tsv carries the
  pins; tools/sh/restore-upstream.sh fetches them and refuses on a mismatch.

  kawpowminer is the exception that proves the rule: three uncommitted local edits,
  including a real #include <cstdint> fix for gcc 13+. A revision pin cannot restore
  work nobody committed, so the patch is preserved separately and the manifest says
  the pin alone is not sufficient for that one.

  WHAT IT REFUSES TO SAY

  No component is called first-party because it was renamed. symoneural-llm, -diffuse
  and -listen are MIT forks and are recorded as THIRD_PARTY_DERIVATIVE_PERMISSIVE.
  symoneural-miner and symoneural-ui are GPL-3.0 and are DISABLED rather than
  relabelled, which is what fork_engines.sh's licence stamping has always refused to
  do. symoneural-adaptive-fabric is README and LICENCE with no implementation and
  says DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, so the plan cannot appear to restore something that
  was never built.

  DEFECTS THIS FOUND IN ITS OWN FIRST DRAFT, ALL FIXED

    * systemctl is-enabled exits non-zero for a legitimately disabled unit, so three
      services read UNMEASURED when systemd had answered.
    * the unit comparison had to become section-aware: the 2026-09-03 fix MOVED
      StartLimit* from [Service] to [Unit] without changing a character, and a
      set comparison of directive text called that a match.
    * a recipe named backend/requirements.lock.txt, which has never existed. The
      serving path is the Debian system interpreter; restore/locks/ now carries a
      real pinned lock per environment, 594 pins across seven.
    * the state table named run/accounts.db and run/api.env. Neither exists.
    * the first-party source bundle for the API was 97% vendored Anthropic and
      OpenAI SDK -- 15,704 files, now 407.
    * symoneural-ui was recorded as having no rebuild path. tools/sh/fork_render_ui.sh
      builds it. Buildable and disabled are different facts; both are now recorded.

  A PRODUCTION FINDING, NOT FIXED HERE

  The installed symoneural-api and symoneural-gateway units are stale against their
  templates: StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst still sit in [Service] where
  systemd silently ignores them, so the crash-loop protection their own comments
  describe has never applied, and Before=symoneural-web.service is absent so the API
  has no boot ordering against the process that actually serves. Reinstalling a unit
  alters a production service and that authority was not granted, so it is recorded
  in SERVICES.tsv as DIVERGED and left for the owner.

  Verified: RESTORE_VERIFY=PASS over 77 rows; 26 new tests; all five upstream pins
  PIN_VERIFIED; generating twice is byte-identical.

  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

The manifests are stable; only RELEASE.json's created_at moves. Two consequences: the earlier failure was stale pre-commit manifests, and created_at makes every regeneration dirty the tree forever. Deriving it from the HEAD commit date makes it deterministic and more meaningful:

The manifests are stable; only RELEASE.json's created_at moves. Two consequences: the earlier failure was stale pre-commit manifests, and created_at makes every regeneration dirty the tree forever. Deriving it from the HEAD commit date makes it deterministic and more meaningful:

  Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  python3 - <<'PY'
  import pathlib

  # 1. RELEASE.json must be a function of the commit, not of the clock.
  p = pathlib.Path("restore/lib/generate.py"); t = p.read_text()
  old = '''    doc = {
          "schema_version": 1,
          "release_id": release_id,
          "created_at": extra.get("created_at") if extra else None,'''
  new = '''    # `created_at` is the COMMIT date of repository_head, not the wall clock. A clock
      # reading makes RELEASE.json differ on every regeneration, so `git status` is dirty
      # forever and a real change is invisible in the noise -- and it dates the act of
      # running a generator rather than the release it describes.
      committed = M.run(["git", "show", "-s", "--format=%cI", "HEAD"])
      doc = {
          "schema_version": 1,
          "release_id": release_id,
          "created_at": committed if committed not in ("UNMEASURED", "") else None,
          "generated_at_note": "created_at is the commit date of repository_head, so this "
                               "document is a function of the commit and not of when the "
                               "generator happened to run",'''
  assert old in t
  t = t.replace(old, new)
  # extra{} must not overwrite it
  t = t.replace('''    if extra:
          doc.update(extra)''',
  '''    if extra:
          # `created_at` is derived above and is deliberately not overridable: a caller
          # passing a clock reading would reintroduce exactly the non-determinism this
          # avoids.
          doc.update({k: v for k, v in extra.items() if k != "created_at"})''')
  p.write_text(t)
  print("generate.py: RELEASE.json created_at is now the HEAD commit date")

  # 2. An exclusion list is a protection rule, not a dependency -- the archive-guard case.
  p = pathlib.Path("backend/apps/test_no_external_source_dependency.py"); t = p.read_text()
  t = t.replace('''    "training/project-history/",             # the history CORPUS: recorded question and''',
  '''    "tools/build/build_recovery_root.py",          # its "external/" is an EXCLUSION list -- the
                                               # rule that keeps vendored trees OUT of a
                                               # first-party source bundle. Deleting it
                                               # because the detector fired would put
                                               # somebody else's SDK back in the bundle.
      "training/project-history/",             # the history CORPUS: recorded question and''')
  p.write_text(t)
  print("detector: exclusion list exempted as a protection rule")
  PY
  python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py >/dev/null
  echo
  echo "############ RELEASE.json now stable across two runs? ############"
  sha1=$(sha256sum restore/RELEASE.json | cut -c1-16)
  python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py >/dev/null
  sha2=$(sha256sum restore/RELEASE.json | cut -c1-16)
  printf '  run1=%s run2=%s  %s\n' "$sha1" "$sha2" "$([ "$sha1" = "$sha2" ] && echo IDENTICAL || echo DIFFERS)")

A genuine circularity, and I've hit this exact class before: a generated file cannot record the hash of the commit that contains it. Amending changed HEAD, so the committed manifests now name the pre-amend revision. My test conflated two different things — generator determinism, and manifests being current. Separating them:

● Bash(cd /home/google/Symoneural
  python3 - <<'PY'

  old = '''class Idempotent(unittest.TestCase):

      def test_generating_twice_changes_nothing(self):
          """Three generators in this repository have accumulated a copy per run."""
          before = {name: (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes() for name in REQUIRED}
          r = subprocess.run(
              [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "build_restore_manifests.py")],
              cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
          self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0,
                           f"the generator failed:\\n{r.stdout}\\n{r.stderr}")
          for name in REQUIRED:
              with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                  self.assertEqual(
                      before[name], (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes(),
                      f"{name} changed on a second generation with no source change. "
                      f"Either a measurement is non-deterministic or the generator is "
                      f"re-reading its own output.")'''

  new = '''class Idempotent(unittest.TestCase):
      """Generator determinism, kept separate from manifest freshness.

      These were one test and should not have been. A generated manifest records the
      revision it was generated FROM, and committing it produces a new revision -- so the
      committed copy can never name the commit that contains it. That is the same
      impossibility as a file containing its own checksum, which this project already hit
      once when BACKUP.json carried the hash of the ZIP it was inside.

      Conflating the two made a real property (the generator does not accumulate output)
      fail for an unrelated and unavoidable reason (HEAD moved). So determinism is tested by
      generating twice and comparing THOSE two runs, and freshness is tested separately with
      the revision columns excluded.
      """

      @staticmethod
      def _generate() -> dict[str, bytes]:
          r = subprocess.run(
              [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "build_restore_manifests.py")],
              cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
          if r.returncode != 0:
              raise AssertionError(f"the generator failed:\\n{r.stdout}\\n{r.stderr}")
          return {name: (MANIFESTS / name).read_bytes() for name in REQUIRED}

      def test_generating_twice_changes_nothing(self):
          """Three generators in this repository have accumulated a copy per run."""
          first = self._generate()
          second = self._generate()
          for name in REQUIRED:
              with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                  self.assertEqual(
                      first[name], second[name],
                      f"{name} differs between two consecutive generations. Either a "
                      f"measurement is non-deterministic or the generator is re-reading "
                      f"its own output.")

      def test_committed_manifests_match_the_working_tree_apart_from_the_revision(self):
          """Freshness. Revision columns are excluded for the reason in the class docstring."""
          committed = {}
          for name in REQUIRED:
              r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "show", f"HEAD:restore/manifests/{name}"],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True)
              if r.returncode == 0:
                  committed[name] = r.stdout
          self.assertTrue(committed, "no manifests are committed yet")

          self._generate()

          def strip_rev(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
              lines = text.splitlines()
              header = lines[0].split("\\t")
              drop = {i for i, h in enumerate(header)
                      if h in ("SOURCE_REVISION", "PIN_VERIFIED")}
              return [[c for i, c in enumerate(ln.split("\\t")) if i not in drop]
                      for ln in lines]

          for name, old_text in committed.items():
              with self.subTest(manifest=name):
                  self.assertEqual(
                      strip_rev(old_text),
                      strip_rev((MANIFESTS / name).read_text()),
                      f"{name} in HEAD differs from what the registry generates now "
                      f"(revision columns excluded). Regenerate and commit: "
                      f"python3 tools/build/build_restore_manifests.py")'''

  assert old in t, "Idempotent class not found"
  p.write_text(t.replace(old, new))
  print("test: determinism and freshness are now separate properties")

# Source 8: `symoneuraldefects.md`

> Original attached content preserved below so commands, measurements, corrections, and historical wording remain intact.

Six real defects in my own output — three of them the exact "reported a value that was never measured" class. Fixing rather than shipping them:

1. systemctl is-enabled returns non-zero for a legitimately-disabled unit, and my generic run() maps non-zero to UNMEASURED. So gateway/progress/caddy read UNMEASURED when the real answer exists.
2. caddy's "installed unit" is /etc/caddy/Caddyfile — a config file, not a unit. I was asking systemd about a unit named Caddyfile.
3. symoneural-ui reads buildable=YES although the registry itself records that no fork_ui() exists.

My measurement bug: the tracked units are templates containing @@ROOT@@, substituted at install time. A raw SHA comparison can only ever say DIVERGED. That's my error and I'll fix the comparison to substitute first.

A genuine production defect underneath it, which the corrected comparison must still catch: the installed symoneural-api.service (2026-09-01) predates the template fix (2026-09-03) and is missing two real changes —

Same on the gateway unit. I am not reinstalling these — that is altering a production service and the authority for it wasn't granted. Recording it as a blocker and making the restore plan install the corrected template.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""Join the judgement registry against measured disk state and emit the restore manifests.

Run it twice and diff. Every generator in this repository re-reads its own output, and one
that does not recognise something it emits accumulates a copy per run -- that bug has
happened three times here, which is why `ops/authority/PROJECT-AUTHORITY.md` makes "run
both twice and diff" part of the completion sequence rather than advice.

## The anti-vacuity rule

A generator that finds nothing passes forever for the wrong reason. Two guards:

* `discover_components()` walks the disk for things that look like a runtime and raises if
  one has no row in the registry. A new engine folder cannot be quietly left out of the
  restore plan; it fails the build instead.
* Every table asserts a minimum row count before it is written. An empty
  `SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv` would satisfy "no component fails closure" and mean nothing.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import sys

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent))

from lib import measure as M          # noqa: E402
from lib import registry as R         # noqa: E402

ROOT = M.ROOT
MANIFESTS = ROOT / "restore" / "manifests"

# `-` is the empty cell. A truly empty cell in a TSV is ambiguous with a parse error, and a
# column that is sometimes absent breaks `cut -f`.
NUL = "-"


def _cell(v) -> str:
    """One TSV cell: never contains a tab or a newline, never empty."""
    s = "" if v is None else str(v)
    s = s.replace("\t", " ").replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ")
    s = " ".join(s.split())
    return s or NUL


def write_tsv(name: str, header: list[str], rows: list[list], minimum: int) -> int:
    if len(rows) < minimum:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"restore/generate: {name} would have {len(rows)} rows, minimum {minimum}. "
            f"A manifest that is empty passes every 'no failures' check for the wrong "
            f"reason; refusing to write it.")
    for r in rows:
        if len(r) != len(header):
            raise SystemExit(
                f"restore/generate: {name} row has {len(r)} cells, header has "
                f"{len(header)}: {r[:3]}")
    out = MANIFESTS / name
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    body = "\t".join(header) + "\n"
    body += "".join("\t".join(_cell(c) for c in r) + "\n" for r in rows)
    out.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
    return len(rows)


# =========================================================================================
# Discovery -- the anti-vacuity guard
# =========================================================================================

def discover_components() -> list[str]:
    """Everything on disk that looks like a first-party runtime.

    Deliberately over-inclusive: it is better to force a registry row for something that
    turns out to be uninteresting than to miss a runtime. The rule the owner set is that
    every runtime gets its own top-level folder, so a top-level `symoneural-*` directory is
    the signal.
    """
    found = []
    for p in sorted(ROOT.iterdir()):
        if p.is_dir() and p.name.startswith("symoneural-"):
            found.append(p.name)
    return found


def check_registry_covers_disk() -> list[str]:
    known = R.component_ids()
    missing = [n for n in discover_components() if n not in known]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(
            "restore/generate: these runtimes exist on disk and have no row in "
            "restore/lib/registry.py:\n    " + "\n    ".join(missing) +
            "\n\nAdd them. A runtime absent from the registry is absent from the restore "
            "plan, and that is how a restore silently loses a component.")
    return discover_components()


# =========================================================================================
# Tables
# =========================================================================================

def gen_components() -> int:
    header = ["COMPONENT_ID", "CANONICAL_NAME", "CLASS", "SOURCE_ROOT", "LANGUAGE",
              "BUILD_SYSTEM", "BUILD_AUTHORITY", "PRODUCTION_STATUS", "PARENT_COMPONENT",
              "PRIMARY_ARTIFACT", "SERVICE", "RESTORE_REQUIRED", "FIRST_PARTY_STATUS",
              "SOURCE_ROOT_PRESENT", "BLOCKER"]
    rows = [[c.component_id, c.canonical_name, c.cls, c.source_root, c.language,
             c.build_system, c.build_authority, c.production_status, c.parent_component,
             c.primary_artifact, c.service, c.restore_required, c.first_party_status,
             M.exists(c.source_root), c.blocker]
            for c in R.COMPONENTS]
    return write_tsv("COMPONENTS.tsv", header, rows, minimum=15)


def gen_applications() -> int:
    header = ["APPLICATION_ID", "DISPLAY_NAME", "PARENT_APPLICATION_ID", "UI_SOURCE",
              "UI_SOURCE_PRESENT", "ROUTE", "API_ROUTES", "PRIMARY_RUNTIME_COMPONENT",
              "SECONDARY_COMPONENTS", "ENGINE_DEPENDENCIES", "PERSISTENT_STATE_IDS",
              "AUTH_REQUIREMENT", "PRODUCTION_STATUS", "RESTORE_SMOKE_ID"]
    rows = [[a.application_id, a.display_name, a.parent_application_id, a.ui_source,
             M.exists(a.ui_source), a.route, a.api_routes, a.primary_runtime_component,
             a.secondary_components, a.engine_dependencies, a.persistent_state_ids,
             a.auth_requirement, a.production_status, a.restore_smoke_id]
            for a in R.APPLICATIONS]
    return write_tsv("APPLICATIONS.tsv", header, rows, minimum=12)


def gen_source_closure() -> int:
    header = ["COMPONENT_ID", "SOURCE_ROOT", "SOURCE_REVISION", "TRACKED_FILE_COUNT",
              "UNTRACKED_SOURCE_COUNT", "GENERATED_SOURCE_COUNT", "CANONICAL_SOURCE",
              "BUILDABLE_FROM_TRACKED_SOURCE", "INSTALLED_ONLY_FILES",
              "EXTERNAL_SOURCE_DEPENDENCY", "EXTERNAL_SOURCE_REACQUIRABLE",
              "SOURCE_BUNDLE", "SOURCE_BUNDLE_SHA256", "STATUS"]
    rev = M.head()
    rows = []
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        derived = c.tracked_in_git == "NO"

        # For a derived tree, "untracked files" is thousands and means nothing: the tree is
        # ignored by design. Its canonical source is the upstream pin plus the fork script,
        # both of which ARE tracked, so the closure question is whether the pin is real.
        if derived:
            tracked = M.tracked_count(c.build_authority.split()[0]) \
                if c.build_authority != NUL else 0
            untracked = "n/a (derived tree, ignored by design)"
            canonical = "UPSTREAM_PIN + tracked fork script"
            buildable = "YES" if c.upstream_rev != NUL else "NO"
            ext = "YES"
            reacq = "YES" if c.upstream != NUL else "NO"
        else:
            tracked = M.tracked_count(c.source_root)
            untracked = M.untracked_count(c.source_root)
            canonical = "YES"
            buildable = "YES"
            ext = "NO"
            reacq = "n/a"

        installed_only = "0"
        status = "PASS"
        if c.production_status == R.PRODUCTION:
            if buildable != "YES":
                status = "FAIL (no rebuild path)"
            elif isinstance(untracked, int) and untracked > 0:
                status = f"FAIL ({untracked} untracked source files)"
        elif c.production_status == R.DECLARED:
            status = "N/A (declared, not implemented)"
        else:
            status = f"N/A ({c.production_status})"

        rows.append([c.component_id, c.source_root, rev, tracked, untracked, "0",
                     canonical, buildable, installed_only, ext, reacq,
                     NUL, NUL, status])
    return write_tsv("SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv", header, rows, minimum=15)


def gen_build_recipes() -> int:
    header = ["COMPONENT_ID", "SOURCE_ROOT", "SOURCE_REVISION", "BUILD_SYSTEM",
              "BUILD_AUTHORITY", "TOOLCHAIN", "TOOLCHAIN_VERSION", "TARGET_PLATFORM",
              "TARGET_ARCH", "BUILD_PROFILE", "DEPENDENCY_LOCK", "PREP_COMMAND",
              "BUILD_COMMAND", "TEST_COMMAND", "OUTPUT_ARTIFACT", "INSTALL_COMMAND",
              "INSTALL_PATH", "CLEAN_BUILD_SUPPORTED", "NETWORK_REQUIRED", "NOTES"]
    rev = M.head()
    # Measured once, reused: these are host facts, not per-component facts.
    versions = {n: M.tool_version(n) for n in
                ("gcc", "g++", "cmake", "nvcc", "python3", "node", "npm", "git")}
    rows = []
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        tv = "; ".join(f"{t}={versions.get(t.strip(), 'UNKNOWN')}"
                       for t in c.toolchain.replace("/", ", ").split(",")
                       if t.strip() and t.strip() != NUL) or NUL
        rows.append([c.component_id, c.source_root, rev, c.build_system, c.build_authority,
                     c.toolchain, tv, "linux-x86_64", c.target_arch, c.build_profile,
                     c.dependency_lock, c.prep_command, c.build_command, c.test_command,
                     c.output_artifact, c.install_command, c.install_path,
                     c.clean_build_supported, c.network_required, c.notes])
    return write_tsv("BUILD-RECIPES.tsv", header, rows, minimum=15)


def gen_artifacts() -> int:
    header = ["ARTIFACT_ID", "COMPONENT_ID", "ARTIFACT_TYPE", "SOURCE_ROOT",
              "SOURCE_REVISION", "BUILD_RECIPE_ID", "BUILD_OUTPUT", "BUILD_SHA256",
              "FILE_TYPE", "ABI_OR_ARCH", "DYNAMIC_DEPENDENCIES", "INSTALLED_PATH",
              "INSTALLED_SHA256", "TEST_STATUS", "SMOKE_STATUS", "FALLBACK_COPY"]
    rev = M.head()
    rows = []
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        if c.primary_artifact in (NUL, ""):
            continue
        p = ROOT / c.primary_artifact
        kind = "directory" if p.is_dir() else (
            "executable" if p.is_file() and p.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else "file")
        rows.append([
            f"art-{c.component_id}", c.component_id, kind, c.source_root, rev,
            f"recipe-{c.component_id}", c.primary_artifact,
            M.sha256(p) if p.is_file() else ("DIRECTORY" if p.is_dir() else "NOT_PRESENT"),
            M.file_type(p), M.elf_arch(p), M.dynamic_deps(p),
            c.install_path,
            M.sha256(pathlib.Path(c.install_path).expanduser())
            if c.install_path not in (NUL, "") and not c.install_path.startswith("(")
            else NUL,
            "SEE BUILD-RECIPES.TEST_COMMAND", "SEE SMOKES.tsv",
            "PENDING (.private/runtime-artifacts/<release-id>/)",
        ])
    return write_tsv("ARTIFACTS.tsv", header, rows, minimum=10)


def gen_services() -> int:
    header = ["SERVICE_ID", "COMPONENT_ID", "SOURCE_UNIT", "INSTALLED_UNIT", "USER",
              "GROUP", "WORKING_DIRECTORY", "EXEC_START", "ENV_FILES", "PORTS",
              "DEPENDENCIES", "ENABLEMENT_DESIGNED", "ENABLEMENT_MEASURED",
              "ACTIVE_MEASURED", "INSTALLED_MATCHES_SOURCE", "INSTALL_COMMAND",
              "START_COMMAND", "HEALTHCHECK"]
    rows = []
    for s in R.SERVICES:
        user_scope = s.installed_unit.startswith("~")
        unit_name = pathlib.Path(s.installed_unit).name
        en, ac = M.unit_state(unit_name, user=user_scope)
        # ExecStart read from the SOURCE template, which is the thing a restore installs.
        src = ROOT / s.source_unit
        execstart = NUL
        if src.is_file():
            for ln in src.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
                if ln.strip().startswith("ExecStart"):
                    execstart = ln.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
                    break
        rows.append([s.service_id, s.component_id, s.source_unit, s.installed_unit,
                     s.user, s.group, s.working_directory, execstart, s.env_files,
                     s.ports, s.dependencies, s.enablement, en, ac,
                     M.installed_unit_matches(s.source_unit, s.installed_unit),
                     s.install_command, s.start_command, s.healthcheck])
    return write_tsv("SERVICES.tsv", header, rows, minimum=4)


def gen_persistent_state() -> int:
    header = ["STATE_ID", "APPLICATION", "COMPONENT", "LIVE_PATH", "LIVE_PRESENT", "TYPE",
              "CONTAINS_SECRETS", "CONSISTENCY_METHOD", "BACKUP_PATH", "BACKUP_SHA256",
              "OWNER", "MODE", "RESTORE_DESTINATION", "RESTORE_COMMAND",
              "VALIDATION_COMMAND", "REQUIRED_FOR_RESTORE"]
    rows = []
    for s in R.STATE_STORES:
        p = ROOT / s.live_path.split(",")[0].strip()
        try:
            owner = p.owner() if p.exists() else "NOT_PRESENT"
        except (KeyError, OSError):
            owner = "UNRESOLVED_UID"
        rows.append([s.state_id, s.application, s.component, s.live_path,
                     M.exists(s.live_path.split(",")[0].strip()), s.type_,
                     s.contains_secrets, s.consistency_method,
                     "PENDING (.private/application-state/<release-id>/)", "PENDING",
                     owner, M.mode_of(p), s.restore_destination, s.restore_command,
                     s.validation_command, s.required_for_restore])
    return write_tsv("PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv", header, rows, minimum=6)


def gen_restore_order() -> int:
    header = ["ORDER", "STEP_ID", "ACTION", "REQUIRES", "COMMAND", "VERIFY_COMMAND",
              "MUTATES_SYSTEM", "REQUIRES_ROOT", "FAILURE_POLICY"]
    rows = [[s.order, s.step_id, s.action, s.requires, s.command, s.verify_command,
             s.mutates_system, s.requires_root, s.failure_policy]
            for s in R.RESTORE_ORDER]
    return write_tsv("RESTORE-ORDER.tsv", header, rows, minimum=10)


def gen_smokes() -> int:
    header = ["SMOKE_ID", "APPLICATION_ID", "PREREQUISITES", "COMMAND", "EXPECTED_RESULT",
              "NETWORK_SCOPE", "MUTATING", "SAFE_AFTER_FRESH_RESTORE"]
    rows = [[s.smoke_id, s.application_id, s.prerequisites, s.command, s.expected_result,
             s.network_scope, s.mutating, s.safe_after_fresh_restore]
            for s in R.SMOKES]
    return write_tsv("SMOKES.tsv", header, rows, minimum=12)


def gen_first_party_closure() -> int:
    """FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv -- written to the REPOSITORY ROOT, where the spec asks for it."""
    header = ["COMPONENT_ID", "APPLICATION", "CURRENT_RUNTIME", "CURRENT_SOURCE",
              "IMPLEMENTATION_CLASS", "THIRD_PARTY_SOURCE_REQUIRED_AT_RUNTIME",
              "THIRD_PARTY_SOURCE_REQUIRED_AT_BUILD", "FIRST_PARTY_REPLACEMENT",
              "TEST_STATUS", "PRODUCTION_STATUS", "EXTERNAL_SOURCE_CAN_BE_OMITTED",
              "BLOCKER"]
    app_of = {}
    for a in R.APPLICATIONS:
        for cid in [a.primary_runtime_component] + a.engine_dependencies.split(","):
            cid = cid.strip().split(" ")[0]
            if cid and cid != NUL:
                app_of.setdefault(cid, []).append(a.application_id)

    rows = []
    for c in R.COMPONENTS:
        derived = c.first_party_status in (R.DERIV_PERMISSIVE, R.DERIV_COPYLEFT)
        # Runtime: does the SHIPPED thing need third-party source present to run? No -- the
        # engines are compiled; once built, the source tree is not read at runtime.
        rt = "NO"
        # Build: yes for a fork, and that is the honest answer.
        bt = "YES (pinned upstream, reacquired)" if derived else "NO"
        # Omittable when the upstream can be fetched again at an exact revision. The
        # kawpowminer tree cannot be fully reconstructed from a pin alone -- it carries
        # uncommitted local edits -- so its patch is preserved and that is said here.
        if not derived:
            omit = "YES (no external source involved)"
        elif c.upstream_rev != NUL and c.local_patch == NUL:
            omit = "YES (clean clone at a pinned revision, reacquirable)"
        elif c.upstream_rev != NUL:
            omit = "YES (pin + preserved local patch)"
        else:
            omit = "NO"

        replacement = NUL
        if c.component_id == "symoneural-miner":
            replacement = "symoneural-miner-core (INCOMPLETE -- see docs/ALGORITHM-GAP.md)"

        rows.append([c.component_id, ",".join(app_of.get(c.component_id, [])) or NUL,
                     c.primary_artifact, c.source_root, c.first_party_status, rt, bt,
                     replacement, "SEE BUILD-RECIPES.TEST_COMMAND", c.production_status,
                     omit, c.blocker])

    out = ROOT / "FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv"
    out.write_text("\t".join(header) + "\n" +
                   "".join("\t".join(_cell(x) for x in r) + "\n" for r in rows),
                   encoding="utf-8")
    return len(rows)


def gen_release(release_id: str, extra: dict | None = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    prod = [c for c in R.COMPONENTS if c.production_status == R.PRODUCTION]
    doc = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "release_id": release_id,
        "created_at": extra.get("created_at") if extra else None,
        "repository_head": M.head(),
        "branch": M.branch(),
        "repository_clean": M.is_clean(),
        "component_count": len(R.COMPONENTS),
        "production_component_count": len(prod),
        "application_count": len(R.APPLICATIONS),
        "production_application_count":
            sum(1 for a in R.APPLICATIONS if a.production_status == R.PRODUCTION),
        "service_count": len(R.SERVICES),
        "persistent_state_count": len(R.STATE_STORES),
        "smoke_count": len(R.SMOKES),
        "restore_entrypoint": "restore/symoneural-restore",
        "manifest_root": "restore/manifests",
        "git_bundle_path": ".private/git-backup/Symoneural-all.bundle",
        "runtime_artifact_root": f".private/runtime-artifacts/{release_id}",
        "source_bundle_root": f".private/source-bundles/{release_id}",
        "persistent_state_root": f".private/application-state/{release_id}",
        "host_snapshot_root": ".private/host-snapshot",
        "claude_backup_root": ".private/claude-backups",
        "host": {
            "gcc": M.tool_version("gcc"),
            "cmake": M.tool_version("cmake"),
            "nvcc": M.tool_version("nvcc"),
            "python3": M.tool_version("python3"),
            "node": M.tool_version("node"),
            "npm": M.tool_version("npm"),
            "gpu": M.gpu(),
        },
    }
    if extra:
        doc.update(extra)
    out = ROOT / "restore" / "RELEASE.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return out


def generate_all(release_id: str, extra: dict | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
    check_registry_covers_disk()
    counts = {
        "COMPONENTS.tsv": gen_components(),
        "APPLICATIONS.tsv": gen_applications(),
        "SOURCE-CLOSURE.tsv": gen_source_closure(),
        "BUILD-RECIPES.tsv": gen_build_recipes(),
        "ARTIFACTS.tsv": gen_artifacts(),
        "SERVICES.tsv": gen_services(),
        "PERSISTENT-STATE.tsv": gen_persistent_state(),
        "RESTORE-ORDER.tsv": gen_restore_order(),
        "SMOKES.tsv": gen_smokes(),
        "FIRST-PARTY-CLOSURE.tsv": gen_first_party_closure(),
    }
    gen_release(release_id, extra)
    return counts

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-SyMoNeuRaL-Proprietary
# Copyright (c) 2026 SymonSays LLC. All rights reserved.
# SyMoNeuRaL is a subdivision of SymonSays LLC. Licence: /LICENSE at the repository root.
"""The measured half of the restore control plane.

Nothing in this module makes a judgement. It reads the disk and reports what is there:
revisions, file counts, checksums, ELF architectures, whether a binary a recipe promises is
actually where the recipe says. Every value it returns is a reading taken now.

That separation is the whole point. This repository has published a test count that was
never true of the commit it sat beside, reported a service as disabled off a table row while
the unit file said enabled, and recorded an engine as unbuilt because a probe looked in the
wrong directory. Each was the same failure -- acting on a row rather than on the thing. So
the judgements live in `registry.py` where a human can argue with them, and everything that
can be measured is measured here, at generation time, every time.

Two conventions that matter:

* A measurement that cannot be taken returns a string saying so. It never returns a
  plausible default. `"NOT_PRESENT"` and `"UNMEASURED"` are values; `0` and `""` are not,
  because a zero that means "absent" is indistinguishable from a zero that means zero.

* Nothing here shells out to anything that could mutate state. It is all reads, so
  `symoneural-restore verify` is safe to run on a live box.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess


def find_root(start: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Walk up for a marker; never count parents.

    `ROOT = HERE.parent.parent` encodes the file's depth in the tree and breaks silently the
    day the file moves. `symoneural-audit` ratchets a count of that pattern and has twice
    caught new files written by the same author who added the check.
    """
    for cand in (start, *start.parents):
        if (cand / "backend" / "api.py").is_file():
            return cand
    raise SystemExit(f"symoneural-restore: no repository root above {start}")


ROOT = find_root(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- process
def run(args: list[str], cwd: pathlib.Path | None = None, timeout: int = 60) -> str:
    """Run a read-only command and return stripped stdout, or a marker string."""
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd or ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                           timeout=timeout)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED"
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return "TIMEOUT"
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return "UNMEASURED"
    return p.stdout.strip()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- git
def head() -> str:
    return run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"])


def branch() -> str:
    return run(["git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"])


def is_clean() -> bool:
    return run(["git", "status", "--porcelain"]) == ""


def tracked_count(rel: str) -> int | str:
    out = run(["git", "ls-files", "--", rel])
    if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED"):
        return out
    return len([ln for ln in out.splitlines() if ln])


def untracked_count(rel: str) -> int | str:
    """Untracked-and-not-ignored files under `rel`.

    Ignored files are excluded deliberately: for the five derived engine trees EVERY file is
    ignored, and counting them as untracked source would report thousands of defects for a
    tree whose canonical source is an upstream pin. `--exclude-standard` is what makes the
    number mean "source we forgot to track" rather than "files on disk".
    """
    out = run(["git", "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", rel])
    if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED"):
        return out
    return len([ln for ln in out.splitlines() if ln])


def repo_rev_of(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    if not (path / ".git").exists():
        return "NOT_A_GIT_REPO"
    return run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=path)


def repo_dirty_count(path: pathlib.Path) -> int | str:
    if not (path / ".git").exists():
        return "NOT_A_GIT_REPO"
    out = run(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=path)
    if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT"):
        return out
    return len([ln for ln in out.splitlines() if ln])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- files
def sha256(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    """Hash a file by reading it. No `-L`: `sha256sum` has no dereference flag, and a
    session was spent chasing a source/launcher 'mismatch' that was `sha256sum -bL`
    silently doing something other than what was intended."""
    if not path.is_file():
        return "NOT_PRESENT"
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    try:
        with path.open("rb") as fh:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
                h.update(chunk)
    except OSError as e:
        return f"UNREADABLE({e.errno})"
    return h.hexdigest()


def exists(rel: str) -> str:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if p.is_file():
        return "FILE"
    if p.is_dir():
        return "DIR"
    return "ABSENT"


def mode_of(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    if not path.exists():
        return "NOT_PRESENT"
    return oct(path.stat().st_mode & 0o7777)[2:].rjust(3, "0")


def file_type(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    if not path.is_file():
        return "NOT_PRESENT"
    out = run(["file", "-b", str(path)])
    return out.split(",")[0].strip() if out not in ("UNMEASURED", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED") \
        else out


def elf_arch(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    if not path.is_file():
        return "NOT_PRESENT"
    out = run(["readelf", "-h", str(path)])
    if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED", "TIMEOUT"):
        return out
    for ln in out.splitlines():
        if ln.strip().startswith("Machine:"):
            return ln.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    return "NOT_AN_ELF"


def dynamic_deps(path: pathlib.Path, limit: int = 6) -> str:
    """Direct NEEDED entries, not the full transitive `ldd` closure.

    `ldd` runs the loader and is not something to point at an untrusted binary; `readelf -d`
    reads the table. The count is what a restore actually needs to know -- which shared
    objects must exist -- and the first few names identify the dependency family.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        return "NOT_PRESENT"
    out = run(["readelf", "-d", str(path)])
    if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED", "TIMEOUT", "NOT_AN_ELF"):
        return out
    needed = [ln.split("[", 1)[1].rstrip("]").strip()
              for ln in out.splitlines() if "(NEEDED)" in ln and "[" in ln]
    if not needed:
        return "none"
    shown = ";".join(needed[:limit])
    return f"{len(needed)} NEEDED: {shown}" + ("…" if len(needed) > limit else "")


def du_bytes(path: pathlib.Path) -> int | str:
    if not path.exists():
        return "NOT_PRESENT"
    out = run(["du", "-sb", str(path)], timeout=300)
    if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED"):
        return out
    return int(out.split()[0])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- toolchain
def tool_version(name: str) -> str:
    """Version of a host tool, or an explicit ABSENT.

    A restore recipe that names a toolchain has to be checkable, and the check has to be
    able to say "this machine does not have it" rather than guessing.
    """
    if shutil.which(name) is None:
        return "ABSENT"
    probes = {
        "gcc": ["gcc", "-dumpfullversion"],
        "g++": ["g++", "-dumpfullversion"],
        "cmake": ["cmake", "--version"],
        "nvcc": ["nvcc", "--version"],
        "python3": ["python3", "--version"],
        "node": ["node", "--version"],
        "npm": ["npm", "--version"],
        "git": ["git", "--version"],
        "rsync": ["rsync", "--version"],
        "sqlite3": ["sqlite3", "--version"],
        "caddy": ["caddy", "version"],
        "ninja": ["ninja", "--version"],
        "ccache": ["ccache", "--version"],
    }
    out = run(probes.get(name, [name, "--version"]), timeout=30)
    if out in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT", "TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED"):
        return out
    first = out.splitlines()[0] if out else ""
    if name == "nvcc":
        for ln in out.splitlines():
            if "release" in ln:
                return ln.strip()
    return first.strip()


def gpu() -> str:
    if shutil.which("nvidia-smi") is None:
        return "ABSENT"
    return run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total",
                "--format=csv,noheader"], timeout=30).splitlines()[0] \
        if run(["nvidia-smi", "-L"], timeout=30) not in ("UNMEASURED", "TIMEOUT") \
        else "UNMEASURED"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- services
def unit_state(unit: str, user: bool = False) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(enabled-state, active-state) as systemd reports them right now.

    Read from systemd, never from a table. A service-map row reading 'defined but disabled'
    was reported as an anomaly three times about a unit that was enabled and active and is
    the public web server -- the row was wrong and nobody had opened the unit.
    """
    base = ["systemctl", "--user"] if user else ["systemctl"]
    en = run(base + ["is-enabled", unit], timeout=30)
    ac = run(base + ["is-active", unit], timeout=30)
    return (en or "UNMEASURED", ac or "UNMEASURED")


def installed_unit_matches(source_rel: str, installed: str) -> str:
    """Does the installed unit still match the tracked template it came from?"""
    src = ROOT / source_rel
    dst = pathlib.Path(os.path.expanduser(installed))
    if not src.is_file():
        return "SOURCE_ABSENT"
    if not dst.exists():
        return "NOT_INSTALLED"
    a, b = sha256(src), sha256(dst)
    if b.startswith("UNREADABLE"):
        return "UNREADABLE(root-owned)"
    return "MATCH" if a == b else "DIVERGED"


Now the generator that joins judgement against measurement and emits all twelve tables.
